We also discuss consequences for 4d gauge theories, including the presence of a BFKL contrail produced by an outgoing wave of hadron number density.

papers.title_en: Mercury (Hg): a relativistic $N$-body simulation for Horndeski gravity
papers.abstract_en: We present Mercury, a relativistic $N$-body code for cosmological simulations in the $α$-basis formulation of Horndeski gravity. Mercury extends a particle-mesh scheme by incorporating the dynamics of the additional scalar degree of freedom and the corresponding modified Einstein equations, expressed in terms of the time-dependent functions $α_{\rm K}, α_{\rm B}, α_{\rm M}, α_{\rm T}$ and the effective Planck mass $M_*^2$. This generalises our previous implementation of Horndeski subclass models, namely $k$-essence and kinetic gravity braiding (KGB), to the general linear Horndeski $α$-basis. The code evolves the additional scalar degree of freedom and its effective stress--energy tensor alongside the nonlinear matter and metric fields, so that nonlinear structure formation sources the scalar-field evolution and feeds back on the gravitational potentials. Through its interface with hi_class, Mercury supports both phenomenological $α$-function parametrisations and covariant Horndeski theories; we demonstrate the latter using nKGB, the Cubic Galileon, and Brans--Dicke models. We validate the implementation against hi_class in the linear regime and recover the expected nonlinear $k$-essence and KGB limits. For the luminal Horndeski models considered here, we show how a running effective Planck mass generates gravitational slip through the scalar anisotropic stress and modifies the friction terms governing the vector and tensor metric perturbations. The evolution of $M_*^2$ also modifies the normalisation and scale dependence of the effective dark-energy density contrast, leaving a corresponding imprint on its power spectrum. The present framework provides an intermediate step towards nonlinear Horndeski simulations, in which nonlinear scalar self-interactions and screening effects can be incorporated consistently within the same relativistic framework.

papers.title_en: Ultrafast X-ray-induced dephasing of valence electrons
papers.abstract_en: Diffract-before-destroy schemes for atomic-scale electron mapping assume that ultrashort X-ray pulses outrun radiation damage. Although atomic cores move over tens of femtoseconds, outer electrons respond much faster, compromising their locations. We test this limit in elemental silicon using broadband, energy-chirped X-ray pulses to encode time with few-femtosecond resolution. Comparing valence-sensitive structurally forbidden reflections with simultaneously measured core-dominated Bragg peaks reveals valence-bond dephasing on sub-20-fs timescales even at pulse energies where direct ionization effects are negligible. Our findings demonstrate that crystallography where outer electrons contribute substantially to Bragg peaks requires pulses shorter than today's standard $\sim50\,fs$ standard. They also establish a path to disentangle valence electron and lattice contributions to order and dynamics with hard X-rays, enabling studies across molecular biology, quantum matter and devices.

papers.title_en: Tracing source imprints on the gravitational direct wave
papers.abstract_en: The direct wave component of black hole (BH) ringdown, revealed through quasinormal-mode filters, carries a non-quasinormal-mode imprint of the plunging perturber's dynamics. However, the connection between the source trajectory and the observed direct wave remains incompletely understood. We first show that the full waveform filtered by the frequency-dependent black hole response gives a substantially more localized kernel than the standard rational filter approach. We then show that analytically continuing the Teukolsky source variables to complex coordinates allows for a semianalytic direct wave which closely reproduces numerical integration throughout the entire plunge. Our generalized steepest-descent method clarifies how coherent emission shapes the imprint of source dynamics on the observed direct wave beyond the light-cone picture.

papers.title_en: Spinless Charged Excitation at the Interface between a Conventional Topological Insulator and a Topological Mott Insulator
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the interface separating two topologically distinct insulating phases of matter using extensive density-matrix renormalization group calculations to study the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model with a spatially varying interaction strength, chosen to realize both integer quantum Hall and chiral spin liquid states in different spatial regions. We find that the integer quantum Hall-chiral spin liquid interface hosts a spinless charged excitation that is bound to the interface. This mode at the interface is identified through charge and spin pumping, and by direct calculations of low-lying excited states. We also characterize bulk excitations in both phases, finding evidence for fractionalization in the chiral spin liquid and for spin-triplet exciton formation in the integer quantum Hall phase.

papers.title_en: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a replica-free approach
papers.abstract_en: We derive an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic $d$-dimensional CFTs. The derivation uses a novel radial sewing expansion of the joint vacuum density matrix, together with a modular response formula for relative entropy and the geometric modular flow of a single ball, without analytic continuation in replica number. The expansion coefficients are modular integrals of modular-flowed vacuum correlators. Our formula provides a systematic treatment of arbitrary multi-point sectors, and recovers known results on two-point sector derived from replica methods. The full two-point sector resums into a modular integral of the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, with an effective temperature depending on ball configuration and modular time. We compute the expansion explicitly in CFTs. In two-dimensional Ising CFT, using analytic reductions and multidimensional numerical integration, we obtain the first ten radial orders in the long-distance expansion, which involve sphere correlators with up to twenty spin insertions. The truncated expansion agrees well with lattice data at finite separation, and approximately satisfies crossing symmetry. Analytic calculations also reproduce known expansion coefficients for 2d free compact boson at self-dual radius and its current sector, as well as for free scalars in higher dimensions.

papers.title_en: Inhomogeneous Synthetic Fluxes in Optical Lattices
papers.abstract_en: Synthetic gauge fields in optical lattices are usually engineered to realize a uniform magnetic flux. Here, we propose a scheme to generate spatially inhomogeneous fluxes and demonstrate how such fluxes reshape the single-particle spectrum. Within Wannier--Stark-assisted tunneling, onsite modulation produces a plaquette flux that depends on the orientation of the static tilt, whereas laser-assisted tunneling (LAT) does not. Using LAT, two coherent Raman processes with different momentum transfers imprint a dimerized Peierls phase that alternates the flux between neighboring plaquettes of a square lattice while keeping the mean flux fixed. A bond-selective Raman phase extends the scheme to the kagome lattice, where a parameter $ξ$ redistributes the flux between triangles and hexagons at fixed flux per unit cell. The Hofstadter--Rammal spectrum of the bipartite square lattice retains chiral symmetry for all $ξ$, whereas the kagome lattice lacks this symmetry, and its flux periodicity and reflection symmetries survive only at special values of $ξ$. As $ξ$ is reduced, the anomalous Landau levels of the kagome singular flat band are compressed toward the flat-band energy and evolve into a degenerate zero-energy manifold at $ξ=0$ with compactly localized states. The dynamical structure factor, accessible through Bragg scattering, resolves this evolution as a Rydberg-like series of peaks whose spectral span tracks the width of the anomalous-level tower and vanishes as $ξ\to0$. We discuss the frequency resolution and temperature required for its observation.

papers.title_en: Spacetime Emergence in the Memory of a Learning Agent
papers.abstract_en: We show that the causal structure of spacetime can emerge within the memory of a learning agent performing a quantum information task. We train a model-based reinforcement-learning agent to maximize the quantum mutual information between localized quantum probes interacting with a quantum field in Minkowski spacetime, without directly providing it with information regarding the spacetime metric or causal structure. In learning to accomplish this task, the reinforcement-learning agent constructs an internal predictive model whose planner develops the characteristic null structure of spacetime, allowing us to reconstruct the causal structure of the Minkowski metric with high accuracy. Within this task, spacetime geometry is obtained from an agent's successful predictions and actions, providing a first step toward showing that spacetime concepts emerge from operational quantum experience.

papers.title_en: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
papers.abstract_en: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.

papers.title_en: Detection of the Galaxy--Galaxy--Temperature Skewed Bispectrum
papers.abstract_en: We present the first measurement of the galaxy--galaxy--temperature skewed bispectrum, obtained by cross-correlating the squared, filtered unWISE galaxy overdensity with \textit{Planck} maps at 100, 143, 217, and 353~GHz. The signal is detected with high significance in all four channels. Its frequency dependence reveals contributions from hot gas through the thermal Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect and from dust through the cosmic infrared background (CIB). With the galaxy occupation fixed, our halo-model fits favor higher integrated pressure and peak star-formation efficiency for the galaxy--temperature cross-spectra than for the skewed bispectrum. Comparisons with component-separated tSZ and CIB maps from the same \textit{Planck} observations indicate that this mismatch is not confined to the frequency-map fits. This difference motivates testing more flexible descriptions of gas pressure, CIB emission, and galaxy occupation. In particular, it could point to a mass dependence of the gas-pressure profile that our model does not fully capture. By giving greater weight to massive halos that host many galaxy pairs, the skewed bispectrum provides a complementary test of these descriptions, using information beyond two-point statistics at a comparable computational cost.

papers.title_en: Modular Krylov Complexity as a Boundary Probe of Area Operators and Entanglement Islands
papers.abstract_en: We show that the area operator of a quantum extremal surface can be reconstructed directly from boundary dynamics without reference to bulk geometry. Our approach combines the operator-algebra quantum error-correction (OAQEC) structure of AdS/CFT with modular Krylov complexity. Using Lanczos coefficients of boundary modular dynamics, we extract the spectrum of the modular Hamiltonian restricted to the algebra of the entanglement wedge and isolate its central contribution, which is identified with the area operator. The construction is purely boundary-based and applies to superpositions of semiclassical geometries as well. As a prospective application, we discuss island formation and the Page transition in evaporating black holes using boundary modular evolution, bypassing any bulk extremization. More broadly, our results establish modular Krylov complexity as a probe of emergent spacetime geometry, providing a new route to accessing black hole interiors from boundary quantum dynamics.

papers.title_en: Nonlinear gauge maps and the structure of Goldstone loops in canonical inflation
papers.abstract_en: We clarify the nonlinear relation between the spatially flat scalar and Goldstone descriptions of canonical single-field inflation. An exact clock map shows how potential interactions are reorganized into derivative Goldstone interactions. A change of slicing further connects their dilation symmetry to its comoving realization. We then study the Goldstone two-point function at one loop in the decoupling limit. Using identities derived from the general mode equation, we reveal how seemingly independent loop contributions combine and their non-boundary parts cancel once the associated counterterms are included. This reduction requires no explicit mode-function solution. The leading adiabatic long-mode response reduces to a total derivative in loop momentum, which requires an additional regularization prescription.

papers.title_en: The Virasoro Bootstrap: from the $c\sim1$ desert to coupled Potts
papers.abstract_en: We develop a numerical conformal bootstrap for two-dimensional CFTs with $c>1$ based on Virasoro conformal blocks, computed with Zamolodchikov's recursion and optimal polynomial interpolation. As a first test we isolate an island around three decoupled Ising models. We then consider three 3-state Potts models coupled through their energy operators, a candidate irrational CFT. Mixed correlators isolate the decoupled theory in an island, and different gap assumptions, motivated by perturbation theory, yield a peninsula that contains the coupled fixed point but not the decoupled one. Finally, we explore the standard single-correlator bound on the lowest-dimension scalar primary in the OPE of two identical scalars. We find that for central charges just above $c=1$ the bound collapses over a wide range of external dimensions. This excludes any theory whose lightest scalar is absent from its own OPE and lies in this range, and supports the conjecture that no compact CFT exists in this region. We explain several features of these bounds analytically.

papers.title_en: Surrogate model of gravitational waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries based on the hybridization of WaSABI-C inspirals with numerical relativity waveforms
papers.abstract_en: With the incorporation of aligned-spin dynamics into self-force waveform models, such as the WaSABI-C inspiral model, and with the release of the SXS collaboration's third public catalog of NR simulations, the gravitational waveform modeling community has made significant advances in the modeling of spinning, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries. In light of these developments, we present WaSABINRHybSur2dq15, the first surrogate model to incorporate information from self-force theory, post-Newtonian theory, and numerical relativity. The model is trained on 65 hybrid waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries with mass ratios spanning 1:1.25 to 1:20 and aligned-spins for the primary black hole ranging -0.5 to 0.5. The hybrid waveforms are generated from a set of WaSABI-C inspirals and NR waveforms from the third SXS public catalog. The model covers the parameter domain $1.25 \leq q \leq 15$ and $|χ_{1z}| \leq 0.5$, and includes the $(2,2),\, (2,1),\, (3,3),\, (4,4),$ and $(5,5)$ spin-weighted spherical harmonic modes. The model also spans the entire LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) frequency band (with $f_{\text{low}}=20$ Hz) for total masses $M \gtrsim 111.5\,M_{\odot}$. We find that the WaSABINRHybSur2dq15 model faithfully reproduces the hybrid waveforms with mismatches less than $10^{-3}$ for total masses in the range $80\,M_{\odot} \leq M \leq 300\,M_{\odot}$.

papers.title_en: Emergence of Lorentzian geometry from string Carroll geometry
papers.abstract_en: The near horizon region of a generic non extremal black hole has been extensively studied in terms of a Carrollian geometry with two null directions, also called a string Carroll geometry. We investigate how this string Carroll geometry evolves to a Lorentzian throat as the four dimensional Reissner-Nordström (RN) black hole approaches extremality. We identify the quadratic temporal contribution that is suppressed in the non extremal description but is required to recover the $\mathrm{AdS}_2$ curvature. Approaching the outer horizon and extremality simultaneously, scaling the horizon separation together with the radial distance and correspondingly rescaling Killing time, brings this contribution into the leading longitudinal metric alongside the Rindler sector. In ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, the string Carroll metric alone has a Lorentzian limit with a flat longitudinal sector. The quadratic temporal term arises from the bilinear of the leading and subleading longitudinal coframe fields and supplies the missing curvature, while higher radial contributions vanish. The reconstructed limiting geometry is already locally $\mathrm{AdS}_2\times S^2$ at finite positive scaled horizon separation; setting this parameter to zero makes the selected horizon extremal without changing the local curvature. The limiting metric and Maxwell field satisfy the Einstein-Maxwell equations. In static coordinates, the temporal component again follows from the quadratic term, while the radial component requires summing contributions from all radial orders. The reconstruction provides a geometric starting point for investigating which expansion data must be retained when extending calculations based on the non extremal string Carroll description into the throat regime, including their implications for string, particle and field dynamics.

papers.title_en: Toward the one- and two-loop EFTofLSS for Simons Observatory CMB lensing
papers.abstract_en: Cosmic microwave background (CMB) lensing observations are becoming sensitive to non-linear structure formation and baryonic feedback scenarios. The effective field theory of large-scale structure (EFTofLSS) provides a systematic description of matter clustering in the mildly non-linear regime, accounting for baryonic effects through counterterms and offering a consistent framework for cross-correlations with other observables. We perform a Fisher forecast for the joint Simons Observatory temperature, polarization, and CMB lensing likelihood using noiseless data vectors with different baryonic feedback scenarios, modelling non-linear structure formation using the one- and two-loop EFTofLSS. We find that, with a single additional parameter, obtained through a principal-component analysis of the EFTofLSS counterterms, both the one- and two-loop EFTofLSS provide a good fit across the baryonic feedback scenarios considered. This parameter is closely aligned with the effective AGN heating temperature $T_{\rm AGN}$. Both loop orders reduce cosmological parameter biases, with only a small loss in marginalized precision at fixed scale cuts. We find that the one-loop EFTofLSS yields unbiased estimates over a range of scales similar to the dark-matter-only model, while the two-loop EFTofLSS extends this range to smaller scales and accommodates different feedback scenarios more robustly. When each model is evaluated at the smallest scales for which its cosmological parameter estimates remain unbiased, the two-loop EFTofLSS yields stronger constraints than the dark-matter-only model.

papers.title_en: Compensator-free $\mathcal N=2$ extension of ModMax and scalar propagation
papers.abstract_en: We construct a compensator-free $\mathcal N=2$ superconformal and electric--magnetic duality-invariant extension of ModMax electrodynamics in ordinary flat superspace. The action is built entirely from the Abelian vector multiplet, using a derivative composite of its field strength, and the self-duality equation is solved to all orders as a formal series in the coupling. Upon setting the additional $\mathcal N=1$ chiral multiplet to zero, the action is equivalent off shell to the $\mathcal N=1$ ModMax action of Bandos, Lechner, Sorokin and Townsend through a local vector-prepotential redefinition. Since the complex scalar of the $\mathcal N=2$ multiplet is set to zero in this reduction, we add one superconformal interaction that leaves the reduction unchanged and is chosen to ensure causal scalar propagation. On constant non-null electromagnetic backgrounds with vanishing scalar expectation value, the higher-order scalar coefficients are fixed by requiring the scalar quadratic action to satisfy the stress-tensor square-root flow, modulo equations of motion and a total derivative. We determine the quadratic action of the full multiplet on these backgrounds to all orders. Its analytic continuation to finite $γ\geq0$ gives causal scalar propagation, with transverse speed squared $e^{-γ}$ and unit longitudinal speed, the ModMax photon cones, luminal gauginos with positive kinetic coefficients, and auxiliary fields with algebraic equations of motion.

papers.title_en: An Intrinsically Gapless Topological Phase with Dipole Symmetry
papers.abstract_en: We show that the boundary fractionalization familiar from gapped topological insulators can enforce bulk gaplessness in a dipole-conserving system. In a one-dimensional fermion model with charge conservation, dipole conservation, and particle-hole symmetry, we realize an intrinsically gapless symmetry-protected topological (igSPT) phase combining a dipolar Luttinger liquid with half-quantized boundary charges. This boundary structure obstructs a unique gapped bulk preserving these symmetries and lattice translation. Remarkably, the two charge-neutral edge configurations remain exactly degenerate even at finite size due to dipole conservation and particle-hole symmetry. The boundary fractionalization also manifests as shifted conformal towers in the dipole-resolved entanglement spectrum, reflecting distinct conformal boundary conditions of the Luttinger liquid. We support our analysis of the igSPT by studying exactly-solvable limits and performing DMRG computations, establishing its stability for a wide range of tuning parameters.

papers.title_en: Baryonic feedback and intrinsic alignments in profile: a frequentist view of DES Y3 cosmic shear
papers.abstract_en: Current cosmic shear surveys primarily constrain $S_8$ and $Ω_\mathrm{m}$, while most other model parameters remain dominated by priors. Consequently, marginal posteriors are vulnerable to prior-volume effects, particularly through degeneracies among $S_8$, baryonic feedback, and intrinsic alignment (IA) model parameters. To isolate data-driven constraints from prior volume effects, we compare profile likelihoods with Bayesian posteriors for DES Y3 cosmic shear under the DES Y3+KiDS-1000 Hybrid model. For cosmic shear alone, the profile global best fit and the marginal posterior mean agree in $S_8$, but the profile likelihood reveals a strong degeneracy between feedback strength and $S_8$, leaving the upper $1σ$ limit on $S_8$ determined by the assumed feedback range. External CMB information on parameters other than $Ω_\mathrm{m}$ and $S_8$ breaks this degeneracy, suppressing prior-volume effects and reconciling the profiles with the posteriors. With CMB data included, small-scale cosmic shear data prefers moderate baryonic feedback strengths consistent with hydrodynamical simulations calibrated to observed gas fractions. Furthermore, additional unconstrained parameters in the tidal alignment and tidal torquing (TATT) model result in weaker constraints, shifting and broadening the $S_8$ profile relative to the nonlinear linear alignment (NLA) model. Adding DES Y3 shear ratios mitigates this degeneracy, bringing profile likelihood and marginal posteriors into close agreement.

papers.title_en: A Collapsar-Disk Origin for GW190814
papers.abstract_en: GW190814 was a remarkable gravitational-wave (GW) event: a merger between a $23 M_\odot$ black hole (BH) and a $2.6\,M_\odot$ compact object, with an extreme mass ratio that is difficult to reproduce through standard isolated-binary or dynamical formation channels. Recent work has shown that neutrino-cooled collapsar disks can become gravitationally unstable and fragment, producing neutron stars (NSs) or low-mass BHs in orbit around the newly formed central BH. These fragments may subsequently interact, scatter, merge with one another, or inspiral into the central remnant. We explore the possibility that GW190814 originated from such a collapsar-disk fragment merging with the central BH. A key prediction of this scenario is a temporal association with a stripped-envelope supernova preceding the GW event, and we identify the Type Ib supernova candidate SN2019npv, which occurred inside the GW190814 credible volume approximately 60 days before coalescence, as a possible electromagnetic precursor. Although this delay is too long for a conventional kilonova counterpart, we show that three-body interactions among disk fragments can excite some compact objects to wide orbits and produce merger delays of weeks to months. While GW190814 itself was not expected to produce detectable tidal-disruption-powered emission, future delayed mergers in this channel could generate luminous transients through either reprocessed kilonova heating or shocks driven as merger ejecta collide with the preceding supernova ejecta. Finally, treating SN2019npv as the electromagnetic counterpart makes GW190814 a bright standard siren and yields $H_{0} = 71.1^{+9.3}_{-7.5} km s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}$.

papers.title_en: Exact static two-body gravitational potential at first self-force order
papers.abstract_en: The static interaction potential of two non-spinning point masses in general relativity was previously computed through seventh post-Newtonian order using methods of effective field theory. Its probe limit, or zeroth-self-force contribution, is determined exactly by the Schwarzschild geometry. We derive a closed-form expression for the static first-self-force correction, quadratic in the light mass, and establish its weak-field expansion to all orders. Working in harmonic gauge, we construct the required Green function for the coupled linearised gravitational equations about the Schwarzschild background. We fix its homogeneous contributions and regularised coincident limit by matching to the dimensionally continued point-source theory. The result reproduces known perturbative coefficients and determines all higher static post-Newtonian coefficients in this mass sector.

papers.title_en: I want to Break Free: The Positive Side of Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract_en: We study the role of internal field-space symmetries in Effective Field Theories constrained by positivity bounds. For theories with $N$ real scalar fields, we classify derivative operators according to the internal symmetries they preserve, organising them into hierarchies based on the maximal symmetry $O(N)$ and its subgroups. We find that the Wilson coefficients of operators that depart from an enhanced symmetry are bounded in terms of those that respect it. This means that departures from an enhanced internal symmetry cannot be made arbitrarily large while maintaining a standard UV completion, even when the enhanced internal symmetry was not imposed in constructing the low-energy theory. Moreover, along a cascade of progressively smaller preserved subgroups, the coefficients of operators preserving lower levels of symmetry are bounded by those preserving larger subgroups in the cascade, and are consequently subject to progressively stronger constraints. We demonstrate these results through a variety of examples involving $2-2$ and $3-3$ scattering of indefinite states formed from superpositions of multiple scalar species.

papers.title_en: Multiprobe strategies for Kinematic Lensing with the Roman Space Telescope High Latitude Wide Area Survey
papers.abstract_en: In its latest design, the High Latitude Wide Area Survey (HLWAS) Medium Tier comprises overlapping photometric and spectroscopic data across 2,300 square degrees. This dataset enables Kinematic Lensing (KL), a Weak Lensing (WL) technique that exploits galaxy kinematics to control for shape noise, the dominant statistical limitation of traditional WL. We present several simulated analyses quantifying the expected cosmological science return of a Roman KL analysis with the latest design of the HLWAS: We explore KL prospects with early Roman data from the Deep Tier fields and from the early Medium Tier fields; we demonstrate the impact of different roll-angle choices on the KL performance; we benchmark KL against traditional WL; we introduce a KL-based multiprobe analysis that jointly models KL, galaxy clustering, and galaxy-galaxy lensing. In these analyses, we consider systematics, including photometric uncertainties, shear calibration bias, galaxy bias, and baryonic feedback. Our results show that KL alone achieves a dark energy figure of merit (FoM) of 22.54, which is more than a factor of two improvement over a corresponding WL analysis. The KL multiprobe approach improves the full-survey FoM to 34.58, even assuming conservative scale cuts in the clustering and galaxy-galaxy lensing. For the HLWAS roll-angle strategy, we find that the current plan of 4 passes with rotations of approximately 0, 10, 170, 180 degrees are near optimal for KL.

papers.title_en: Wide Area VISTA Extragalactic Survey (WAVES): Redshift-limited selection of targets for the Wide survey using decision-tree classification
papers.abstract_en: The Wide-Area VISTA Extragalactic Survey (WAVES) on the 4-metre Multi-Object Spectroscopic Telescope (4MOST) includes two flux-limited subsurveys with very high (95%) completeness requirements: Wide over $\sim\!1200$ deg$^2$ and Deep over $\sim\!65$ deg$^2$. Both are $Z$-band selected, and additionally redshift-limited, while the true redshifts are not known a priori but will only be measured by 4MOST. Here, we present a classification-based method to select the targets for WAVES-Wide. Rather than estimating individual redshifts for the input photometric galaxies, we assign probabilities of them being below $z=0.2$, the redshift limit of the subsurvey.This is done with the supervised machine learning approach of eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), trained and tested on a comprehensive spectroscopic sample overlapping with WAVES fields and using nine-band VST+VISTA photometry for the feature space. We check the performance of our classifier both for the fiducial WAVES-Wide limits, as well as for a range of neighboring redshift and magnitude thresholds, finding purity and completeness at the level of 90-95% depending on the test set. The metrics deteriorate for sources close to the selection limits and for test sets selected from DESI, not used in training. We apply the classifier trained on the full spectroscopic sample to the 8.6 million galaxies from the WAVES photometric catalog. This gives us about 1.2 million target candidates, reducing to 1 million if we apply an XGB probability threshold $P_\mathrm{XGB}(z\leq0.2) > 0.72$. Our work demonstrates that a machine-learning classifier could be used to select a flux- and redshift-limited sample from deep photometric data.

papers.title_en: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
papers.abstract_en: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $Π_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[ρ]\in H^3(BG,Π_2)$ that characterizes the mixing. We develop a method to extract anomalies of these symmetries in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near its endpoints. We also construct explicit qubit symmetry actions in $d=1,2,3$ spatial dimensions for a $2$-group with $G=Π_2=\mathbb{Z}_2$. These actions share the same nontrivial Postnikov class but include both anomaly-free and anomalous realizations. Their cohomological anomalies are classified by $H^{d+2}(B\mathcal G,U(1))$, which is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=1,2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=3$, and our constructions realize every class in these dimensions. Our results connect higher-group symmetry and its anomalies to concrete lattice operations, providing a microscopic framework for studying anomalous symmetries.

papers.title_en: Cherenkov radiation constraint on the photon mass from a two-form gauge potential
papers.abstract_en: We investigate how electromagnetic radiation in massive antisymmetric tensor theories can be used to constrain the photon mass. In this context, massive electrodynamics constitutes one realization of the $B \wedge F$ class of models in $(3+1)$ dimensions and is obtained by dualizing Stueckelberg-like massive gauge theories. Notably, this model is characterized by the mixing of a $U(1)$ gauge potential with an Abelian $3$-form field of the type found in the topological sector of QCD. We then examine how mass affects permittivity and susceptibility and, consequently, modifies the refractive index through the dispersion relation. We subsequently investigate the electromagnetic radiation emitted by a moving charged particle as it interacts with a medium within the framework of massive electrodynamics. Our findings indicate that the medium through which the particle travels drives the radiation, in a manner analogous to the Cherenkov effect. Applying our results to data on Cherenkov radiation produced at Super-Kamiokande, we derive a photon mass bound of 1 eV ($ 10^ {- 36} $ kg), which is consistent with known estimates based on superconductors.

papers.title_en: Theory of the Ferroaxial Charge Density Wave in 1T-TiSe$_2$
papers.abstract_en: Recent experiments using strain to probe the charge-density wave (CDW) of 1T-TiSe$_2$ have uncovered additional transitions and broken symmetries inside the CDW state. The elastocaloric effect reveals a second transition below $T_\mathrm{CDW}$, which elastoresistivity shows to be associated with ferroaxial order, breaking all vertical mirror symmetries while preserving inversion. In addition, at even lower temperatures, a diverging nematic susceptibility has been reported through elastoresistivity. In this work, we argue that this rich phenomenology cannot be explained by the standard $L_1^-$ CDW order parameter, and instead requires the existence of a secondary CDW order parameter. Based on symmetry, microscopic, and diffraction considerations, we propose this subleading CDW to have $L_2^-$ symmetry. By analyzing the Landau theory of coupled $L_1^-$ and $L_2^-$ orders in the presence of strain, we reproduce the phase boundaries observed in the elastocaloric measurements and the emergence of ferroaxial order below the CDW transition. Moreover, the model supports a third threefold-rotational symmetry breaking transition at lower temperatures, consistent with the reported divergence of the nematic susceptibility.

papers.title_en: Mass inflation and the $C^2$-inextendibility of spherically symmetric charged scalar field dynamical black holes
papers.abstract_en: It has long been suggested that the Cauchy horizon of dynamical black holes is subject to a weak null singularity, under the mass inflation scenario. We study in spherical symmetry the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations and \textit{while we do not directly show mass inflation}, we obtain a "mass inflation/ridigity" dichotomy. More precisely, we prove assuming (sufficiently slow) decay of the charged scalar field on the event horizon, that the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}= \mathcal{D} \cup \mathcal{S}$ for two (possibly empty) disjoint connected sets $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{S}$ such that: _$\mathcal{D}$ (the dynamical set) is a past set on which the Hawking mass blows up (mass inflation scenario). _$\mathcal{S}$ (the static set) is a future set isometric to a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon i.e.\ the radiation is zero on $\mathcal{S}$. As a consequence, we establish a novel classification of Cauchy horizons into three types: dynamical ($\mathcal{S}=\emptyset$), static ($\mathcal{D}=\emptyset$) or mixed, and prove that $\mathcal{CH}_{i^+}$ is globally $C^2$-inextendible. Our main motivation is the $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship Conjecture for a realistic model of spherical collapse in which charged matter emulates the repulsive role of angular momentum: in our case the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon system on one-ended space-times. As a result, we prove in spherical symmetry that: - two-ended asymptotically flat space-times are $C^2$-future-inextendible i.e. $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship is true for Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon, assuming the decay of the scalar field on the event horizon at the expected rate. - In the one-ended case, the Cauchy horizon emanating from time-like infinity is $C^2$-inextendible. This result suppresses the main obstruction to $C^2$ Strong Cosmic Censorship in spherical collapse.

papers.title_en: The inner dark-matter structure of TNG50 simulated galaxies
papers.abstract_en: In the $Λ$CDM framework, galaxies evolve within dark matter (DM) haloes, where baryonic processes can modify the inner structure of the DM distribution. In particular, the condensation of baryons and associated feedback mechanisms can alter the inner density profiles of haloes, motivating detailed studies of their central regions. We investigate inner DM density slopes in TNG50 galaxies, their relation to galaxy properties, and their cosmic evolution. We assess baryonic effects on the inner DM structure by comparing galaxies with their DM-only (DMO) counterparts. We constructed spherically averaged DM density profiles in both runs. The inner slope was quantified using an inner linear fit, defined as a direct power-law fit to the central region of the density profiles and motivated by the asymptotic behaviour of generalised Navarro-Frenk-White models. Subhaloes were matched between simulations and tracked across redshifts $z = 0$, $0.2$, $0.7$, and $1$. The inner DM structure of galaxies in TNG50 shows that high-stellar-mass systems ($M_\star \gtrsim 10^{11}$ M$_\odot$) exhibit shallow inner slopes regardless of whether they are centrals or satellites, while lower-mass galaxies ($M_\star \lesssim 10^9$ M$_\odot$) show a broader diversity of profiles. At fixed stellar mass, low-mass satellites tend to be more cuspy, with the steepest slopes found in redder systems with lower $V_{\mathrm{max}}$ in more massive host haloes. At the population level, we find a modest cosmic evolution, with steeper profiles towards low redshifts in the hydrodynamical run and the opposite trend in DMO, while hydrodynamical galaxies remain systematically steeper at all redshifts. Finally, we verified that the fiducial interval provides the most suitable reference for measuring the shallowest inner slopes of DM density profiles at the TNG50 resolution limit.

papers.title_en: Fractional $θ$-dependence from the sum over all instanton sectors
papers.abstract_en: An instanton carries integer topological charge, seemingly at odds with the multibranched $θ$ dependence of the Yang-Mills vacuum. We show that summing over all instanton sectors resolves this mismatch in self-dual supersymmetric $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$ and $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Yang-Mills theories with a chiral mass, in two and four dimensions. The path integral reduces to a sum of instanton moduli-space volumes, yielding the multibranched vacuum structure. In four dimensions, this extends Nekrasov's instanton counting for Seiberg-Witten theory to a QCD-like theory without scalars.

papers.title_en: Hamiltonian variational reconstruction of the 3D magnetic geometry of relativistic jets
papers.abstract_en: Every resolved image of a relativistic jet encodes its magnetic field, yet no image records which way the field points: synchrotron intensity and linear polarization probe the field only through even combinations of its components. We introduce H-MOG (Hamiltonian Magnetic Optimization of Geometry), a variational method that reconstructs the 3D field from the jet width $W(z)$ and linear polarization $p(z)$, and we determine exactly which properties of the field these observables fix. We validate H-MOG on synthetic jets and apply it to ten GRMHD simulations of magnetically arrested and standard accretion flows at five spins, testing four routes to recover the field sense: a rotation-measure term, full 3D sampling, a spin-based prior, and resolved multi-frequency polarimetry with internal Faraday rotation, including ray-traced GRMHD images. For a side-on jet, $W$ and $p$ are exactly invariant under field reversal and under reflection through the plane of the sky, which reverses the handedness of the helix. Within this four-fold degeneracy the geometry is recovered, with $\langle\cos\rangle \simeq 0.94$-$1.00$ on synthetic jets and $0.76$-$0.98$ on the GRMHD library up to the mirror image, which is inherited from the initial guess. The rotation measure fixes the sign of the toroidal field but not that of the poloidal field, at any resolution; the spin prior fails because spin does not set the poloidal sign. Internal Faraday rotation breaks all four images, but in ray-traced GRMHD images it separates them only weakly. From width and polarization alone, field sense and helical handedness are undetermined; for a side-on jet the poloidal sense requires, beyond the rotation measure, the rotation sense of the field lines, a viewing angle away from $90^\circ$, or circular polarization.

papers.title_en: The large $N$ vector model with angular velocity
papers.abstract_en: We study the free energy of a critical vector model at large $N$ on $S^{1}\times S^{2}$ with an angular velocity $\hatμ$ without the singlet constraint. We study the model for which the large $N$ dynamics is controlled by the uniform saddle point of the auxiliary field arising in the Hubbard-Stratanovich transformation. The leading high-temperature behaviour is determined analytically both as an expansion about $\hatμr=0$ and $\hatμ^{2}r^{2}=1$ where $r$ is the radius of the sphere. We supplement the analytic results with a numerical analysis that agrees with both the analytical expansions in their respective regimes and smoothly interpolates between them. The leading high-temperature contribution to the free energy develops a pole at $\hatμ^{2}r^{2}=1$, in agreement with expectations from the thermal effective field theory. Its residue coincides with that of the massless free theory. Sub-leading terms, however, exhibit non-analytic dependence on the angular velocity and distinguish the critical fixed-point result from the free theory answer. The residue at the pole can also be obtained by placing the model on the pp-wave geometry. We show that the residue agrees with that obtained from the direct computation. The free energy of the model connects the non-trivial fixed point of the $O(N)$ model at $\hatμr=0$ to its free fixed point at $\hatμ^2r^2=1$.

papers.title_en: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

papers.title_en: Helical Domain-Wall-Ring Networks Reshape Superconducting Correlations
papers.abstract_en: Extended domain-wall networks that emerge in moiré materials provide a distinct platform for quasi-one-dimensional electronic states. However, the interaction-driven orders in confined networks remain largely unexplored. Here, we discuss superconducting (SC) correlations in interacting helical domain-wall-ring networks in the closed topological domains formed within the moiré patterns of an underlying twisted bilayer honeycomb lattice. We first analyze the system within the framework of an infinite-size theory and show that inter-ring SC-pair tunneling is renormalization-group relevant in an appropriate interaction regime, favoring enhanced SC correlations through inter-ring phase locking. To address finite-size effects resulting from the ring-network geometry, we present a self-consistent variational approach. Our analysis shows that even in the regime where the infinite-size theory predicts strongly coupled pair tunneling, the induced phase-locking scale remains strongly suppressed. In contrast, the SC scaling dimension is governed mainly by density-density interactions and ring geometry, decreasing modestly with decreasing twist angle while remaining insensitive to the pair-tunneling strength. This discrepancy demonstrates that ring networks cannot generally be understood as simple finite-size truncations of their infinite-size counterparts but can exhibit qualitatively distinct collective behavior. Our study highlights how the interplay of confinement effects and ring-network geometry can reshape SC correlations.

papers.title_en: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic Rényi defects
papers.abstract_en: The Rényi entropies of a ball are computed by a conformal defect, the Rényi defect, dual in holography to a hyperbolic black hole. At an index $n_*$ its charged operator merges with its alternate-quantization partner, and the defect loses conformality. Beyond $n_*$ it flows with no source to a conformal defect that breaks the U(1) symmetry; below $n_*$ that defect needs a symmetry-breaking source, so at large $N$, conformality loss makes the breaking spontaneous. The scalar hair beyond $n_*$, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, thus preserves them outside a thin layer at the entangling surface, as conformal symmetry requires. The region outside the layer sets the universal term of the Rényi entropy. We demonstrate the mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, where the saddles are in closed form and numerical methods confirm the flows. On a sphere we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the sphere is large enough; it is then unique and ends at the symmetry-breaking defect. The mechanism needs a scalar mass in a finite window, and for potentials attractive at small amplitude, the symmetry can break before conformality is lost. For operators of low enough dimension, already the second Rényi entropy lies beyond the merger. Classical backreaction does not move the merger at any order; we argue that away from $n_*$ the flows persist at first order.

papers.title_en: Acoustic damping limits superfluid helium as a thermal bath for mechanical resonators
papers.abstract_en: Thermalization is a persistent problem for cryogenic mechanical resonators. The weak supports used to obtain high mechanical quality factors are also poor thermal links, while the optical or microwave fields used for readout and control can heat the resonator above the cryostat temperature. Superfluid helium is therefore an appealing exchange medium: it has excellent low-temperature thermal transport and an inviscid superfluid component, suggesting cooling of mechanical devices without the damping associated with an ordinary fluid. Here we test this idea by immersing a \qty{250}{\micro\meter}-diameter yttrium iron garnet sphere in liquid \textsuperscript{4}He and reading out a \(\sim\qty{12.47}{\mega\hertz}\) mechanical mode using cavity magnomechanics. The mechanical linewidth increases from \qty{6.1}{\hertz} in vacuum to \qty{9.1}{\kilo\hertz} after filling the cavity with liquid helium in the normal state, and reaches \qty{17.5}{\kilo\hertz} deep in the superfluid at \qty{84}{\milli\kelvin}. Thus the mechanical quality factor is reduced by more than three orders of magnitude, and crossing into the superfluid does not recover low dissipation. At the same time, the magnon linewidth remains strongly dependent on microwave power at the lowest temperatures, showing that the sphere is not perfectly anchored to the cryostat despite the large mechanical damping. The result follows from acoustic radiation: the surface motion of the sphere efficiently launches gapless longitudinal sound into the liquid, and a radiation-impedance estimate gives a linewidth of order \qty{25}{\kilo\hertz}. Superfluid helium is therefore not a low-loss thermal bath for mechanical modes that efficiently radiate compression waves. Shear motion, on the other hand, may provide a route around this limitation.

papers.title_en: Milliarcsecond-scale jet reorientations in GRS 1915+105 pointing towards a warped accretion disc
papers.abstract_en: The black hole X-ray binary GRS 1915+105 was persistently X-ray bright for over 26 years before entering a prolonged low X-ray flux state in 2018, while remaining bright at radio wavelengths. Multi-wavelength observations suggest this state results from a complex layer of absorbing material of unknown nature. Radio jet observations provide an unobstructed view of the physical changes during this phase, and recent Very Large Array and East Asian VLBI Network observations revealed substantial changes in the jet position angle (PA). We use higher-resolution VLBI observations to investigate the connection between the obscuration event and the jet behaviour close to the launch region. We observed GRS 1915+105 with the Very Long Baseline Array and European VLBI Network at four epochs during the early obscuration phase (2019-2021), sampling a diverse range of jet and accretion behaviours. We study the milliarcsecond jet morphology and PA changes and relate these to the reported X-ray behaviour. Many post-2018 PAs are significantly offset from the pre-obscuration jet axis, which has a weighted mean of $142^\circ \pm 7^\circ$ on milliarcsecond scales. We measure a maximum offset of $57^\circ \pm 8^\circ$, the largest reported for GRS 1915+105 to date. Our epochs reveal a variety of jet behaviour, ranging from a stable, compact source with a large PA offset, to a bright, flaring source with a similar offset, to an extended jet with a PA closer to the pre-obscuration axis, and a non-detection. The lack of measurable PA changes within individual 8-hour epochs rules out rapid Lense-Thirring precession of the inner disc as the direct driver of the jet reorientation. Instead, the timescales involved, the system geometry, and the apparent connection to the X-ray obscuration favour a radiation-driven warped accretion disc, a configuration that could naturally explain the persistent obscuration.

papers.title_en: The Quasar Main Sequence of Highly Accreting NLSy1 Galaxies
papers.abstract_en: The quasar main sequence, or Eigenvector 1 (EV1), describes the optical diversity of active galactic nuclei, with Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies anchoring the high-accretion end. Recent discoveries of overly massive black holes in the early Universe highlight the need to study low-redshift, low-mass super-Eddington accretors as analogs of rapid black hole growth. We map 18,749 NLSy1 galaxies from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 (DESI DR1) onto the EV1 plane. We compare the spectral properties of the DESI DR1 NLSy1 sample with the SDSS DR17 NLSy1 catalog, analyzed homogeneously. We extract key parameters, including the broad H-beta full width at half maximum (FWHM) and Fe II strength (R4570). To evaluate their accretion states, we derive single-epoch virial black hole masses using an Fe II strength-dependent scaling relation and an Eddington ratio-dependent fundamental plane, and test this choice with an Fe II-independent calibration. The DESI DR1 NLSy1 population occupies the extreme end of the EV1 parameter space, with strong Fe II emission (median R4570 = 0.96 +/- 0.35), similar to the SDSS sample (0.96 +/- 0.36). Under both calibrations, DESI and SDSS sources harbor low-mass black holes (median log black hole mass ~6.81-6.85). About 50% of both samples formally exceed the Eddington limit (log Eddington ratio > 0); this fraction drops to ~8-9% with the Fe II-independent calibration and is thus strongly calibration dependent. The unprecedented sensitivity of DESI has unveiled a large population of low-mass, highly accreting NLSy1 galaxies. Under the high-accretion interpretation, a geometrically thick inner disk would shield the outer broad-line region, naturally producing the observed strong Fe II emission. This sample provides a statistical dataset of low-redshift candidate super-Eddington accretors for understanding early-Universe black hole growth.

papers.title_en: A derived evolution of dark energy from cosmic inhomogeneity confronted with baryon acoustic oscillations and type Ia supernovae
papers.abstract_en: The volume dynamics of space is a framework in which the possibility that matter can be unevenly distributed enters the expansion dynamics directly. It yields a redshift-dependent effective Hubble constant and dark-energy density parameter from the Planck parameters alone. We derive the expansion history $H(z)$ that the framework implies and show that it is flat $Λ$CDM with the cosmological constant replaced by a dark-energy density that grows by 31 percent toward the present, with an effective equation of state $w(0) = -1.21$ approaching $-1$ at high redshift and a present-day age of 13.52 Gyr, 0.30 Gyr younger than in the homogeneous limit. We confront it with the DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations and the Pantheon+ type Ia supernovae, with the Hubble constant, the sound horizon and the supernova absolute magnitude free, so that only the shape of $H(z)$ is tested. Relative to $Λ$CDM the prediction is disfavored by $Δχ^2 = 65$ with one parameter fewer. A free matter density reduces this to $Δχ^2 = 42$, because each probe alone accommodates the model only with incompatible matter densities (0.35 from the oscillations, 0.54 from the supernovae). Their combination bounds the heterogeneity amplitude to $σ_8 < 0.14$ at 95 percent confidence, against the Planck value 0.81 that enters the derivation; the best fit of the heterogeneous model is its homogeneous limit, flat $Λ$CDM. At the leading order in which it is currently evaluated, the heterogeneous contribution therefore cannot account for the Hubble tension, and it acts opposite to the evolution of dark energy that current distance data favor.

papers.title_en: Geometric duality between effective field theories. Part II. Exact classical solutions
papers.abstract_en: Geometric duality reveals a novel bridge between a series of well-known scalar effective field theories: the Yang-Mills theory coupled to a specific scalar sector (aka the Yang-Mills-scalar theory), the nonlinear sigma model on a symmetric coset space, the Dirac-Born-Infeld theory, and the special Galileon theory. In our previous work, we used the geometric duality to map scattering amplitudes in the various theories to one another. In this sequel, we show that the duality makes it also possible to transport exact classical solutions. Thus, exact solutions of the nonlinear sigma model are mapped to a subset of solutions of the Yang-Mills-scalar theory. Likewise, solutions of the special Galileon theory map to solutions of the Dirac-Born-Infeld theory, which in turn map to solutions of the nonlinear sigma model coupled to dynamical gravity. For all these duality maps, we provide explicit examples of exact solutions of the source theory and their corresponding image in the target theory. While the duality maps are manifest at the level of certain geometric building blocks of the theories, we show that with a suitable choice of parametrisation, it is also possible to map directly the elementary scalar fields of the various theories to one another. This offers a practically convenient tool for constructing new exact solutions of the target theories. Finally, the duality sequence including the nonlinear sigma model and the Yang-Mills-scalar theory can be extended by uplifting the solutions of the latter to a higher-dimensional spacetime. One thus arrives at a class of exact solutions of pure Yang-Mills theory in higher dimensions. In a similar vein, it is possible to obtain exact solutions of higher-dimensional pure gravity by uplifting solutions of the nonlinear sigma model, coupled to dynamical gravity, obtained via a duality map from solutions of the special Galileon theory.

papers.title_en: Matrix Holography on an Optical Lattice
papers.abstract_en: We propose an analog quantum-simulation protocol based on a lattice of atomic ensembles and time-averaged Floquet dynamics to construct the four-body potentials that typically appear in bosonic BFSS-like matrix quantum mechanics. In contrast to gate-based digital implementations requiring deep circuits, our approach generates the target model through a fixed set of control stages per Floquet cycle, keeping the number of consecutive unitaries constant with respect to the matrix size $N$. The principal scaling cost in our construction is given by the frequency range required to control the growing lattice. We show that this cost grows at most as $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$, giving a polynomial scaling route to large$-N$, attractive to experimental implementation. Additionally, we demonstrate that the coupling parameter can be tuned beyond $\mathcal{O}(1)$, enabling the simulation of strong-coupling physics necessary for holographic phases.

papers.title_en: Measuring the Neutron-Star Moment of Inertia using Nonlinear Orbital Variations from Lense-Thirring Precession
papers.abstract_en: A future measurement of Lense-Thirring (LT) precession using a binary radio pulsar is expected to yield the pulsar's moment of inertia ($I_{\rm p}$). However, most of the known pulsar-binary systems expected to provide this opportunity will exhibit linear variations in the orbital elements, due to LT precession, that are difficult to separate from distance-dependent variations induced by other mechanisms. In this work, we demonstrate that the pulsar-timing signature of LT precession for an arbitrary orbital orientation produces nonlinear orbital variations after a sufficient amount of time; if detected, these nonlinear variations provide a means to constrain $I_{\rm p}$ without the need for independent measurements of orbital geometry or distance. We show through simulations that these nonlinear signatures are indeed detectable in pulsar-binary systems with an appropriate combination of timing precision and orbital geometry. Our simulations also show that nonlinear orbital variations from LT precession are expected to be detectable in PSR J1757$-$1854 and that its $I_{\rm p}$ can be constrained to precision as high as 10% by 2040 even without knowledge of distance.

papers.title_en: Accreting stellar-mass black holes
papers.abstract_en: Accreting stellar-mass black holes exhibit dramatic variability across the electromagnetic spectrum, including spectral state transitions, outbursts, and jet production, making them unique laboratories for understanding accretion processes in strong gravitational fields. This review synthesizes recent progress in understanding these systems, focusing on their continuum emission, timing properties, emission lines, and X-ray polarization. A complex interplay between the accretion disk, the so-called corona, and jet underlies the observed spectral and timing behavior, with quasi-periodic oscillations and broadband noise providing windows into the dynamics of the innermost accretion flow. Emission lines across all wavelengths serve as critical diagnostics of disk structure, outflows, and reprocessing, while iron K lines in the X-ray band probe the properties of the inner disk through relativistic reflection. Polarization studies suggest that the corona is likely extended perpendicular to the jet axis in the hard state, while the soft state remains poorly understood, with observations that do not yet conform to simple theoretical expectations; a puzzle that continues to challenge our interpretation of accretion geometry. Despite significant advances, fundamental questions remain about the physical origins of state transitions, the role of magnetic fields in driving outflows and shaping the accretion flow, and the connection between disk instabilities and jet launching. This review underscores the need for future multi-wavelength, timing, and polarimetric studies to deepen our understanding of accretion physics in strong-gravity environments.

papers.title_en: The formation of the first cosmic structures in hybrid Milgromian cosmology
papers.abstract_en: Tackling cosmology with Milgromian Dynamics (MOND) has been a challenge ever since its theoretical inception. In a hybrid MOND scheme, a hypothesized light sterile neutrino of $\approx$ 11 eV/$c^2$ rest-mass is able to provide realistic initial conditions, fitting the third peak of the Planck CMB power spectrum as a Hot Dark Matter (HDM) component. At the same time, MOND governs the gravitational dynamics of density perturbations, while the background expansion follows the standard FLRW metric. We conduct and analyze hydrodynamical simulations of the fiducial $Λ$CDM model ($H_0 = 67.8$ km/s/Mpc, $Ω_m \approx 0.31$, $Ω_{\text{CDM}} \approx 0.26$), the progenitor $ν$HDM model ($H_0 = 67.64$ km/s/Mpc, $Ω_m = 0.3, Ω_ν\approx 0.26$), and its optimized version (opt-$ν$HDM model, $H_0 \approx 55.6$ km/s/Mpc, $Ω_m \approx 0.49$, $Ω_ν \approx 0.42$), utilizing the publicly available codes RAMSES and Phantom of RAMSES. We compare for the first time the total matter power spectrum $P(k)$ of the hydrodynamical simulations at various redshifts, examining the systematic differences of the three investigated cosmologies. The redshift evolution of the power spectrum of the $Λ$CDM model compared to the $ν$HDM variants' counterpart offers important insight about the onset of structure formation. The combination of a light sterile neutrino and MOND gravity exceeds the $Λ$CDM model's matter $P(k)$ over all collapsing scales at late times ($z\lesssim 1$). The density and velocity fields reveal a distinct difference between the underlying laws of gravity. Regardless of the modeled dependence in the jointly estimated data from Planck, DES Y1, SDSS, and eBOSS, the $ν$HDM hybrid models seem to produce an excess of power at associated resolution scales due to their cosmological design.

papers.title_en: Stability of Homogeneous minimal hypersurfaces in the Page space and $Y^{p,q}$ Sasaki-Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the stability of homogeneous minimal submanifolds in two families of closed Einstein manifolds, the Page space $\mathbb{CP}^2 \# \overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ and the Sasaki-Einstein spaces $Y^{p,q}$, which are equipped with cohomogeneity-one Einstein metrics admitting the isometric action of $SU(2) \times U(1)$ and $U(1) \times U(1) \times SU(2)$ respectively. We determine all the homogeneous, minimal hypersurfaces and explicitly compute the spectrum of their associated stability operators and determine their index.

papers.title_en: Smoothing the Bouncing-Geodesic Singularity in AdS/CFT
papers.abstract_en: Black hole singularities remain a central open problem in quantum gravity. In the AdS/CFT correspondence, bulk spacelike extremal surfaces can probe the black hole interior, and information about the near-singularity geometry is encoded in analytically continued boundary correlators. As the bouncing geodesic approaches the black hole singularity, it becomes nearly null and gives rise to characteristic divergences at complex times. Importantly, these complex-time singularities emerge only in the strict semiclassical limit ($G_N\to 0$ or $c\to\infty$) and are governed by the asymptotically linear quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum. At finite $c$, nonlinear deformations of the QNM trajectories produce suppression kernel that smooths out the complex-time singularities. Using Liouville CFT as an analytically solvable example, we explicitly demonstrate the finite-$c$ deformation of the QNM spectrum and its associated pole-zero structure. We also identify a complementary Gaussian smoothing mechanism arising from finite-energy fluctuations in the thermal spectral decomposition. These results show how finite $G_N$ quantum corrections modify the holographic imprints of the classical black hole singularity.

papers.title_en: Exact Regular Planar Black Holes solutions in Bumblebee gravity
papers.abstract_en: We discuss possibilities of finding exact regular planar black hole solutions in bumblebee gravity with temporal and radial components of the bumblebee field. We consider quadratic and linear potentials, with vanishing and nonzero cosmological constants, respectively. The field equations determine the nonminimal coupling and the relations between the model parameters. Found solution produce regular planar black hole with planar deformation function. Analytical expressions for this functions has been found. This solutions free of singularities at the $r=0$.

papers.title_en: Regular black holes with Minkowskian cores: energy-condition obstruction and optical screening
papers.abstract_en: We construct an asymptotically flat black-hole geometry with a Minkowskian core using gravitational decoupling and analyze its static and rotating extensions. Rather than imposing global energy-condition viability, we show that the vanishing central density required by the Minkowskian core produces a local null-energy-condition obstruction for the present static closure class. The exact mass profile can be written in terms of the regularized incomplete gamma function, which makes transparent both the horizon structure and the exponential localization of the deformation. This localization yields an analytic optical-screening mechanism: on the black-hole branch, deviations of the critical impact parameter from Schwarzschild are controlled by the exponentially suppressed mass deficit at the photon sphere. We also clarify the status of the rotating extension: curvature invariants remain finite on the physical domain $r\geq0$, but this local statement does not by itself establish a globally regular analytic extension through the Kerr disk. These results separate local core regularization from global completeness and explain why strong modifications of the interior can coexist with very small changes in exterior optical observables.

papers.title_en: On 2-loop AdS$_2$ superstring partition function in AdS$_5 \times S^5$ and AdS$_4\times CP^3$
papers.abstract_en: We revisit the 2-loop computation of the partition function of the GS superstring expanded near the AdS$_2$ surface in AdS$_5\times S^5$ and AdS$_4\times {\rm CP}^3$, dual to $\frac{1}{2}$ BPS circular Wilson loop in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM and ABJM theories. In arXiv:2601.08809 it was done in AdS$_5\times S^5$ using dimensional regularization and a UV pole was found. Since dimensional regularization is problematic for the GS string, here we use a heat-kernel cutoff instead. Then the contribution of the local path integral measure, proportional to $δ(0)$, can no longer be ignored. We show that it cancels the $δ(0)$ terms coming from the quartic interactions in the action, leaving the square of the difference ${\rm Str}\,E$ between the regularized numbers of bosonic and fermionic modes. The result is thus UV finite, the pole of arXiv:2601.08809 being an artefact of dimensional regularization. If all fields are regularized with the same smearing kernel, ${\rm Str}\,E=0$ and the 2-loop coefficient $f_2$ vanishes, in tension with $f_2=\frac{3}{32π^2}$ in SYM theory. In the AdS$_4\times{\rm CP}^3$ case the same cancellation leaves a finite term proportional to the square of the coincident value of the massless 2d fermion Green's function, giving, ironically, $f_2=\frac{3}{32π^2}$ instead of $f_2=0$ required by localization. This term is the level-zero (string) part of the result of arXiv:2609.14497 for the AdS$_2\times S^1$ M2 brane in AdS$_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, where it is cancelled by the higher $S^1$ modes, which also remove a finite mass shift of the massless fermion in conflict with the AdS$_2$ supersymmetry. This suggests that the type II string path integral measure should contain an extra contribution, supplied in the IIA case by the parent M2 brane; in the AdS$_5\times S^5$ case it is still to be identified and may resolve the remaining 2-loop mismatch with localization.

papers.title_en: Functional Dimensional Regularization for the Lee-Yang Model
papers.abstract_en: We apply functional dimensional regularization (FDR) to the Lee-Yang universality class, a paradigmatic non-unitary theory, and compute its main critical exponents across the dimension range $3\leq d\leq 6$. By combining a second-order derivative expansion with polynomial field expansions, we obtain results that are compatible with resummed $\varepsilon$-expansion as well as with state-of-the-art estimates from Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy Sphere techniques. This demonstrates that, in the context of non-unitary theories, FDR retains the efficiency and rapid convergence to accurate critical exponents already observed in the Ising and O(N) cases.

papers.title_en: Nonintegral Flux Trapping in Frustrated Josephson Networks of Triplet Superconductors
papers.abstract_en: In a Josephson junction network, anisotropic coupling between spin triplet pairing correlations can lead to frustrated $d$ vector textures that support spontaneous Josephson currents and nonintegral flux trapping. Such networks can appear in superconducting polycrystals, as well as single-crystal superconductors. In analogy to classical spin systems, in which the presence of geometric frustration and anisotropic superexchange can lead to nontrivial spin textures, Josephson networks with anisotropic Josephson couplings cannot simultaneously optimize their $\mathrm{U}(1)$ superconducting phase differences and relative $d$ vector orientations. The internal pairing structure of Cooper pairs twists as they tunnel across the Josephson junction, and the $d$ vector texture enters as an emergent geometric phase which can spontaneously trap fractional flux. For real-valued Josephson couplings between unitary $d$ vectors, the emergent geometric phase reduces to a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ structure, allowing for spontaneous $π$-flux trapping above a critical antisymmetric coupling, distinct from usual half-quantum vortices. Further, we demonstrate a continuously tunable nonintegral flux for complex Josephson couplings. The results of this work reveal new routes to engineer frustrated Josephson networks from the interplay of magnetic textures and spin triplet superconducting pairing order.

papers.title_en: Mass-Varying Neutrinos from an Inverse Symmetron
papers.abstract_en: Neutrinos enter cosmology in different ways and are constrained by distinct observational probes across different epochs: as a relativistic species at high redshift, as a massive but clustering-suppressing component at low redshift, and as a particle physics observable in laboratory experiments. Low (verging on negative) bounds on neutrino mass from galaxy surveys motivate exploration of models where neutrinos may couple to dark energy, causing their mass to vary over cosmic evolution. If the coupling involves an inverse phase transition (symmetry broken, rather than restored, as neutrinos become nonrelativistic) this can tame instabilities in neutrino growth, appear as a lower neutrino mass in galaxy surveys, and add extra suppression to the matter power spectrum. We find that the late-time decoupling shuts down the fifth force and inhibits the excessive growth of neutrino perturbations, thereby eliminating linear-regime instabilities. The model may potentially address the Hubble tension via an early dark energy component localized around the time of recombination.

papers.title_en: Forecast for the detectability of patchy hydrogen reionization in WEAVE-QSO measurements of the Lyman-$α$ forest power spectrum at redshift $z \geq 4$
papers.abstract_en: We present the first detailed forecasts for the detectability of patchy hydrogen reionization in the one-dimensional Ly$α$ forest power spectrum to be measured by the WEAVE-QSO survey. Using the Sherwood-relics reionization simulations and a WEAVE-QSO survey configuration, we generate mock spectra in four redshift bins, $z=4.0,4.2,4.4,$ and $4.6$, in which relic ionization and temperature fluctuations from patchy hydrogen reionization enhance the Ly$α$ forest power spectrum on large scales (i.e., at wavenumber $k\sim 10^{-3},\mathrm{s\,km^{-1}}$). Our Ly$α$ forest pipeline forecasts the power spectrum covariance by considering sample size, spectral resolution, noise subtraction, continuum placement, metal contamination, and damping wings from high-column density absorbers. Applying our covariance forecast within a Bayesian parameter inference framework, we find that the signature of patchy hydrogen reionization should be detectable at a significance of $\simeq 4.5σ$. The forthcoming WEAVE-QSO 1D power spectrum measurements should therefore be able to directly detect and characterize the large-scale relic imprint of patchy hydrogen reionization in the Ly$α$ forest power spectrum at $z\geq 4$.

papers.title_en: Gauge-invariant quantum gravitational corrections to correlation functions
papers.abstract_en: A recent proposal for gauge-invariant observables in inflation [R. Brunetti et al., JHEP 1608 (2016) 032] is examined. We give a generalisation of their construction to general background spacetimes. In flat space, we calculate one-loop graviton corrections to a scalar two-point function in a general gauge for the graviton. We explicitely show how the gauge-dependent terms cancel between the usual self-energy contributions and the additional corrections inherent in these observables. The one-loop corrections have the expected functional form, contrary to another recently studied proposal for gauge-invariant observables [M. B. Fröb, Class. Quant. Grav. 35 (2018) 035005] where this is not the case. Furthermore, we determine the one-loop graviton corrections to the four-point coupling of the gauge-invariant scalar field, and the corresponding running of the coupling constant induced by graviton loops. Interestingly, the $β$ function is negative for most values of the non-minimal coupling of the scalar field to curvature, including minimal and conformal coupling.

papers.title_en: From photons to fractons: Casimir effect in higher-rank electrodynamics and its fractonic branch
papers.abstract_en: The Casimir effect probes the modes that can propagate between boundaries. This makes it useful for fracton gauge theories, where restricted mobility follows from the simultaneous conservation of charge and dipole moment and changes the physical sector of the theory. We compare ordinary Maxwell electrodynamics with a Lorentz-covariant higher-rank theory of a symmetric tensor gauge field and with the scalar-charge fractonic branch selected from it by a preferred timelike background. The comparison shows why the distinction matters. In the full covariant theory, the Euclidean slab problem contains three independently propagating Maxwell-like modes and two coupled vector sectors that do not reduce to independent ordinary modes. Their boundary determinants are well defined, but a Lorentzian analysis shows that the vector sector has an unbounded Hamiltonian, so these determinants do not describe the vacuum energy of a stable fractonic phase. On the fractonic branch, the Gauss constraint removes that vector sector and leaves three stable massless modes: two transverse-traceless tensor modes and one scalar trace mode. For ideal reflectors, the physical Casimir energy is therefore 3/2 of the corresponding Maxwell result, for both equal and complementary boundary conditions. The calculation isolates the effect of the fractonic restriction on the radiative spectrum and clarifies which features of the full higher-rank boundary problem survive in the physical fracton sector.

papers.title_en: Flowing with Displacements and Tilts: Surface Operators in $O(N)$ Models
papers.abstract_en: Defect conformal field theories have special operators of protected dimension known as displacements and tilts. They arise due to the breaking of global symmetries by the defect and the normalisations of their two-point functions are characteristics of the defect. In the case of surface defects, these normalisations are related to some of the anomaly coefficients in the surface effective action. To study these operators and their flows between different defect renormalization group fixed points we present an elegant approach using conformal perturbation theory that easily reproduces the known examples from the critical Wilson-Fisher $O(N)$ model in $4-\varepsilon$ dimensions and allows us to construct new ones in other multiscalar theories. In all the systems that we study the flows are short and under full control, as is the change of the displacement and tilt normalizations. We point out some novel features like the existence of vortices when the defect conformal manifold is not simply connected. In addition to regular human labour, this work relied heavily on generative AI; see full disclosure in methodology section.

papers.title_en: Eccentricity Distribution for Dynamical Gravitational-Wave Merger Channels in The Pinhole Regime
papers.abstract_en: We argue that various dynamical astrophysical black hole merger channels are expected to result in a common eccentricity distribution at gravitational-wave (GW) frequencies relevant for LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA (LVK) in the high eccentricity limit. This follows from the large separation of scales between the GW regime required for creating eccentric mergers in LVK, and the underlying astrophysical formation environment. Our analytical solution shows exceptional agreement with numerical studies. This finding has important implications for both theoretical studies and ongoing searches for eccentric GW sources.
