papers.title_en: Nonexistence of Multiple Black Holes in Stationary Analytic Vacuum spacetimes
papers.abstract_en: We prove the nonexistence of non-rotating and degenerate horizon components in the stationary, asymptotically flat, $I^+$-regular, analytic vacuum spacetime. This result rules out the final case in the classification of stationary analytic black-hole spacetimes. Consequently, the stationary, asymptotically flat, $I^+$-regular, analytic vacuum black hole uniqueness conjecture is settled affirmatively in full.

papers.title_en: A GeV PWN Candidate in the PSR J1135--6055/G293.8+0.6 Field
papers.abstract_en: We present a \textit{Fermi} Large Area Telescope (LAT) study of PSR~J1135--6055 and the composite supernova remnant (SNR) G293.8+0.6. MeerKAT radio observations reveal a bright central plerion within the faint SNR shell, while Chandra observations detect a compact nebula around the pulsar. Together, these observations establish the presence of a PWN within G293.8+0.6. Our analysis of the 20~GeV--1~TeV LAT data yields a point-like excess with $\mathrm{TS}=26.30$ and photon index $Γ=1.63\pm0.33$. Its best-fit position is consistent with the pulsar within the 95\% statistical localization region, and neither the uniform-disk nor Gaussian model is favored, providing no evidence for significant extension. A one-zone leptonic model, together with an independent jet component, reproduces the multiwavelength observations. In this model, the GeV photons are produced mainly by inverse-Compton scattering from relativistic electrons and positrons. Given its positional agreement with the pulsar/PWN and broadband interpretation, we regard the LAT point source as a GeV PWN candidate.

papers.title_en: Stability and instability of the sub-extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole interior for the Einstein-Maxwell-Klein-Gordon equations in spherical symmetry
papers.abstract_en: We show non-linear stability and instability results in spherical symmetry for the interior of a charged black hole -approaching a sub-extremal Reissner-Nordström background fast enough at infinity- in presence of a massive and charged scalar field, motivated by the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in that setting : 1. Stability : We prove that spherically symmetric characteristic initial data to the Einstein-Maxwell- Klein-Gordon equations approaching a Reissner-Nordström background with a sufficiently decaying polynomial decay rate on the event horizon gives rise to a space-time possessing a Cauchy horizon in a neighbourhood of time-like infinity. Moreover if the decay is even stronger, we prove that the spacetime metric admits a continuous extension to the Cauchy horizon. This generalizes the celebrated stability result of Dafermos for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry. 2. Instability : We prove that for the class of space-times considered in the stability part, whose scalar field in addition obeys a polynomial averaged-L^2 (consistent) lower bound on the event horizon, the scalar field obeys an integrated lower bound transversally to the Cauchy horizon. As a consequence we prove that the non-degenerate energy is infinite on any null surface crossing the Cauchy horizon and the curvature of a geodesic vector field blows up at the Cauchy horizon near time-like infinity. This generalizes an instability result due to Luk and Oh for Einstein-Maxwell-real-scalar-field in spherical symmetry. This instability of the black hole interior can also be viewed as a step towards the resolution of the C^2 strong cosmic censorship conjecture for one-ended asymptotically initial data.

papers.title_en: R7-branes and AdS$_{\text{9}}$ solutions in type IIB
papers.abstract_en: We consider the recently found $\mathrm{AdS}_9$ backgrounds in type IIB supergravity. We start by reviewing the solutions in a more convenient set of coordinates, which allows us to explicitly compute a few relevant observables, including the holographic central charge. Subsequently, we study non-supersymmetric 7-brane configurations sourced by the IIB axio-dilaton. We find explicit analytic 7-brane solutions that possess the above $\mathrm{AdS}_9$ backgrounds as their near-horizon geometry. Finally, we discuss the relation of these 7-brane solutions to the R7 branes by imposing the reflection monodromy $τ\rightarrow -\bar τ$ in the transverse plane.

papers.title_en: A Multi-messenger Study of the Cygnus bubble
papers.abstract_en: We perform a comprehensive investigation of particle acceleration at the termination shocks of massive star clusters, with a particular focus on the Cygnus region. Building on the particle-acceleration model for cluster-driven winds, we use recently available spectral and spatial measurements of ultra-high-energy $γ$-rays from the Cygnus bubble to place stringent constraints on the physical conditions in the acceleration zone. By jointly modelling the observed $γ$-ray spectrum and spatial morphology, we derive quantitative limits on key parameters such as the maximum particle energy, acceleration efficiency, magnetic-field strength, and shock geometry, and assess their consistency with a hadronic origin of the emission. These data allow us to refine the target gas profiles within and around the bubble, thereby improving estimates of the expected hadronic $γ$-ray and neutrino fluxes. Using this revised gas model, we compute the neutrino emission associated with the Cygnus bubble and evaluate the statistical significance of a potential neutrino signal from this region for current and near-future high-energy neutrino observatories. Taken together, these results provide a more precise characterisation of the particle-acceleration environment at cluster termination shocks and help clarify the role of young massive star clusters as potential Galactic PeVatrons and contributors to the observed diffuse high-energy neutrino and $γ$-ray emissions.

papers.title_en: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
papers.abstract_en: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= 1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.

papers.title_en: What crossing symmetry forbids just above $c=1$
papers.abstract_en: What does a unitary two-dimensional conformal field theory look like just above $c=1$? Using the numerical conformal bootstrap, we study the four-point function of a scalar Virasoro primary $φ$ such that no primary lighter than $φ$ appears in its operator product expansion with itself. Slightly above $c=1$, crossing symmetry excludes the interval $0.17\lesssimΔ_φ\lesssim1$, although the compact boson realizes every such $Δ_φ$ at $c=1$. Combining this exclusion with results from the modular bootstrap, we show that the lightest primary of a compact unitary conformal field theory at $c=1.0005$ or $1.001$ has dimension $Δ_{\rm gap}<0.17$. Further from $c=1$, the largest excluded central charge at fixed $Δ_φ$ has two sharp minima near $Δ_φ=1/2$ and $4/7$. At these values it lies within $2\times10^{-7}$ of $c=8/7$, where the $\mathbb{Z}_5$ parafermion and its charge-conjugation orbifold have scalars of exactly these dimensions.

papers.title_en: The quantum magic of top quarks
papers.abstract_en: In recent years, a growing community of researchers has been applying ideas from Quantum Information theory to high energy physics. Entanglement is one such quantity, but there are by now many others. This contribution will examine the property of ``magic" (also known as ``non-stabliserness") which, roughly speaking, measures whether quantum systems have a genuine computational advantage over their classical counterparts. We will review the origin of this concept, before describing recent applications in collider physics, including top quark production.

papers.title_en: Universality and Emergent Classicality in Krylov Space
papers.abstract_en: Krylov complexity grows linearly at late times for many systems. In this regime, we give a general spectral formula for the leading growth coefficients of Krylov complexity and its higher moments, without requiring detailed knowledge of the Lanczos coefficients. For states with a narrow energy distribution compared to the bandwidth, dynamics in the Krylov basis resembles motion along a classical trajectory. We demonstrate our results for the critical XY chain and double-scaled SYK. For the latter, we compute the leading late-time behavior of the chord-number moments through one-loop order.

papers.title_en: Entanglement in the Schwinger effect
papers.abstract_en: We analyze entanglement generated by the Schwinger effect using a mode-by-mode formalism for scalar and spinor QED in constant backgrounds. Starting from thermal initial states, we derive compact, closed-form results for bipartite entanglement between particle-antiparticle partners in terms of the Bogoliubov coefficients. For bosons, thermal fluctuations enhance production but suppress quantum correlations: the logarithmic negativity is nonzero only below a (mode-dependent) critical temperature $T_c$. At fixed $T$, entanglement appears only above a critical field $E_{\text{entang}}$. For fermions, we observe a qualitatively different pattern: the fermionic logarithmic negativity is non-vanishing at finite temperature, and is monotonically suppressed by thermal noise. As a function of the electric field, it is non-monotonic, featuring a temperature-independent optimal field strength $E_*$ and decreasing on both sides of the maximum. We give quantitative estimates for analog experiments, where our entanglement criteria convert directly into concrete temperature and electric field constraints. These findings identify realistic regimes where the quantum character of Schwinger physics may be tested in the laboratory.

papers.title_en: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and Rényi entropies
papers.abstract_en: The Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$, in the probe limit, is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. When the scalar mass saturates the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling takes the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase can be found in closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is linearly stable, as is any nodeless probe-limit condensate in the standard quantization with a nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On each slicing it answers a different question about the dual conformal field theory. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and the attenuation of sound are found in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it describes a state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$, arguably the lowest-energy one, and gives its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers that the superfluid effective theory does not describe; they come from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector. The hyperbolic slicing gives in closed form a homogeneous hairy phase of the black holes that compute the charged Rényi entropies of a ball. Its condensate does not vanish at the entangling surface. When sourced by operators inserted there, the phase sets in at Rényi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar.

papers.title_en: Enforced Gaplessness by Combining Non-Anomalous Symmetries
papers.abstract_en: Symmetry-enforced gaplessness is a phenomenon in which a quantum system is forced to be gapless due to its global symmetry. Previous works have mainly focused on anomalous symmetries. Another approach, using symmetry spans, which specify two embeddings of a common symmetry into two larger symmetries, was proposed by the authors. In this work, we show that a symmetry span can enforce gaplessness even when both larger symmetries are invertible and non-anomalous: each alone admits a trivially gapped phase, but because the embeddings differ by a twist associated with a symmetry-protected topological phase, the symmetry they generate admits no gapped phase with finitely many ground states. We present such a span of a finite group and $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$ in 1+1 dimensions, with continuum realizations and a lattice Hamiltonian, with a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space and finitely many parameters, that is gapless in any region of its parameter space. We also discuss a 2+1-dimensional example and spans of only finite symmetries.

papers.title_en: Non-Abelian Dirac oscillator in a uniform Yang--Mills background: spin--isospin mixing and singlet--triplet splitting
papers.abstract_en: We investigate a planar Dirac oscillator coupled to a spatially uniform \(\utwo=\uone\times\su\) Yang--Mills background. The gauge configuration, adapted from the Dossa--Avossevou construction, contains an Abelian magnetic field \(B\), a non-Abelian spatial amplitude \(β\), and a non-Abelian scalar amplitude \(ρ\). Within the Pauli-reduced formulation, the non-Abelian field strength produces a constant operator on \(\mathbb{C}^{2}_{\mathrm{spin}}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{2}_{\mathrm{iso}}\). This operator contains a diagonal internal-Zeeman contribution proportional to \(σ^{3}T^{3}\) and an off-diagonal spin--isospin term proportional to \(σ^{1}T^{1}+σ^{2}T^{2}\). Its diagonalization gives a doubly degenerate aligned branch and two mixed branches with eigenvalues \[ λ_{\mathrm{FM}}=\frac{g^{2}β^{2}}{4m},\qquad λ_{S}=-\frac{g^{2}β(β-2ρ)}{4m},\qquad λ_{T}=-\frac{g^{2}β(β+2ρ)}{4m}. \] Consequently, the aligned internal-Zeeman scale is quadratic in \(β\), whereas the singlet--triplet separation is linear in \(βρ\). The revised formulation makes the sign conventions explicit, verifies the main limiting cases, distinguishes the Pauli-reduced spectrum from a full first-order Dirac diagonalization, and clarifies the physical meaning of the numerical illustrations.

papers.title_en: De-lensing cosmic birefringence with joint reconstruction
papers.abstract_en: Reconstruction of anisotropic cosmic birefringence from the CMB is limited by lensing $B$-mode sample variance and partially degenerate with the lensing curl. We study the joint reconstruction of lensing (gradient and curl) and birefringence at the maximum-a-posteriori point, whose spectra are near-optimal statistics. We predict the joint response and noise analytically, validate them on simulations, and show unbiased inference of its amplitude. Errors will shrink $5$-fold relative to quadratic estimators at SPT-3G+ depths, promising much tighter constraints on parity-violating new physics, owing to the removal of the lensing $B$-polarization sample variance.

papers.title_en: Integrable mass of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black hole
papers.abstract_en: The nontrivial asymptotic structure of rotating black holes in the Bertotti-Robinson universe complicates a direct determination of their conserved mass, leading previous studies to rely on a priori thermodynamic input. We address this long-standing problem using integrability methods, establish local analytic existence and uniqueness via the Cauchy-Kovalevskaja theorem, and obtain a closed expression via a rescaled recurrence whose termination is proved at all orders. The resulting Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson mass coincides with the expression previously derived using the canonical first law identity and reproduces the masses of both Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson subcases. With the mass thus fixed without invoking thermodynamic relations for the first time, we rigorously establish the first law of black-hole thermodynamics and the Smarr formula for a whole family of Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson black holes suitable for future applications.

papers.title_en: Complete quasinormal modes of Type-D black holes. II. Extremal Kerr black holes
papers.abstract_en: We develop a double-confluent Heun method that extends our previous study of complete quasinormal-mode (QNM) spectra of Type-D black holes to extremal Kerr black holes. Radial boundary conditions and angular regularity determine the gravitational frequencies at extremality. Compared with earlier spectra restricted to the conventional Riemann sheet, analytic continuation across frequency branch cuts reveals additional QNMs on unconventional Riemann sheets. Spin continuation follows our Schwarzschild mode families toward extremality, with the survey extending through the 41st overtone on specified angular branches and Riemann sheets. We show for the first time that unconventional Class I modes with $m<0$, continued from unconventional Schwarzschild modes, form zero-damping sequences approaching the superradiant bound $Mω=m/2$ in the extremal limit. Within a fixed angular sector, finite-damping and zero-damping sequences are interspersed in the Schwarzschild overtone ordering, so a single overtone cutoff cannot separate them. Matching near the superradiant bound distinguishes nonextremal sequences accumulating at the critical frequency from isolated QNMs at exact extremality. Scattering-amplitude calculations verify representative roots and their sheet assignments. The expanded spectrum clarifies how Schwarzschild mode families reorganize at extremality, with completeness established by contour counting within a bounded frequency domain on a specified angular branch and Riemann sheet.

papers.title_en: Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes
papers.abstract_en: The recently proposed "phase-space microscope" (PSM) extends quantum gas microscopes by allowing joint, single-shot measurements of position and momentum. We show that the $n$-body correlation functions constructed from such phase-space snapshots determine, in principle, all $n$-body observables of a many-body quantum state. This establishes phase-space imaging as a complete probe of strongly correlated matter, beyond what snapshots of position and momentum can provide---a limitation that goes back to a famous question posed by Pauli. Even without the full reconstruction of the density matrices, the PSM provides valuable insight into the quantum states. We demonstrate this power through several applications: witnessing entanglement hidden from both position and momentum, including between spatially separated collective degrees of freedom; resolving pairing structure across the BEC-BCS crossover, including the phase of the pair wavefunction and the reconstruction of its two-body Wigner function; probing inhomogeneous systems and preformed pairs without long-range order, relevant to the pseudogap phase; extracting the interaction energy in a magnetic field; and measurements of the local Chern marker. Furthermore, we discuss phase imprinting in the matter-wave Fourier plane as an alternative method for probing time-reversal-symmetry-broken phases such as chiral $p$-wave superconductors. Together, these results establish the PSM as a versatile new tool for exploring fundamental features of quantum many-body phases in strongly correlated quantum matter.

papers.title_en: Multipolar exchange in a many-body homonuclear mixture of atoms in different internal states
papers.abstract_en: We develop a general method for constructing the many-body Hamiltonian of pairwise interactions describing homonuclear mixtures of atoms occupying states with different total angular momenta or other quantum numbers. This Hamiltonian explicitly accounts for isotropic interactions governed by low-energy s-wave scattering. The advantage of the irreducible spherical tensor operator formalism is demonstrated: these operators give the Hamiltonian an explicit physical structure, account for all scattering channels, and include multipolar exchange interactions. The latter correspond to the exchange of both angular-momentum projections and the total angular momentum. Particular realizations of the general Hamiltonian, widely used in the physics of ultracold gases, are also analyzed. The resulting Hamiltonian provides a universal framework for investigating a broad range of quantum many-body phenomena in bosonic and fermionic atomic gases.

papers.title_en: Construction of an analytic multi-component accretion environment and its application to Kerr black hole imaging
papers.abstract_en: The construction of accretion environments is fundamental to black hole imaging. From a purely geometric perspective, we construct a novel analytic accretion environment comprising a geometrically thick disk, ring-like bumps with a Gaussian profile, and localized compact emission regions modeled by Gaussian distributions. This environment offers high flexibility, enabling independent adjustments of disk thickness, vertical structure, and the positions and morphologies of localized spots, thereby allowing it to qualitatively mimic high-energy astrophysical phenomena. Applying this model to the Kerr spacetime, we investigate the resulting images via radiative transfer and ray-tracing simulations. The results confirm the effectiveness of the numerical implementation and reveal novel observational signatures of Kerr black holes under multi-component illumination, including multiple bright spots and arc-like structures. This work provides a convenient and fully analytic framework for modeling accretion in curved spacetimes, and offers a new perspective on inferring accretion mechanisms and transient high-energy processes from image features.

papers.title_en: Second-order evolution of spin shear tensor for massive spin-1/2 particles
papers.abstract_en: We present the second-order evolution equation for the spin shear component of the spin tensor in spin-polarized fluids, using a classical description of the spin degrees of freedom. Employing a semi-classical kinetic theory for the massive spin-1/2 particles within the relaxation time approximation we obtain a relaxation-type equation describing the evolution of spin shear driven by various thermodynamic forces and high-order gradient corrections. This equation yields a new set of transport coefficients that govern the dynamics of the dissipative spin-shear tensor.

papers.title_en: Signatures of Novikov-Thorne accretion disks around rotating black holes in semiclassical gravity with trace anomaly
papers.abstract_en: Semiclassical gravity provides a promising framework to address the black hole singularity problem through quantum backreaction characterized by a coupling parameter, making it essential to thoroughly explore the accretion properties around such objects. In this paper, within the framework of semiclassical gravity with type-A trace anomaly, we investigate the thermal radiative signatures of Novikov-Thorne accretion disks around rotating black holes across diverse parameter spaces, focusing on the energy flux density, temperature profile, and thermal luminosity. Our findings demonstrate that the introduction of a positive coupling parameter suppresses disk emission, leading to lower peak values of both energy flux density and temperature, as well as lower peak values and corresponding peak frequencies in thermal luminosity compared to their Kerr counterparts in general relativity. In particular, this discrepancy becomes remarkably pronounced when the black hole possesses a high spin. Mechanistically, increasing the coupling parameter reinforces the effective gravitational field strength of the central compact object, which pushes the equatorial stable circular orbits outward and increases the specific energy of the orbiting matter, thereby reducing the radiative efficiency and weakening the overall disk emission. This suppression mechanism offers a potential astrophysical window to distinguish semiclassical gravity from general relativity and to place observational constraints on the coupling parameter via thermal disk spectra.

papers.title_en: Hidden variable $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological order in a bilayer kagomé antiferromagnet
papers.abstract_en: Topological orders in realistic systems are quite rare, raising one fundamental question of whether they might be harbored with hidden degrees of freedom rather than directly exposed in conventional spins or electrons. We here propose a set of hidden variables and their effective interactions in a bilayer kagomé antiferromagnet. By properly organizing four local states of the spin dimer into two pseudospin-$1/2$ variables ($\boldsymbolτ$ and $\boldsymbolμ$), we identify a regime where an effective Balents-Fisher-Girvin model emerges, realizing a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological order in the hidden $\boldsymbolτ$ sector while the auxiliary $\boldsymbolμ$ sector remains a trivial paramagnet. This hidden nature drastically alters the experimental manifestations. Physical spins map to composite objects, typically convolving fractionalized anyon continua with non-topological magnon excitations. Nevertheless, specific symmetry-selected channels, such as the longitudinal intralayer response, exclusively reveal the bare two-vison continuum without collective-mode dressing. Our findings demonstrate that the topological order could be buried in certain hidden and emergent degrees of freedom, pointing to a promising pathway for seeking elusive topological states disguised within hidden internal degrees of freedom.

papers.title_en: Spectral instability of charged scalar quasinormal modes and superradiance: Stabilizing the unstable
papers.abstract_en: The spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. Small changes to the black-hole scattering potential are known to produce disproportionately large migrations of its quasinormal modes in the complex plane, but it is unclear whether this sensitivity carries over to energy extraction through superradiance. We study this relation for massless charged scalar fields on Reissner--Nordström and Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter backgrounds. A localized positive potential bump, small in mass-scaled height, is displaced outward from the light ring while the original radiative boundary conditions are preserved. In the asymptotically flat case, a quasinormal branch enters the superradiant frequency regime while remaining damped. By searching for competing modes, we show that the least-damped positive-frequency mode also enters this regime, after a series of mode overtakings driven by quasinormal-mode migration. The real-frequency amplification, nevertheless, is only weakly affected and develops no pronounced narrow resonance. In de Sitter black holes, the bump can move an initially growing monopole mode into the damped half of the complex plane, stabilizing selected configurations that are initially modally unstable. After stabilization, the peak superradiant amplification can remain above both its unperturbed value and a gain of $100\%$; it falls below $100\%$ only for more distant bump locations. A prescribed positive perturbation can thus suppress modal growth without changing the superradiant frequency bounds or immediately suppressing the scattering peak.

papers.title_en: MPS overlaps and Sklyanin determinants
papers.abstract_en: We derive explicit overlap functions for integrable matrix product states associated with arbitrary finite-dimensional irreducible evaluation representations of the orthogonal and symplectic twisted Yangians. The central step is to relate the commuting quasi-determinants entering the universal overlap formula to Sklyanin determinants of nested subalgebras. For orthogonal evaluation representations, this relation determines their spectra directly in the Gelfand--Tsetlin basis. In the symplectic case, we combine Sklyanin determinants and minors with a factorization of the nested rank-two boundary matrices to obtain the corresponding spectra. The resulting overlap functions are explicit products parametrized by Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns and require only the highest-weight data of the underlying orthogonal or symplectic representation. Together with the universal ratio of Gaudin determinants and the model-dependent pseudovacuum overlap coefficients, they determine the normalized MPS overlaps. We also express the overlap functions in the orthogonal case beyond evaluation representations in terms of the highest weights arising along the nested twisted-Yangian subalgebras.

papers.title_en: Higher Groupoids of Gauge Potentials in Higher Gauge Theories admitting Weights
papers.abstract_en: We construct an explicit small model for the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances of higher gauge curvatures by algorithmically trivializing their nonlinear Bianchi identities. More precisely, for a finite-type Sullivan minimal Bianchi algebra equipped with positive integer weights, we organize weighted potentials and higher gauge parameters at each fixed curvature into an $\infty$-groupoid whose gauge transformations are linear in the parameters. We prove that this model is naturally equivalent to the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances through an intermediate total-form model, with explicit projection and section maps and simplicial homotopies. When nonempty, its connected components form a torsor for the degree-zero cohomology of an associated weighted gauge complex, and its higher homotopy groups are computed by the higher cohomology of this complex.

papers.title_en: Unconventional Mixed-Parity Magnetism in Rare-Earth Tetraborides
papers.abstract_en: Altermagnetism has advanced the study of compensated magnets by revealing non-relativistic spin splitting, traditionally classified into strictly even- or odd-parity spin textures. Here, we establish component-resolved mixed-parity spin splitting in a fully three-dimensional compensated magnet and identify its microscopic origin. Using first-principles calculations, tight-binding and $\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{p}$ models, along with spin-group symmetry analysis, we demonstrate that the non-coplanar ground state of $\mathrm{TbB}_4$ enforces odd-parity $p$- and $f$-wave-like textures for the in-plane spin components while the out-of-plane component retains an even-parity $d$-wave altermagnetic character. Crucially, the $p$-wave texture is driven not by relativistic spin-orbit coupling but by a staggered emergent flux arising from the scalar spin chirality of the non-coplanar order. This mixed-parity structure dictates distinct transport fingerprints, including bulk non-relativistic Edelstein and spin Hall responses that respond characteristically to reversal of the chirality domains. Spin-orbit coupling additionally enables a Berry curvature dipole. These results establish the rare-earth tetraborides as a robust platform for engineering complex spin-charge conversion phenomena.

papers.title_en: Entanglement asymmetry in the gapped XYZ spin-$\frac12$ chain
papers.abstract_en: The entanglement asymmetry measures how strongly a symmetry is broken inside a subsystem. Analytic results at equilibrium have so far covered free theories and, perturbatively, the critical XXZ chain. We compute the Rényi entanglement asymmetries of a large interval in the gapped, $U(1)$-breaking phase of the interacting XYZ chain. The calculation combines three ingredients. A charged-moment identity, which we prove for fermionic Gaussian and for injective matrix-product ground states, ties the asymmetry to the static susceptibility of the broken charge. A non-conservation sum rule then evaluates the susceptibility from sine-Gordon form factors, its two-kink and one-breather channels providing a lower bound on the universal amplitude. The Baxter--Johnson--Krinsky--McCoy solution supplies the kink mass for different couplings. Infinite-system density-matrix renormalization group simulations built on these masses reproduce the master formula.

papers.title_en: Transgression branes in seven dimensions
papers.abstract_en: A seven dimensional theory with branes, described by a Transgression Action is investigated. The theory has special properties owing to the factorization of the trace used to define the Transgression form. It is shown that in some cases the theory is similar to the models of branes proposed by Nepomechie, Wu and Zee as a higher dimensional generalization of models of particles with fractional statistics of Wilczek, Wu and Zee. Static Euclidean solutions are presented, and compared with similar solutions of Nepomechie,Wu and Zee. Then Lorentzian static solutions are considered, based in solutions of constant curvature black holes presented by Bañados and further studied by Guilleminot, Olea and Petrov. Topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics are discussed.

papers.title_en: The imprint of individual neutron star spins on ejecta, $r$-process nucleosynthesis, and kilonovae in binary neutron star mergers
papers.abstract_en: To leading order, the gravitational-wave (GW) signal from binary neutron stars depends on the individual spins, $χ_1$ and $χ_2$, only through the effective spin parameter $χ_{\rm eff}$. We present the first systematic investigation of individual-spin effects on ejecta, $r$-process nucleosynthesis, and kilonova emission, including comparisons at fixed total mass, mass ratio and $χ_{\rm eff}$. We use numerical relativity ejecta from three total mass regimes with the finite-temperature, composition-dependent SFHo equation of state and neutrino emission and absorption. For $M_{\rm tot}=2.55\,M_\odot$ at fixed $χ_{\rm eff}=0$, individual spins change the dynamical ejecta mass by a factor of ${\sim}45$, while the absolute $A\geq140$ yield spans more than two orders of magnitude and the lanthanide to light $r$-process mass ratio increases from ${\sim}2$ to ${\sim}70$. Prompt-collapse $4.10\,M_\odot$ models show heavy-element yield differences exceeding four orders of magnitude at $χ_{\rm eff}=0$. The kilonova retains the individual-spin imprint, with peak brightness differences reaching ${\sim}0.9$ mag. At $40\,{\rm Mpc}$, all three fixed $χ_{\rm eff}=0$ pairs remain above adopted depths at common epochs for all viewing angles, with same-epoch colour differences reaching ${\sim}1.5$ mag. The colour imprint persists when the simulation-derived secular ejecta are replaced by the same parametric disc outflow, indicating that disc mass differences are not the primary driver and that dynamical ejecta make an important contribution. Neutrino absorption systematically brightens the kilonova and shifts peak-associated colours blueward. These EM signatures can break the degeneracy between individual spins in the GW signal.

papers.title_en: Decomposition of disk and jet optical emission: Case of PKS~1510-089 and PKS~0736+017
papers.abstract_en: Measuring BLR size and black hole mass of jetted quasars with strong radio emission is challenging due to the contribution from non-thermal synchrotron radiation from the jet in the optical continuum. Here, we investigate the optical continuum emission in two flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs), PKS~0736+017 and PKS~1510-089, by separating the thermal emission from the accretion disk and the non-thermal synchrotron emission from the jet using their distinct polarization signatures. Our analysis combines multi-epoch optical spectro-photometric and polarimetric observations from the archival optical continuum, H$β$ emission line light curves from earlier reverberation mapping campaigns, and 37 GHz radio data. For PKS~0736+017, we find that the disk contributes approximately 70 % ($f_d = 0.70^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$) of the total optical emission. After removing the jet component, we obtain a revised H$β$ lag of $84.8^{+23.2}_{-18.4}$ days. In contrast, the disk contribution in PKS~1510-089 is lower with 37.5 % ($f_d = 0.37^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$), with a corresponding H$β$ lag of $54.4^{+4.4}_{-5.4}$ days. Our findings highlight the need for careful decomposition of optical light curves in jet-dominated AGN.

papers.title_en: The Quantum Noise Fraction and the addressable fraction in High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Detection
papers.abstract_en: The quantum noise fraction $β$, the share of a detector's noise power that is quantum in origin, sets a ceiling $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{max}} = 1/\sqrt{1-β}$ on the sensitivity improvement that removing quantum-origin noise can yield. In the kHz--GHz band the readout degree of freedom is a bosonic mode and $β= 1/(2\bar{n}_{\mathrm{th}}+1)$, with $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{th}}$ the Bose--Einstein occupation. Quantum noise then dominates only on the cold side of the thermal frontier $k_BT\ln 3 = \hbarω$ (above 229 MHz at 10 mK), which governs mechanical resonators and electromagnetic cavities alike; a real readout turns it into a joint condition on the occupation and on the excess noise of the readout chain. On a multimode acoustic antenna the frontier can be observed within one device, since the logarithmic slope of $\sqrt{S_hQ}$ along the odd-overtone comb increases by one half across it whatever the dependence of the quality factor on overtone number. On this antenna, crossing the frontier costs more in classical sensitivity than quantum enhancement returns. For a GHz mode of an existing bulk acoustic wave device at 10 mK, $β= 0.984$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{max}} = 7.8$. That ceiling cannot be reached with a linear readout, because with intrinsic damping the zero-point term is the force noise of the bath, fixed by the fluctuation--dissipation theorem. The addressable fraction $β_a$ excludes it: at the standard quantum limit the same mode has $β= 0.992$ but $β_a = 0.496$, an available improvement of 1.41 against a ceiling of 11.0. An array of $10^4$ such devices cross-correlated for one year reaches $3.6\times 10^{-24}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ for an integration bandwidth equal to the linewidth; even granting $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{max}} = 7.8$ in full, a factor $1.0\times 10^{10}$ above the big-bang-nucleosynthesis bound remains, and it is classical.

papers.title_en: Asymptotic evaluation of multidimensional oscillatory integrals
papers.abstract_en: Oscillatory integrals appear throughout physics, from diffraction and gravitational lensing to real-time path integrals. Their asymptotic evaluation is complicated by the need to determine which real and complex saddle points contribute, and how they are connected by Stokes phenomena. In multiple dimensions, this traditionally requires computing the steepest descent manifolds in a high-dimensional complex space. Here, we develop an algebraic alternative for integrals with polynomial and rational exponents. Using integration by parts and Brieskorn reduction, we construct a finite-dimensional Gauss-Manin system that generates the asymptotic expansions of all saddle points. Its Borel transform yields a Fuchsian system, whose monodromy determines the Stokes constants and hence the adjacency of the saddles. Combined with the recent South-East rule, this identifies the contributing saddles and enables superasymptotic and hyperasymptotic approximations without computing gradient flows. We demonstrate the method for the parabolic umbilic diffraction integral and a Lorentzian lens as examples, obtaining agreement to machine precision. The methods are implemented in an accompanying open-source Julia package \href{https://github.com/jfeldbrugge/IntegralResurgence.jl}{\texttt{IntegralResurgence.jl}}.

papers.title_en: Quantum Simulation of Detuning-Controlled Proximity-Induced Localization and Reentrant Delocalization in a Quasiperiodic Ladder
papers.abstract_en: Proximity effects, in which one subsystem imprints its properties onto another, offer a route to controlling quantum matter. For localization, this raises the question of whether an extended system can be localized by its neighbor, and then delocalized again, in the regime of weak quasiperiodic disorder. Here, we demonstrate this behavior in a coupled Aubry--André ladder, where a staggered detuning applied to only one leg localizes the neighboring, undetuned leg through inter-leg hybridization, even before the detuned leg itself localizes. Upon further increasing the detuning, the undetuned leg undergoes re-entrant delocalization, while the detuned leg remains localized. Finite-size scaling supports the persistence of these regimes in the thermodynamic limit. On an IBM Quantum processor, we experimentally observe their dynamical signatures: strongly suppressed wave-packet spreading in the proximity-localized regime and its recovery upon re-entrant delocalization. Our results establish leg-selective detuning as a reversible control knob for localization and transport in coupled quantum systems.

papers.title_en: Nucleating an Inflationary Universe: Euclidean Wormholes and their No-Boundary Limit
papers.abstract_en: No-boundary instantons and Euclidean "wineglass" wormholes have both been proposed as providing suitable initial conditions for the current expanding phase of our universe, and in particular for providing conditions that are favorable to an inflationary phase. These finite action solutions have generally been regarded as unrelated, and enacting different scenarios - in one case the creation of spacetime from nothing, and in the other up-tunneling from a Euclidean Anti-de Sitter vacuum. By studying explicit solutions of both axionic and magnetic wineglass wormholes, we find that in the zero-charge limit the throat of the wormholes pinches off, leaving a no-boundary instanton that disconnects from the asymptotic Anti-de Sitter region. Thus wormholes and no-boundary instantons are part of a common family of Euclidean solutions. Along the way, we resolve the long-known puzzle that the action of wineglass wormholes can become negative. Moreover, small-charge wormholes lead to a longer inflationary phase than large-charge solutions, while no-boundary instantons dominate the probability distribution overall.

papers.title_en: Constraints on Rastall gravity from current observational data
papers.abstract_en: We study the cosmological features of Rastall gravity, where the covariant energy-momentum conservation is modified to $\nabla_μT^μ_ν=λ\nabla_νR$ in curved spacetime. For this purpose, we obtain the modified field equations of Rastall model to linear order of perturbations, and then inspect the evolutionary behavior of cosmological observables, chiefly the matter power spectrum and the Hubble parameter, within the context of Rastall gravity. We also compare Rastall model with cosmological probes, namely cosmic microwave background, weak lensing, supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, and redshift-space distortions data. According to our numerical results, Rastall gravity prefers lower growth of structures compared to the $Λ$CDM model, which indicates consistency with low-redshift large-scale structure probes. Moreover, numerical analysis reveals that Rastall gravity with a cosmological constant as the dark energy component suffers from the Hubble tension, like the $Λ$CDM model.

papers.title_en: Intrinsic Zak Phase of Solitons: A Geometric Correspondence with the Center-of-Mass Position
papers.abstract_en: The center-of-mass position of a nonlinear soliton in a lattice is commonly attributed to the interplay between nonlinearity and lattice confinement. Here, we reveal its geometric origin by establishing an exact relation between the soliton position and an intrinsic Zak phase. Unlike the Zak phase of a linear Bloch band, this intrinsic Zak phase arises from the nonlinear self-consistent band of the lattice reconstructed by the soliton density. We construct a composite periodic function to define this phase and demonstrate that its topological winding during nonlinear Thouless pumping dictates the quantized soliton displacement. Our results establish band geometry as a fundamental descriptor of nonlinear soliton position in a lattice and provide a geometric framework for their topological transport.

papers.title_en: Scalar Vacuum Polarization in Loop Quantum Gravity Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: A quantum macroscopic ``Kruskal'' black hole solution that incorporates quantum geometry effects has been derived in \chg{loop quantum gravity} as the counterpart to the classical Schwarzschild solution with a distinct imprint outside the event horizon, even at scales much larger than the Planck length. This resulting black hole quantum geometry is supported by an effective energy density of quantum origin, outside the horizon, which prevents asymptotic flatness at large distances and confines massive particles to finite radii, thereby preventing their escape to infinity. In this work\chg{,} we adapt to these solutions the extended Anderson-Candelas-Christensen-DeWitt approach to compute the quantum vacuum polarization in order to provide an accurate measure of the quantum activity around these black holes. We carry out a numerical implementation of the formalism and present, to our knowledge for the first time, the scalar vacuum polarization $\langleφ^2\rangle$ exterior to this quantum-corrected geometry. We find that the quantum-gravity exponent $ε$ enhances the near-horizon polarization and induces, farther out, a small negative tail that we identify---through a parameter-free \chg{DeWitt-Schwinger} comparison---with the field's response to the nonzero curvature of the background (absent for Ricci-flat Schwarzschild). The correction scales linearly with $ε$, the parameter tracking the quantum gravitational corrections, so that\chg{,} for astrophysically realistic (i.e., tiny) $ε$, the result is numerically indistinguishable from Schwarzschild. The calculation furnishes a consistency check on the quantum activity around these solutions, the fluctuations tracking the local curvature without anomalous growth in the exterior.

papers.title_en: Hunting Dark Matter with the Einstein Telescope
papers.abstract_en: Too light primordial black holes evaporate and are therefore strongly constrained by various bounds, e.g. Cosmic Microwave Background distortion. However, if they are formed strongly clustered, the corresponding haloes may collapse into heavier black holes which may form the entirety of the dark matter of the universe. The indirect signal of such a scenario is the production of a flat stochastic background of gravitational waves which is detectable by the Einstein Telescope.

papers.title_en: Mach's principle in atomic transitions
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the atomic transition probabilities in atom-mirror set-ups that are in circular motion. In one scenario, the atom is in circular motion inside a static cylindrical mirror. In the other scenario, the cylindrical mirror rotates around its central axis while the atom remains static. We report structural similarity in the atomic transition probabilities between these two cases -- these probabilities are equivalent upon interchanging the field frequencies between the two scenarios. We interpret such an observation as a semi-classical phenomenon analogous to the classical Mach's principle.

papers.title_en: The generalized entropy in holographic semiclassical de Sitter spacetime
papers.abstract_en: We consider generalized de Sitter entropy which includes both entanglement entropy of the strongly coupled quantum field and the gravitational Wald entropy in the framework of holographic semiclassical gravity. The quantum corrected de Sitter spacetime is constructed perturbatively by considering static deformations of the classical solution. By applying the Noether charge formula to our semiclassical model, we show that both the renormalized entropies remain finite without introducing a cutoff, even when the bulk AdS gravitational field does not satisfy the Dirichlet boundary condition. We show that the first order variation of the generalized entropy with respect to the de Sitter horizon always vanishes when the conformal boundary metric is promoted to a dynamical variable.

papers.title_en: Quantum States Prepared by Wormholes: Long-Wavelength Deviations from Bunch-Davies
papers.abstract_en: Wineglass wormholes mediate the nucleation of baby universes out of an asymptotically Anti-de Sitter or flat spacetime. Upon materialization, the new universe naturally undergoes an inflationary phase. Here we study the quantum state of tensor and probe scalar field fluctuations that these wormhole geometries prepare, finding that they reproduce the Bunch-Davies vacuum for short-wavelength modes but lead to deviations from Bunch-Davies on large scales. These deviations, which depend on the charge of the wormhole, cause a small shift as well as oscillations in the angular power spectrum generated by an ensuing inflationary phase, and thus provide a distinctive cosmological observable. The wormholes are supported by either axionic or magnetic charges. In the limit of vanishing charge, they undergo a topological transition after which they contain no-boundary instantons. We find that the small-charge limit suppresses deviations from the Bunch-Davies state for both scalar and tensor fluctuations, indicating that the topological transition is smooth.

papers.title_en: Magnon bandstructure and topology in a periodically deformed Kagome lattice with DM interaction
papers.abstract_en: We study the band structure and topology of magnons for a Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction on a deformed Kagome lattice. For simplicity, we focus on a periodically deformed lattice with hexagonal symmetry and an enlarged unit cell. This enlarged unit cell gives rise to a more complex band structure than in the undeformed case. Analyzing band topology, there is a distinction between the topologically trivial case with anti-ferromagnetic coupling and the topologically non-trivial case with ferromagnetic coupling. In the anti-ferromagnetic case, a spin-space symmetry, also present in the classical ground state, enforces these topologically trivial states. In the ferromagnetic case, this symmetry is spontaneously broken by the classical ground state. Consequently, the band structure also hosts numerous topological features. Specifically, we observe many topological transitions and bands with Chern numbers ranging from $+2$ to $-2$, which makes the system richer than in the undeformed case. This emergent topological structure demonstrates that deformed magnets can host new and exciting physics.

papers.title_en: A Matrix View of Holographic Null-State Equations in $d\geq 2$
papers.abstract_en: We show that the null-state-type partial differential equations recently derived from AdS gravity with a black hole can be efficiently organized using finite-dimensional matrices with systematic off-diagonal structures. This matrix formulation generates an infinite tower of CFT differential equations at arbitrary levels. The $d=2$ matrix reproduces a known result based on Virasoro null-state vectors at large central charge and admits an algebraic representation in terms of a linear combination of the identity matrix and $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ generators, with a heavy-state deformation encoding the central charge contribution. The $d=4$ governing matrix exhibits a similar yet richer structure involving products of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ generators. We also discuss recursion relations and factorized product structures associated with these holographic differential equations.

papers.title_en: KiDS-1000 cosmic shear reanalysis using MetaCalibration
papers.abstract_en: A number of cosmic shear studies have reported results that are in mild tension with the Planck cosmic microwave measurement. To explore if this can be caused by biases in the shear estimation, we revisit the analysis of data from the Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS) using an alternative shape measurement pipeline that is more robust to uncertainties in the calibration. To this end, we present an implementation of MetaCalibration, and compare its performance to that of lensfit, which has been used in previous analyses of these data. We find that the multiplicative bias is reduced, especially for the most distant redshifts, as derived from multi-band image simulations designed to match the KiDS data (SURFS-based KiDS-Legacy-Like Simulations: SKiLLS). For all tomographic bins we obtain a multiplicative bias $|m|<0.017$, with negligible additive bias. Importantly, the calibration has a negligible sensitivity to key galaxy properties. The resulting robust shear estimates were used to obtain cosmological parameter constraints. We find that the parameter $S_8\equiv σ_8 \sqrt{Ω_\mathrm{m}/0.3} =0.789_{-0.024}^{+0.020}$ is consistent with the previous KiDS-1000 lensfit constraint of $S_8=0.776^{+0.029 +0.002}_{-0.027-0.003}$ (statistical + systematic errors). Thanks to the higher effective source density, the constraining power is improved by about 28%. The difference in $S_8$ with the Planck value remains at a similar level, 1.8$σ$, implying that it is not caused by the shear measurements.

papers.title_en: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
papers.abstract_en: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.

papers.title_en: Targeting the future of spectroscopic galaxy surveys -- A cosmological study case with the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
papers.abstract_en: The next generation of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys are designed to measure hundreds of millions of galaxy and quasar spectra, extending precision large-scale-structure cosmology to redshifts and volumes well beyond the reach of current Stage-IV facilities. Realising this potential requires revisiting the target selection strategies and designing them explicitly around the depth, multiplexing, and survey time of the new instruments, rather than a direct extrapolation of existing recipes. This work develops and characterises new strategies for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST), a proposed 12-metre, highly multiplexed facility expected to operate in the 2040s. Using deep multi-band photometry, including COSMOS-field data from CLAUDS and HSC, we revisit low-redshift $z<1.6$ tracer selection of SDSS, BOSS/eBOSS, DESI and 4MOST-CRS -- Bright Galaxies, Luminous Red Galaxies, Emission Line Galaxies and quasars -- to photometric depth achievable in the WST era, and introduce a purely magnitude-limited sample (MagMax) exploiting three-dimensional colour-colour star-galaxy separation, and a set of Lyman-Break Galaxy dropout samples extending target selection to $z>2$. Using Fisher-matrix forecasts, we showcase the constraining power of a WST-like cosmological survey on BAO distance parameters $α_\parallel$ and $α_\perp$, the growth rate $f$, the evolving dark energy equation $w_0w_a$, the local-type primordial non-Gaussianity $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc}$, and the sum of the neutrino mass $Σm_ν$. The main outcome of this work is an optimisation framework that directly links instrumental capabilities and observing time to cosmological constraining power, providing a science-driven template applicable to the design of future generations of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys.

papers.title_en: Differentiable Inverse Design of Two-Body Interactions for the Moore-Read State
papers.abstract_en: Designing interactions that stabilize target quantum states is a central challenge in strongly correlated physics. For fractional quantum Hall states, identifying suitable two-body interactions remains difficult even when a target wave function is known. Here we implement a differentiable inverse-design approach that combines automatic differentiation with exact diagonalization to optimize two-body interactions, using the Moore--Read Pfaffian state as a benchmark. The optimized ground states achieve overlaps exceeding 99\% with the target for systems containing up to 12 electrons. Excitation and entanglement spectra provide complementary finite-size diagnostics. A common exponential pseudopotential profile retains an overlap of 91.1\% at 14 electrons without further optimization, supporting its transferability beyond the optimization sizes. These results demonstrate the approach on a non-Abelian quantum Hall benchmark and motivate its application to other numerically accessible trial states for which suitable approximate parent Hamiltonians remain unknown.

papers.title_en: High resolution Lyman-α forest constraints on dark matter-neutrino scattering
papers.abstract_en: We present new constraints on models of dark matter interacting with neutrino, based on high-resolution Lyman-$α$ forest data. We perform a suite of full hydrodynamical simulations of these models, spanning a range of interaction strengths and thermal histories. We train an emulator on the simulation results. A Monte Carlo Markov Chain analysis yields an upper limit on the interaction strength of $u_{νχ} \leq1.5\times10^{-8}$ (95% C.L.), which is the strongest direct bound to date on such interactions. Our results exclude previous hints of non-zero interactions presented in the literature. We furthermore compare our results to those obtained by mapping warm dark matter constraints to other models with suppressed small-scale structure, and find that these methods would overestimate the constraining power for this model.

papers.title_en: Love at First Loop: Quantum Deformability of Near-Extremal Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: The static Love numbers of black holes vanish in classical, four-dimensional, asymptotically flat General Relativity. We study how this changes for the response of near-extremal Reissner--Nordström black holes to a minimally coupled massless scalar, at energies where the Schwarzian mode of the near-horizon throat fluctuates strongly. The black hole then responds as a quantum system with a spectrum of states. Its static response is a polarizability, given by virtual transitions between them. For $\ell=0$ the static Love number vanishes, by the shift symmetry of the scalar, but for multipoles $\ell\geq1$ the static Love numbers are nonzero: the finite rotational energy of the spin-$\ell$ intermediate states spoils the cancellation responsible for the classical result. Since the throat no longer has a classical geometry from which to read off a tidal response, we define it through the retarded Green's function, and compute its full frequency dependence at leading order in $r_+ω$. Its conservative part requires renormalization: the near-horizon theory fixes the coefficient of its logarithm, and with it a dependence on the energy that no local term can remove, while its finite local terms are matching data of the four-dimensional theory. The dissipative part is finite and scheme independent. For $\ell\geq1$, it vanishes at low frequencies when the energy is below the rotational gap, while at the gap threshold it becomes non-analytic in frequency and produces a late-time $t^{-3/2}$ tail.

papers.title_en: Cluster Condensation and Symmetry-Protected Thermal Rigidity of Bose gases on the Haldane Sphere
papers.abstract_en: We show that a spinless Bose gas on a Haldane sphere with a small monopole charge \(q\) realizes, in the lowest Landau level (LLL), an exactly solvable SU(2)-protected cluster condensate: a Hafnian condensate of two-boson singlets for \(q=1\), analogous to resonating-valence-bond singlet coverings, and a four-boson singlet condensate for \(q=3/2\). Unlike topologically protected quantum Hall states, the exactness of these states relies only on SU(2) symmetry and repulsiveness, with no pseudopotential fine-tuning. Their SU(2)-protected degeneracy renders the single-particle correlations exactly temperature-independent even as the clusters dissociate, a thermal rigidity absent in conventional Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs). Increasing the interaction drives a transition to a vortex BEC with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry.

papers.title_en: Quantized pumping of boundary Hilbert space in chiral Floquet phases
papers.abstract_en: Chiral Floquet phases support quantized chiral flow along their boundaries even when the bulk is fully localized. In this Letter, we establish a complementary phenomenon, which we call Hilbert-space pumping: under a boundary condition twisted by time translation, a part of the boundary Hilbert space, of quantized dimension, is transferred between the opposite boundaries. The twist is the temporal analogue of Laughlin's flux insertion in the quantum Hall effect. For noninteracting fermions, the number of transferred boundary modes is determined by the winding number, as we show analytically for the boundary dynamics and numerically for the anomalous Floquet Anderson insulator. For interacting systems whose boundary dynamics is a quantum cellular automaton, the transferred dimension is set by the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index: the twisted boundary Floquet operator is the Floquet operator on a tilted time slice, whose Hilbert-space dimension is multiplied by the index for each period of twist. We derive this relation for matrix product unitaries and test it numerically in random unitary circuits. Applied to the matrix product operators of non-invertible symmetries, the same twisted rank returns the quantum dimension of the symmetry operator in addition to its flow index.

papers.title_en: Sub-sonic compressible magnetohydrodynamic turbulence I. Alfvénic and fast-magnetosonic injection, amplitude dependence, and compressibility effects
papers.abstract_en: We investigate how sub-sonic compressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence properties that are relevant for cosmic-ray (CR) transport in the Galaxy are affected by the nature and amplitude of initial fluctuations, and by the plasma compressibility $β$. We perform 3D simulations of decaying compressible ideal-MHD turbulence at $1024^3$ resolution with the PLUTO code. The level of density fluctuations in fully developed turbulence is insensitive to whether this state is reached starting from Alfvénic or fast-magnetosonic perturbations. Fast-magnetosonic injection is characterized by an early phase of rapid shock dissipation, followed by a turbulence-dominated decay with a rate comparable to that of the Alfvénic case. The contribution of fast-magnetosonic fluctuations in fully developed turbulence remains relevant only when the initial injection consists exclusively of fast modes. Large-amplitude turbulence ($δB/B_0>1$) is characterized by a nearly isotropic Kolmogorov or Iroshnikov-Kraichnan spectrum for Alfvénic or fast-magnetosonic injection, respectively. At low amplitudes ($δB/B_0\ll1$), both initial Alfvénic and mixed-wave perturbations lead to strongly anisotropic turbulence with spectra $\propto k_\perp^{-5/3}$ and $\propto k_z^{-2}$ (becoming steeper at $β\gg1$), whereas fast-magnetosonic perturbations produce a turbulent state populated by shocks with a nearly isotropic $k^{-2}$ spectrum. Magnetic-field curvature and mirror structures are strongly sensitive to fluctuation amplitude and plasma $β$. The predicted -2.5 power-law scaling emerges only in the large-amplitude regime at high $β$. This work highlights that features of sub-sonic compressible MHD turbulence that may affect CR transport are sensitive to large-scale conditions and to the plasma $β$. Their effect on CR diffusion and field-line random walk is the object of Paper II.

papers.title_en: X-ray Variability of Mrk 421 in 2025 January: A Ten-Day XPoSat XSPECT Campaign with Contemporaneous NICER Coverage
papers.abstract_en: We present an X-ray study of the high-synchrotron-peaked blazar Mrk 421 using ten days of XPoSat/XSPECT observations (2025 January 20-29; 202 ks) and contemporaneous NICER data. The 0.8-15 keV light curve has a fractional variability amplitude of 19.6 +/- 0.3 per cent, and Bayesian blocks resolve 26 flux states spanning a factor of 2.3. The best-constrained flare has a fast rise and a slow decay, with e-folding times of about 3 h and 30 h. For typical jet parameters, the X-ray-emitting electrons cool faster than this, suggesting that the decay traces a gradual weakening of their acceleration. The count-rate distribution is best described by two lognormal components, consistent with multiplicative variability. The power spectrum is a red-noise power law with a slope of about 1.7 over timescales of 25 min to 10 d, typical of blazars. XSPECT and NICER count rates are well correlated over eight matched epochs (r = 0.941). We fitted log-parabola models to day-resolved spectra from XSPECT, NICER and both jointly, and to flux-resolved XSPECT spectra. Both show spectral hardening with brightness. In the flux-resolved spectra, the photon index at 1 keV decreases from 2.24 in the faintest state to 1.96 in the brightest, and the synchrotron peak moves from about 0.66 to 1.06 keV, while the curvature ($β\approx 0.7$) shows no significant change. Power-law fits to Bayesian blocks show that bright blocks at the same rate can differ in photon index by up to $6.4σ$, so count rate alone does not fix the spectral state.

papers.title_en: Band Structure and topology of a periodically deformed Kitaev honeycomb model
papers.abstract_en: Motivated by the growing interest in spin liquids and topological phases, as well as the rise of deformation engineering, we study the combined effects of deformation and magnetic fields on the honeycomb Kitaev model. The Kitaev model, as one of the prototypical and exactly solvable spin liquid-hosting models, serves as a simple platform that demonstrates the rich physics one can expect at the intersection of deformation physics and quantum spin liquids. Our work builds on a simplified solution to the undeformed base model that we present. This simplified solution allows for a straightforward extension of our analysis to the deformed case. After incorporating periodic deformations into the Kitaev model (chosen for its similarity to moiré physics), we investigate the effects of a hexagonally symmetric deformation on the band structure. We find that deformation leads to a smaller Brillouin zone with new band gaps at the edges, indicating the potential for topological transitions. Finally, we introduce a magnetic field to break time-reversal symmetry and thereby allow for non-trivial topology. We find that, under specific parameter conditions, the magnetic field leads to multiple band-gap closings and openings. An investigation into topological properties reveals nontrivial Chern numbers and a plethora of topological transitions. The resulting nontrivial band topology may motivate future investigations of thermal Hall or related transverse responses, which are not calculated here. We also propose a bulk-measurement approach to the Chern numbers and a possible path to their physical realization. Most importantly, our results demonstrate the rich phenomenology that can arise from the interplay between deformation and spin-liquid physics.

papers.title_en: Pure Spinor Factorization of Belinski-Zakharov Solitons and Regular Gravitational Instantons
papers.abstract_en: We show that the Belinski-Zakharov soliton construction factorizes into signed Pfaffian tau-functions, revealing a pure-spinor description of the metric and its regularity conditions. We derive analytic restrictions on the integral rod data, prove uniqueness for the asymptotically flat balance problem at fixed rod structure and periods, and give a conditional criterion for global existence. Combining these results with exhaustive enumeration of the admissible data and rigorous existence certificates, we construct a catalogue of regular asymptotically flat solutions representing 356 rod-word classes through twelve turning points, and 52 isolated regular asymptotically locally flat solutions through eight turning points. Analytic positivity and smooth-completion results establish regularity beyond the finite numerical solve. Based on this catalogue, we investigate two organizations of the solution space: generalized rank-two root systems and compositions of simpler endpoint geometries. The endpoint composition rules reproduce exactly all retained asymptotically flat words through twelve turning points.

papers.title_en: Fast holographic inversion of superconducting domes
papers.abstract_en: A holographic superconductor whose scalar mass depends on the gauge field strength, $M(\Fsq)$, reproduces a superconducting dome for a suitable $M$, but recovering $M$ from a dome has taken days. We obtain the condition that fixes the critical temperature from two integrations, started at the horizon and at the boundary, and its derivative with respect to $M$ from the same two solutions, so training needs no finite differences and an inversion takes ten minutes to an hour. With this speed we study the interval between the horizon value of $\Fsq$ at the lowest doping and $\Fsq=0$, which no horizon reaches and at whose end the scalar mass $M(0)$ fixes the dimension of the dual operator. Holding $M(0)$ at several values, the pinned masses, and retraining the rest, we find reconstructions that share the minima of $M$ and agree wherever the horizons reach, apart from the deepest end, but differ on that interval. A rule that keeps the reconstruction with the simplest closed form recovers the scalar mass and the mass function of a dome generated from a quadratic $M$. On Gaussian and double-Gaussian domes and the measured phase diagrams of YBa$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{y}$ and 2M-WS$_{2}$ its choice rests on ties or narrow margins, and it recovers the scalar mass of only two of the four domes generated from the closed forms it keeps for them. The dome thus constrains $M$ where its horizons reach but not the scalar mass, which a second observable would have to fix.

papers.title_en: General Form Factors from String Amplitudes
papers.abstract_en: We extend the string-amplitude construction of single-insertion form factors to multiple operator insertions carrying independent off-shell momenta. By deforming the bulk closed-string punctures onto the open-string boundary, we establish a relation between stringy general form factors and scattering amplitudes. Using this relation, we evaluate the field-theory limit and find that the resulting form factors receive contributions from both separate operator insertions and local contact terms. Furthermore, we uncover several hidden structures of stringy general form factors at finite $α'$: $2$-splits and hidden zeros analogous to those of scattering amplitudes, bulk zeros specific to form factors, and a decoupling split unique to multiple insertions.

papers.title_en: Charge-Activated Birefringence and Shadow Mimicry around Reissner-Nordström Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: We discover that electric charge can activates birefringence for a neutral vector field coupled to the Einstein tensor around a Reissner-Nordström black hole. Changing the electric charge of an uncoupled black hole can mimic one parity's shadow radius of a coupled black hole. The coupling makes the two parity looks differently. It separates their shadow edges of two parities and produces a backward-scattered signal with reversed helicity. However changing the charge alone cannot reproduce both effects. They require both nonzero charge and coupling. At weak coupling, the leading correction is the same for both potential. Positive coupling raises the potential, reduces low-frequency absorption and decrease the average shadow radius. Negative coupling reverses these trends. The backward signal is nonzero, this is due to the difference between the complex scattering amplitudes of the two parities. It is entirely helicity reversed. For the uncoupled field, the shadows is the same for both parities and the backward intensity vanishes exactly at every charge. We can use the split edge and backward signal to distinguish the coupling from a change of charge alone. A comparison with observations still requires a mechanism that produces and detects this field.

papers.title_en: Universal Curve Counting in Calabi-Yau 4-folds
papers.abstract_en: Recently, Pardon introduced a universal curve counting framework, which allows him to show that curve counting on 3-folds is "generated" by local curves (in a precise sense). We implement this universal curve counting program for Calabi-Yau 4-folds, where a significant technical difficulty comes from the dependence of the virtual dimension on the genus, which leads to more complicated generators than just local curves. Our main techniques are combinations of deformation-theoretic and homotopy-theoretic methods with an adaptation of Pardon's generic transversality results, which allow us to establish a full set of (computable) generators for CY4 curve counting. As a result, we prove (a slight correction of) the Gromov-Witten/Pandharipande-Thomas correspondence with primary descendents for CY4-folds, formulated by Cao, Maulik, and Toda. From this, we additionally obtain integrality of Gopakumar-Vafa style invariants for CY4-folds, as conjectured by Klemm-Pandharipande.

papers.title_en: Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Ray Boosted Relic Neutrinos
papers.abstract_en: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) can boost relic neutrinos to high energies through Standard Model (SM) neutral-current interactions, providing an indirect probe of the cosmic neutrino background (C$ν$B). In this work, we perform a systematic study of the diffuse UHECR-boosted C$ν$B flux including elastic neutrino--nucleon scattering (ES), coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (COH), incoherent neutrino--nucleus scattering (INCOH), baryon-resonance production (RES), and deep inelastic scattering (DIS). For the UHECR flux, we use mixed-composition spectra obtained from the UHECR propagation code PriNCe and from the H3a and H4a implementations of the Hillas model, together with SFR, QSO, and GRB source evolution models. We find a clear hierarchy of scattering channels as a function of boosted neutrino energy. The coherent scattering dominates at low-energy neutrino flux for heavy nuclear components, while ES and INCOH become important once individual nucleons are resolved. The RES channel gives a non-negligible contribution in the high-energy region, and DIS appears only at the highest energies and is most visible for the H4a case. Using current IceCube and Pierre Auger Observatory data, we obtain upper limits on the C$ν$B overdensity. Our results show that reliable predictions of the UHECR-boosted C$ν$B signal require a combined treatment of the relevant SM scattering channels, UHECR composition, source evolution, and the neutrino mass spectrum.

papers.title_en: Kelvin-Wave Multiplication by Sound Emission
papers.abstract_en: Kelvin waves are bending excitations of a quantized vortex. We identify a subsonic decay channel in which one Kelvin quantum emits a phonon and splits into two lower-energy Kelvin quanta, reducing the Kelvin-wave energy while increasing the number of quanta. For sound wavelengths much longer than the Kelvin wavelengths, rotational symmetry fixes the leading shear contribution to the emission amplitude in terms of the released Kelvin energy. This contribution is odd in the phonon momentum along the vortex. Microscopic calculations support the relation. Coherently seeded Gross--Pitaevskii evolution in a reflecting cavity demonstrates phase-controlled Kelvin gain, with increased mean-square vortex displacement and reduced mean-square slope.

papers.title_en: Competing interaction driven broad magnetic entropy distribution in triangular net compounds \text{Ba$_3$RE(BO$_3$)$_3$}, RE= Dy and Ho
papers.abstract_en: Triangular magnetic lattices have attracted significant attention as a model platform for exploring frustrated magnetism and quantum spin liquids, particularly in rare-earth-based systems. These materials also hold considerable promise for cryogenic magnetic refrigeration. In this work, we investigate the magnetic and magnetocaloric properties of the rare-earth (RE) based compounds $\text{Ba}_3\text{RE}(\text{BO}_3)_3$ ($\text{RE} = \text{Dy}$ and $\text{Ho}$). Polycrystalline samples synthesized via a solid-state reaction method crystallize in a hexagonal structure with the space group $P6_3mc$, featuring triangular nets separated by approximately $8.8~\textÅ$ along the $c$-axis. Detailed magnetic investigation reveals a deviation from pure paramagnetic behavior at low temperatures ($T < 20\text{ K}$). This is further corroborated by isothermal magnetization measurements, which exhibit non-overlapping $M$ vs. $H/T$ plots and reduced magnetization moments, suggesting significant crystal electric field (CEF) splitting of localized $f$-states. For an applied magnetic field change of $70\text{ kOe}$, the maximum entropy change (Relative Cooling Power) reaches $4.2\text{ J kg}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$ ($204\text{ J kg}^{-1}$) and $7.3\text{ J kg}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$ ($230\text{ J kg}^{-1}$) for the Dy- and Ho-based compounds, respectively. Overall, the positive slopes of Arrott plots, the universal scaling behaviour of $ΔS_{\text{m}}/ΔS_{\text{m}}^{\text{max}}$ versus reduced temperature ($t$), and the field exponent $c$ of the RCP versus $H$ curves indicate a second-order nature of entropy distribution, making them promising candidates for magnetocalorics in the millikelvin range.

papers.title_en: Probing cosmic anisotropy with galaxy clusters and supernovae
papers.abstract_en: Using $Λ$CDM and Padé-(2,1) cosmography, we study directional variations in the Hubble constant, $H_0$, using galaxy clusters (GC) and Type Ia Supernovae (SNe), from the PantheonPlus compilation, employing the hemisphere decomposition method. Since there is a degeneracy between $H_0$ and absolute magnitude $M_B$ for SNe, Cepheid-host calibration is usually required to constrain $H_0$. To complement the Cepheid-host calibration in the SNe analysis, we use GC X-ray scaling relations as a complementary probe of anisotropy. We consider five redshift bins on the full SNe sample $[z_\mathrm{min}, 0.5]$ where $z_\mathrm{min}= \{0.015, 0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2\}$. Our results show that the combined GC sample is consistent with statistical isotropy and that there is a $\sim 2.5 σ$ anisotropy preference in the lowest-redshift bin in the SNe-only case. This preference weakens when low-redshift SNe are progressively removed. In the SNe$+$GC analysis, we find that any anisotropy preference is driven by how the $H_0-M_B$ and the $H_0-k$ (where $k$ is the normalization parameter in the GC scaling relation) degeneracies are treated.
