The low-redshift bin anisotropy preference in the SNe-only analysis persists in the SNe$+$GC case when Cepheid-host calibration is used while the results are consistent with statistical isotropy when $k$ is fixed. Overall, our results do not provide compelling evidence for a statistically significant anisotropy in the local expansion rate. Our findings highlight the importance of combining complementary cosmological probes and examining the dependence of anisotropy constraints on calibrations and parameter degeneracies when assessing claims of cosmic anisotropy.

papers.title_en: A Tribute to S. Deser: Conserved Quantities in Generic Gravity Theories
papers.abstract_en: I describe parts of my joint work with S. Deser [March 19, 1931 - April 21, 2023] which started when I was working as a post-doc at Brandeis University in 2001. Our work was mostly, but not exclusively, on conserved charges of higher curvature theories of gravity. I also describe some recent developments, such as expressing the conserved charges in terms of the linearized Riemann tensor; I expound upon the computations. I also reminisce about our interaction for over two decades that went beyond our scientific collaboration. The physics part of this review is intended for graduate students and researchers interested in extended theories of gravity, especially about the conserved quantities and perturbative techniques in these theories.

papers.title_en: Two Fast Radio Burst Candidates Detected in the RATAN-600 Blind Survey
papers.abstract_en: We report the detection of two single dispersed pulses with widths of about 6.7\,ms and 15.6\,ms and flux densities of about 0.8 and 1.7\,Jy. These were found in a blind survey of two circular regions (Dec$\;=+22^{\circ}$ and $+5^{\circ}$,RA: 0--24~h) at high radio frequencies \mbox{(4400--5000\,MHz)} using four 4-channel filter radiometers (central frequencies of 4475, 4625, 4775, and 4925\,MHz) spanning a total frequency bandwidth of 600\,MHz. The survey was carried out with the Western Sector antenna of the RATAN-600 radio telescope, which had an effective area of 1200\,m$^2$ in~2017--2025. The total area of the survey was about 1500~square degrees, and each pointing of the antenna lasted one year. We consider these to be two rare, high-frequency FRB events (MJD~58614.38257 and MJD~58659.62482), detected with estimated dispersion measures of $200\pm20$ and $266\pm10$\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$ at a final signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level of 8--9 after additional optimal filtration. After subtraction of the estimated dispersions within the Milky Way, we estimated redshifts of approximately 0.09 and 0.13, respectively, using the traditional equation: ${\rm DM}\,[{\rm pc~cm}^{-3}] = 1000\,z$ for the intergalactic medium. The estimated isotropic energies of the FRBs are equal to $10^{40}$\,erg and $2\times 10^{40}$\,erg, respectively. To effectively detect single pulses, we applied machine learning methods using a neural network trained on synthetic FRB pulse profiles.

papers.title_en: Constraints on the number of inner horizons from gravitational Noether charges
papers.abstract_en: A central question in the study of black hole interiors is how matter and geometry constrain the number of horizons. In Einstein gravity, one known method is to use the ADM decomposition of the field equations to derive a differential inequality for the lapse, which then constrains the possible existence of multiple inner horizons. We show that the same obstruction can instead be formulated through the Komar integral as a bulk-boundary balance of gravitational Noether charge. In higher-curvature gravity, a direct ADM analysis becomes more complicated, whereas the gravitational Noether charge naturally retains this bulk-boundary structure. We naturally apply the gravitational Noether charge analysis to Lovelock gravity. We introduce a TCC-like curvature condition and prove that, together with the thermodynamically motivated assumption of positive Wald entropy, it allows at most one nondegenerate inner Killing horizon inside a nondegenerate event horizon. This suggests that the obstruction reflects a compatibility between bulk gravitational response and horizon thermodynamics.

papers.title_en: Gravitational Dark Matter Production in Einstein-Cartan Theory
papers.abstract_en: Introducing torsion into General Relativity leads to new four-point interactions for fermions. These are universal and must also affect any fermion dark matter. We improve existing calculations of dark matter production through the Einstein-Cartan theory four-fermion interaction by also considering the s-channel graviton exchange as another contributing process. The effect on both the total cross section as well as the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation collision term is calculated and discussed. We also introduce the Holst term, which generally modifies the four-fermion interaction coupling constant as well as introduces two new four-fermion interactions, and discuss and compute its effect on the total produced dark matter abundance.

papers.title_en: Hidden by Exponential Screening: The Invisibility of the Dymnikova Black Hole de Sitter Core to Accretion Observables
papers.abstract_en: The Dymnikova spacetime replaces the Schwarzschild singularity with a de Sitter core, and its lapse deviates from Schwarzschild by a factor decaying as $e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2M)}$. Whether this screening renders the core invisible to accretion has remained an open quantitative question. We address it with GRHD simulations of BHL accretion onto Dymnikova BH for six values of the critical length, $0.1M\le l_{\rm cr}\le 1.1M$, the last being 97% of the extremal value. All runs share identical gas parameters and resolution, so any difference in the flow must originate from the geometry. The dynamically relevant quantity is the gravitational acceleration, whose deviation reaches 12% at the inner boundary for the most strongly corrected model, yet the flow responds only locally: the post-shock density drops by 10% in the innermost zone and the quiet-phase accretion rate by 0.12%, with no effect beyond $r\simeq2.7M$. Because runs differing by as little as $\sim 10^{-10}$ in the metric decorrelate completely once the shock-cone instability saturates, we compare models statistically using ensembles of independent realizations. The time-averaged accretion rate is then independent of $l_{\rm cr}$ to within 0.8% $(2σ)$ at all radii; the variability amplitude, shock-cone opening angle $(1.077\pm0.003 rad)$, and stagnation radius $(26.8\pm0.3M)$ vary only within the realization scatter; the propagation lags $(75.5\pm1.0M$ and $31.6\pm0.4M)$ agree to within 1.6%; and no power spectrum carries a detectable core signature. Accretion onto a Dymnikova BH is therefore observationally indistinguishable from accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole: timing observations test the shock-cone mechanism, not the regular core. More broadly, ensemble-based statistical comparisons are essential before differences between simulated accretion flows in different spacetimes can be interpreted as physical.

papers.title_en: BCS superconductivity in the presence of wave dark matter
papers.abstract_en: As particle physics and condensed matter physics continue to expand their boundaries, emerging intersections between the two fields suggest well-motivated frontiers for physics models. In particular, dark matter, which is cosmologically predicted to form the background to our ordinary matter, can affect the physics of materials in a fundamental sense. In this work, we investigate the scenario in which relic ultralight wave dark matter alters the superconductor Hamiltonian via a sinusoidal source term. The Yukawa interaction with the scalar dark matter changes the effective electron mass, inducing periodic perturbations of macroscopic observables such as the superconducting order parameter, whose size could be important in future experiments. We provide here the actual calculations for this scenario on the superconducting resonators, calculating the modulation size depending on the dark matter parameters.

papers.title_en: Mass and angular momentum assessement of the neutron star XTEJ 1807-294 using X-ray triplets
papers.abstract_en: The X-ray power-density spectrum of the accreting millisecond pulsar XTEJ 1807-294 contains several triplets of simultaneously observed quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs): a lower and a upper kHz QPOs and a low-frequency QPO. This fact allows us to assess the mass and the specific angular momentum of the central neutron star. We also apply an error propagation formula to obtain interval estimates of the parameters of the star. The calculations are repeated with several different models for the kHz QPOs. The degree of consistency of the bounds obtained with the different triplets may provide information for the viability of the used models.

papers.title_en: First law of thermodynamics for interacting charged black holes and applications
papers.abstract_en: We derive a mass variation identity expressing the first law of black hole thermodynamics for asymptotically flat, stationary, axisymmetric Einstein-Maxwell solutions with multiple electrically charged horizons and finite conical axis singularities. Under the stated asymptotic and parameter regularity hypotheses, the identity holds for independent variations of all parameters within families of fixed horizon types. On the all-degenerate family, a correction to the ADM mass defines a scalar function whose derivatives with respect to angular momenta are the horizon angular velocities. At the Majumdar-Papapetrou family, its angular momentum Hessian is positive definite. Combining the first variation identity with a separate theorem on the sign of the conical parameters shows that this Hessian is nondecreasing in the positive-semidefinite order along admissible paths of increasing Weyl gaps at fixed positive charges.

papers.title_en: Cloudy black-hole configurations of the composed Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory: Analytic treatment
papers.abstract_en: Non-Abelian black holes that violate the non-hair conjecture are known to exist in the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory. The onset of hair formation in this composed physical system is marked by the presence of `cloudy' black-hole spacetimes, magnetically charged Reissner-Nordström black holes that support spatially regular linearized field configurations. In the present paper we explore, using {\it analytical} techniques, the physical and mathematical properties of the composed black-hole-linearized-field bound-state configurations of the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs theory. In particular, we derive a remarkably compact analytical formula for the discrete resonance spectrum $\{μ_k\}^{k=\infty}_{k=1}$ of the dimensionless mass-radius parameter $μ\equiv m_{\text{w}} r_+$ that characterizes the cloudy black-hole-field configurations in the regime $1\ll r_+\ll m^{-1}_{\text{w}}$ of small-mass weakly-magnetized black holes (here $r_+$ is the horizon radius of the central supporting black hole and $m_{\text{w}}$ is the mass of the Yang-Mills field due to the Higgs effect). Interestingly, our results reveal that the excited black-hole-field resonances are characterized by the asymptotic $k$-independent dimensionless ratio ${μ_{k+1}/{μ_{k}}}=e^{-{{2π}/{\sqrt{3}}}}$.

papers.title_en: No smooth real instanton saddles in self-dual Yang-Mills on AdS$_4$
papers.abstract_en: In the self-dual limit of Yang-Mills theory on Euclidean AdS$_4$ studied by Heuveline, Ruzziconi, Sheta and Strominger, the boundary condition of the second-order action becomes vacuous, but the boundary equation of the first-order action is non-trivial. We show that, with this equation, the vacuum is the only saddle with a real gauge field when both fields are smooth up to the conformal boundary, for any compact gauge group. In particular, the self-dual solutions of Sarioglu and Tekin (2009) are not saddles; we also correct their charges, which omitted a surface term at the conformal boundary. Complex saddles and singular limits remain open.

papers.title_en: Self-lensing of electromagnetic counterparts to extreme mass ratio inspirals
papers.abstract_en: Extreme mass ratio inspirals on inclined orbits can produce recurrent electromagnetic flares by shocking gas at accretion-disk crossings. Using forward ray tracing in Kerr spacetime, we investigate how self-lensing by the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) reshapes these flares. Flares emitted behind the SMBH can be strongly magnified, whereas near-side flares remain almost unmagnified, producing strong-weak alternation even for identical intrinsic emission. As Lense-Thirring precession shifts the crossing azimuths, it generates long-term amplitude envelopes whose spacing can be used to infer the precession period. Lense-Thirring precession can also increase the cumulative geometric lensing probability over longer observing windows. Within individual flares, Keplerian motion of hotspots co-rotating with the disk produces time-dependent magnification, which can generate shoulders or double peaks and change the effective width. We also propose a spectral diagnostic to distinguish self-lensing from external lensing when their light curves are similar: self-lensing can amplify later, cooler emission and produce a softer secondary peak, whereas delayed images from a static external lens repeat the same intrinsic spectral evolution.

papers.title_en: Effective Optical Geometry and Holographic Phase Structure of a Magnetic AdS Black Hole
papers.abstract_en: We study circular null orbits, thermodynamic topology, and the holographic thermodynamic description of a four-dimensional magnetically charged AdS black hole in nonlinear electrodynamics. The background orbit structure is classified using Duan s phi-mapping construction and compared with the extraordinary electromagnetic characteristics. The latter defines an effective optical metric with an additional radial factor that modifies the orbit condition and introduces explicit dependence on the AdS radius. For four representative configurations, the local indices of the five isolated orbits are unchanged while their radii shift by up to 5.187 %. The background mass thresholds vary smoothly across sigma = 1/4 when the total mass is used, whereas the fixed-m0 parametrization is singular there. Regularity at the center requires sigma > 1 and m0 = 0. The thermodynamic analysis separates local stability indices from equilibrium coexistence: stable Gibbs-free-energy branches cross only in model-dependent parameter intervals. The boundary canonical ensemble exhibits critical behavior consistent with mean-field exponents, and the examined grand-canonical ensemble has a Hawking-Page crossing. In the mixed ensemble, the free-energy branches have a finite endpoint discontinuity, but the sampled competing states do not satisfy the full local-stability criterion

papers.title_en: Raising the Optical Depth to Reionization with Dark Matter Decay
papers.abstract_en: DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements have sharpened a discrepancy with cosmic microwave background (CMB) inferences that can be recast as a preference for $τ_{\rm reio}\simeq0.09$, above the $\simeq0.06$ inferred from large-scale CMB polarization. We test whether electromagnetic energy injection from dark matter (DM) decaying through $χ\to e^+e^-$ can supply this additional optical depth. Adopting an asymmetric, simulation-calibrated Gompertzian model for astrophysical reionization, we derive $τ_{\rm reio}$ self-consistently from the free-electron history including DM decay. We jointly constrain cosmological and reionization parameters and the decay rate using ACT+Planck CMB temperature and polarization anisotropies, CMB lensing, BAO, and quasar damping-wing observations. For $m_χ=1$ GeV, DM decay raises the marginalized mean optical depth from 0.064 to 0.072 under a flat decay-rate prior, without significantly improving the fit. Reweighting the chains with log-uniform priors lowers the mean optical depth, indicating prior dependence. The additional optical depth arises primarily from a broad ionization tail through the cosmic dark ages, rather than an earlier onset of astrophysical reionization. For DM masses from 2 MeV to 7 GeV, the 68% credible intervals remain below $τ_{\rm reio}\simeq0.08$, a benchmark previously found sufficient to bring both the neutrino-mass tension and the exclusion of $Λ$CDM below $2σ$. The DM lifetime constraints complement photon, cosmic-ray, and gas-heating bounds and are competitive with previous CMB limits. DM decay therefore shifts the inferred optical depth upward, but the posterior-favored increase remains insufficient to substantially alleviate the CMB--BAO discrepancy.

papers.title_en: Recovering Missing Degrees of Freedom in Simulation-Trained Field-Level Generative Models
papers.abstract_en: Simulation-trained generative models are emerging as a powerful framework for field-level inference in cosmology, particularly in strongly nonlinear regimes where analytical approaches become intractable. However, the finite size of training datasets often leads to variance shrinkage, indicating that part of the realization-level variability of the underlying physical process is not captured by the learned generative dynamics. In this Letter, we interpret variance shrinkage as a diagnostic of missing effective degrees of freedom and introduce physics-informed latent modifications to the generative dynamics of a continuous normalizing flow. We show that these latent corrections recover a substantial fraction of the missing variability without requiring additional training simulations. Using weak-lensing field-level inference as a representative cosmological application, we further demonstrate through posterior analysis that the learned latent directions are actively exploited during inference and behave as effective nuisance parameters that absorb part of the mismatch between the training and target distributions. As a result, the model exhibits improved robustness to out-of-distribution shifts in field-level inference. Our work establishes variance shrinkage as a practical diagnostic for identifying missing degrees of freedom in simulation-trained generative models and provides a framework for recovering them through physics-informed modifications of generative dynamics.

papers.title_en: Cosmogenic photon fluxes at ultra-high energies
papers.abstract_en: During their propagation, ultra-high energy cosmic rays produce cosmogenic photons. The expected flux level of these photons may vary by orders of magnitude depending on parameters such as the spectrum and composition of cosmic rays at injection or the source distance. We investigate the photon yields for various assumptions on injection parameters. The photon yield is largest for proton-emitting sources at about 15 Mpc distance for cosmogenic photons above $10^{18}$ eV. While the photon yield from protons always exceeds the one from heavier nuclei of the same total energy, the differences are reduced for larger source distances. Then, we quantify the cosmogenic photon fluxes for different source scenarios. We regard mixed-composition scenarios that were found to provide a reasonable description of the data from the Pierre Auger Observatory. In addition, benchmark scenarios leading to comparably high (``maximum'') or low (``minimum'') photon fluxes are determined assuming pure proton or pure iron primaries. For the mixed-composition scenarios that do not contain initial protons, the predicted cosmogenic photon fluxes are below present experimental limits by more than 1.5 orders of magnitude. In case of a substantial fraction of protons at the highest energies, the related photon flux might be in reach. Certain parameter combinations of pure proton scenarios are constrained already by present photon limits.

papers.title_en: Non-invertible symmetries and mixed anomalies from equations of motion in (3+1)D twisted $BF$ topological quantum field theories
papers.abstract_en: We develop a systematic study on the topological operators that generate invertible and non-invertible higher-form symmetries in $\left(3+1\right)D$ twisted $BF$ topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). We focus on the twisted $BF$ theories with gauge group $G=\prod_i \mathbb{Z}_{N_i}$ and an $a\wedge a\wedge b$ twist, where $a$'s and $b$ are 1-form and 2-form gauge fields, respectively. These theories realize non-Abelian $(3+1)$D TQFTs supporting Borromean-Rings braiding and describe three-dimensional non-Abelian topological orders in condensed matter. For $G=(\mathbb{Z}_2)^3$, a microscopic realization is given by the $\mathbb{D}_4$ Kitaev quantum double model. Starting from the equations of motion (EoMs), we construct gauge invariant operators that are supported on closed submanifolds, hence are genuine topological operators. Some of them are associated with nontrivial Hilbert spaces which are the projective representation spaces of specific gauge subgroups, thus being non-invertible. The others are invertible topological operators with group-like fusion rules. The fusion rules of non-invertible topological operators correspond to the decomposition of the product of the projective representation spaces. We provide a field-theoretical algorithm to calculate the fusion rules. Besides, we identify an obstruction to retaining a non-invertible topological operator after gauging an invertible symmetry, and derive the constraints on pairs of non-invertible operators relevant to simultaneous gauging. Our results give a unified and practical approach for identifying and characterizing higher-form symmetries and mixed anomalies, which can be extended to more general TQFTs and topological orders.

papers.title_en: Long-range model for electronic pseudospin-nuclear-spin coupling and two-stage ordering in TmVO$_4$
papers.abstract_en: We study an infinite-range coupled electronic-pseudospin and nuclear-spin model for ferroquadrupolar and nuclear-spin ordering in TmVO$_4$ in external magnetic and strain fields. This material is an experimental realization of a transverse-field Ising model, where the Ising degree of freedom is quadrupolar and non-magnetic, but a transverse component is magnetic and couples both to external magnetic fields and to the nuclear spins via a hyperfine coupling. At zero external magnetic field, the electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom undergo well-separated two-stage ordering, accompanied by the release of their respective entropies. A transverse magnetic field polarizes the electronic orbital moments and, via the hyperfine coupling, the nuclear spins. The quadrupolar ordering temperature is gradually reduced to zero. However, the nuclear transition is replaced by a crossover at nonzero magnetic field. Quantum fluctuations are enhanced near the phase transitions and lead to peaks in the magnetic susceptibility. The spectral functions reveal a softening of a low-energy mode near the quantum critical point, consistent with the closing of the excitation gap and its reopening in the disordered phase. These features provide direct dynamical signatures of the field-driven quantum critical phenomena.

papers.title_en: Quantum 6j-symbols arising from a subfactor of finite index and finite depth and the zipper condition for 4-tensors in two-dimensional topological order
papers.abstract_en: We study 3-tensors satisfying the ``zipper condition,'' which play an important role in tensor network approaches to two-dimensional topological order. In our previous work, we identified the 4-tensors appearing in these approaches with bi-unitary connections in the Jones theory of subfactors in operator algebras. These bi-unitary connections give rise to subfactors of finite index. We prove that, when the associated subfactor has finite depth, the 3-tensors satisfying the zipper condition correspond precisely to the quantum $6j$-symbols, also known as $F$-symbols, of the unitary multi-fusion category arising from the subfactor. This realization of quantum $6j$-symbols differs from their realization through a flat bi-unitary connection arising from the higher relative commutants of a subfactor.

papers.title_en: The Stellar-Mass Dependence of Feedback-Driven Outflows in DESI DR1 Star-Forming Galaxies
papers.abstract_en: Stellar feedback plays a key role in regulating star formation and shaping the evolution of star-forming galaxies. Low-mass galaxies provide one of the most powerful laboratories for testing stellar feedback and its impact on galaxy evolution. Numerical simulations predict that repeated feedback-driven gas inflows and outflows generate a "breathing mode," producing a positive correlation between mass-normalized gas velocity dispersion and recent star formation in dwarf galaxies. Whether this kinematic signature persists at higher stellar masses has remained untested. We investigate this question using $\sim1200$ star-forming galaxies with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectroscopy and COSMOS2020 photometry spanning $7.9<\log M_\star/M_\odot<11.5$ within $z<0.25$. Ionized-gas kinematics are measured with pPXF, and recent star formation histories are reconstructed through joint spectrophotometric fitting with Prospector. We confirm the predicted positive correlation throughout the low-mass regime with $\log M_\star/M_\odot \lesssim 9.8$, quantitatively consistent with previous observations and FIRE-2 simulations. Above $\log M_\star/M_\odot \sim 9.8$, the correlation weakens rapidly and becomes consistent with zero, providing the first empirical constraint on the stellar mass scale above which the kinematic signature of feedback-driven outflow cycles becomes negligible. Our results establish a characteristic stellar mass above which stellar feedback no longer dominates galaxy-scale gas kinematics, providing a new observational benchmark for models of feedback-regulated galaxy evolution. Future joint analyses of gas kinematics and stellar structure will test whether this transition is accompanied by the broader galaxy response predicted by the breathing mode scenario.

papers.title_en: A simple flux criterion for trapped surface formation by short pulses of gravitational radiation and matter
papers.abstract_en: We discuss the formation of trapped surfaces induced by short pulses of incoming gravitational radiation and matter fields, in a double-null formulation. We identify a hierarchy of orders in the pulse width for the geometric and matter quantities consistent with the evolution equations. Under the assumption that this hierarchy holds throughout the region considered, the incoming fluxes undergo approximately conservative inward transport and are thereby amplified. The Raychaudhuri equation then gives an initial flux criterion for trapped surface formation. The conditions on the matter are expressed through the Ricci components and their derivatives, which allows the argument to be developed without specifying a particular matter model.

papers.title_en: Thermal Festina Lente
papers.abstract_en: According to the Festina Lente bound, particles charged under a $U(1)$ gauge field cannot be too light. Otherwise, the largest charged black holes of de Sitter space would discharge in a way that leads to a crunching singularity in violation of cosmic censorship. The Festina Lente bound has previously been extended to also include a background of thermal radiation, but where vacuum energy still dominates cosmic evolution, which imposes a maximal temperature $T\leq T_{\max}=(cV/σ)^{1/4}$. We extend this analysis by accounting for thermal enhancement of the discharge process and making the analysis more quantitative. The result is a bound $m\gtrsim\ell (cV/σ)^{1/4}$ on the masses of charged particles. Here, $\ell$ is a term that depends logarithmically on the gauge coupling and particle charge. At weak coupling this leads to a significantly stronger constraint than the $\sqrt{gq}$ scaling of the original Festina Lente bound. As a result, the present vacuum energy requires every particle of charge $10^{-26}\lesssim gq\lesssim e$ to be heavier than $0.03$--$0.2$ eV, provided its gauge boson is lighter than the Hubble scale. An unbroken gauged $B-L$ with Dirac neutrinos gives $m_{ν,{\rm lightest}}\gtrsim10$--$43$ meV for $10^{-29}\lesssim g_{B-L}\lesssim10^{-24}$, in tension with the DESI DR2 limit once $g_{B-L}\gtrsim7\times10^{-28}$. The same limit bounds a neutrino millicharge to $ε_ν\lesssim2\times10^{-27}$. We also revisit the Standard Model effective field theory constraints from the electroweak phase transition. During slow-roll inflation the Standard Model electron violates the bound over the whole range of Hubble rates allowed by the CMB tensor limit and by nucleosynthesis, unless the photon is Higgsed, its coupling is suppressed, or one considers very fine-tuned versions of Higgs inflation.

papers.title_en: Dipolar mixtures in checker-board optical bilayers
papers.abstract_en: Ultra-cold dipolar mixtures in component-dependent optical potentials constitute an interesting platform for the study of the interplay between intra- and inter-component anisotropic long-range interactions. We study the particular case of binary dipolar mixtures placed in separated bilayers which are displaced in an anti-magic wavelength configuration. Using a combination of second-order perturbation theory and cluster-Gutzwiller calculations, we unveil a rich landscape of possible crystalline phases for the two components, showing that, interestingly, inter-site hopping may result, via super-exchange, in solid-into-solid transitions between different crystalline phases. These crystalline phases and the corresponding transitions can be experimentally realized using e.g. lanthanide mixtures in optical lattices.

papers.title_en: Black hole free energy landscapes from constrained instantons
papers.abstract_en: We apply gravitational path integral factorization to provide a semiclassical interpretation of generalized black hole free energy landscapes at fixed external temperature and angular velocities. Boundary integral transforms express the formal partition function as an integral over constrained sectors labeled by complete local partial-Neumann data on an auxiliary hypersurface. Independent variation establishes paired regular subregion solutions as constrained instantons, with Lagrange multipliers supporting lapse and tangential shift jumps that accommodate thermal and rotational mismatches. For selected nonextremal stationary families with an asymptotic boundary, the constrained saddle action takes the form $I_{\rm constr}=β\mathcal F_{\rm gen}=β(E_{\mathcal B}-Ω_{\mathcal B}^{I}J_{\mathcal B,I})-S$, with $β=T^{-1}$. Here $E_{\mathcal B}$ and $J_{\mathcal B,I}$ are renormalized Hamiltonian charges and $S$ is the black hole entropy, whose contribution to the action comes from the regular horizon cap. Interior stationary points of the landscape correspond to smooth equilibrium saddles when the retained variations independently span the entropy and angular momentum directions. We extend the construction to local, parity-even $f(\mathrm{Riemann})$ theories without curvature derivatives by retaining the complete auxiliary interface data. The same thermodynamic form follows with Wald entropy, without a small-deficit expansion. Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes illustrate the Einstein construction, while five-dimensional static AdS black holes in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity and the rotating BTZ branch of new massive gravity provide explicit checks of the higher-curvature extension.

papers.title_en: Reference-renormalized Jacobi primitives for finite-distance massive-particle deflection
papers.abstract_en: We develop a reference-renormalized Jacobi-primitive Gauss-Bonnet formalism for finite-distance weak deflection of massive particles in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. The construction uses the fixed-energy Jacobi metric associated with timelike geodesics and treats the radial curvature primitive as a quantity defined only up to an additive constant. Instead of fixing this constant by requiring the primitive to vanish at a circular timelike orbit, we subtract a reference Jacobi geometry at the same conserved particle energy and impose endpoint normalization on the curvature-density discrepancy. This gives a circular-orbit-free primitive representation of the Gauss-Bonnet curvature contribution while preserving the operational finite-distance definition of the bending angle through local source and receiver directions. We prove that the reference-normalized and circular-orbit-normalized prescriptions agree whenever both are admissible, since their primitives differ only by a constant that cancels from the exact curvature strip integral. The method remains applicable when no admissible circular timelike orbit exists, when the orbit lies outside the Riemannian Jacobi domain, or when the natural no-lens comparison geometry is non-Euclidean. We demonstrate the formalism in three representative settings: Schwarzschild-like bumblebee, Kottler, and Janis-Newman-Winicour (JNW) spacetimes. The formalism therefore identifies circular-orbit anchoring as an auxiliary primitive gauge choice rather than a prerequisite for finite-distance Jacobi Gauss-Bonnet deflection.

papers.title_en: SPLIT: Loosely-coherent inference of long-inspiral gravitational-wave sources for robustness against modeling and data outliers
papers.abstract_en: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will detect gravitational waves (GWs) from dozens of extreme- and intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs/IMRIs). These sources will stay in-band for months to years, offering extraordinary scientific potential. However, their fully phase-coherent analysis standard in current pipelines imposes stringent waveform accuracy requirements; failing to model the signal over such long durations can result in significant systematic biases. To address this, we formulate a robust Bayesian inference framework that segments the data into blocks, infers each block coherently, and recombines the results using loosely-coherent phase information. By restricting full phase-tracking to much shorter block durations, this approach prevents significant accumulation of phase errors. We implement this methodology in \textsc{SPLIT} (Segmented Posteriors for Long-Inspiral Templates), a GPU-accelerated Python package. Applying \textsc{SPLIT} to an environment-rich injection, we demonstrate that while a fully-coherent vacuum-GR analysis incurs a maximum 1D systematic bias of $\approx 4.8σ$ from the truth, the shorter integration window of our loosely-coherent approach restricts such biases to $\lesssim 0.5σ$. Overall, despite a fractional loss of optimal signal-to-noise ratio, the substantial improvement in parameter accuracy offered by our method presents a highly advantageous trade-off for LISA and other future GW detectors.

papers.title_en: Summing over Seifert Manifolds in Narain Ensemble Averages
papers.abstract_en: The ensemble average of Narain conformal field theories over their moduli space is a real-analytic Eisenstein series, whose Poincaré expansion can be interpreted as a sum over lens spaces weighted by the partition functions of Abelian Chern-Simons theory. In this paper we extend this correspondence from lens spaces to Seifert manifolds, which gives an example of a restricted sum over topologies of the kind that arises in three-dimensional quantum gravity. A Seifert manifold is obtained from a fixed core, a punctured surface times a circle, by gluing solid tori to its boundary tori, and we place a copy of the Narain theory on each of these tori. The ensemble average supplies the sum over the solid tori, or more precisely over marked presentations with fixed base genus, number of fibers and integer Seifert invariant. The resulting sum converges absolutely and is a polynomial in the components of the vector-valued Eisenstein series. When all the boundary tori share a single modulus, the average acquires connected corrections, which we identify with wormholes gluing the core to itself; for two boundary tori, the terms with rational Lagrangian sublattices of the Siegel-Eisenstein series are realized by wormholes containing an exceptional fiber. After reduction along the fiber, the construction closely parallels the two-dimensional topological gravity of Marolf and Maxfield, with the base of the fibration playing the role of their spacetime. We also discuss Dehn fillings of 3-manifolds with torus boundary, non-orientable bases, and the surgery formula. Our results suggest that modularity could be an organizing principle in the summation of geometries in quantum gravity.

papers.title_en: For any static interaction the self-energy and vertex corrections to the electron-gas polarizability combine exactly into one integrand free of the Coulomb singularity
papers.abstract_en: The first-order corrections to the polarizability of the uniform electron gas are a self-energy insertion and a vertex correction. For the Coulomb interaction the coefficient of q^2 in each diverges logarithmically at small wave vector, and the two divergences have opposite signs and cancel in their sum. This Note shows that for any interaction that depends only on the momentum it transfers, the two integrands combine exactly into one before any integration is done. At zero temperature the combined integrand has no Coulomb singularity and no chemical-potential counterterm. For screened interactions, which must be integrated numerically, it should be computed in place of the two diagrams. The Note gives the derivation and its physical reason, the one term added at finite temperature, and checks for bare, Yukawa and screened interactions. With a frequency-dependent interaction the combination is no longer exact.

papers.title_en: Gravitational-Wave Signal from a Short GRB Relativistic MHD Jet
papers.abstract_en: We analyze the gravitational-wave (GW) signal produced by a relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of a short GRB jet with parameters corresponding to those of GRB 170817A. The signal that is generated in the hidden central engine of the GRBs is computed by direct integration of the retarded solution of the linearized Einstein equations of an MHD simulation. Separating the GW signal into its baryonic and electromagnetic contributions, we identify the physical origin of its dominant features. The waveform is of the memory type, with $h(f) \propto 1/f$ at low frequencies and a knee at $\sim 0.5-0.5$Hz set by the energy injection time, which corresponds to the GRB duration. A pronounced early peak reflects the opening of the magnetic field lines and the equatorial kick given to the ejecta at the onset of the jet, demonstrating that the GW signal can reveal processes deep in the GRB engine that cannot be observed otherwise. The signal is strongest for observers far from the jet axis. The total radiated GW energy is only $\sim 10^{42}$ erg, about $10^{-9}$ of the jet energy; it scales as ${\cal E}^2/τ$ with the shortest variability time $τ$, so this is a lower limit. Comparing the predicted spectrum with the sensitivity of current and future detectors, we find that events similar to GW170817 are marginally detectable by DECIGO from up to 10 Mpc and by the Einstein Telescope from 1 Mpc. The injected Poynting flux in this simulation was smooth. An engine variable on a millisecond timescale, as predicted in some GRB models, would substantially increase the GW energy and detectability.

papers.title_en: Probing Cosmic-Ray-Boosted and Supernova-Sourced Sub-GeV Dark Matter with Paleo-Detectors
papers.abstract_en: Astrophysical dark matter particles with masses well below GeV-scale can be difficult to detect using conventional nuclear recoil experiments due to their low velocities in our Milky Way halo. Elastic scattering with high-energy cosmic rays or thermal production inside core-collapse supernovae can accelerate sub-GeV DM to (semi-)relativistic velocities, producing nuclear recoil energies above the keV threshold that paleo-detectors can record over geological timescales. Using olivine as the target with 100$\,$g$\cdot$Gyr exposure, we compute track length distributions from such (semi-)relativistic dark matter fluxes, incorporating all major backgrounds (neutrinos, uranium-chain neutrons, thorium recoils) with a statistical analysis on an Asimov dataset. We derive 95 C.L. projected sensitivity of paleo-detectors to the DM-nucleon cross section for dark matter masses between a few MeV and hundreds of MeV. Our results show that paleo-detectors are able to probe large parameter regions that are not covered by current and near-future experiments designed to detect dark matter and neutrinos. In particular, paleo-detectors offer a unique ability to record the dark matter flux from Galactic supernova events over geological times. Such cumulative exposure enables sensitivity gains of a few orders of magnitude compared to conventional experiments.

papers.title_en: Dual-Space Analysis of Vortex Configurations and Rotational Energy in a 2D Optical Lattice
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the effects of a stationary two-dimensional periodic optical lattice on a rotating Bose--Einstein condensate confined by an isotropic harmonic trap. Within the mean-field description, the condensate is modeled by the two-dimensional Gross--Pitaevskii equation in the rotating frame and solved numerically using an imaginary-time split-step Crank--Nicolson method to obtain stationary vortex states. We examine how the lattice depth, lattice wave vector, particle number, and angular velocity influence the vortex configurations, real-space density, momentum-space density, and energetics of the condensate. We find that the stationary periodic lattice significantly modifies vortex nucleation and spatial organization: vortices emerge progressively with increasing angular velocity and, for sufficiently strong lattice strength, undergo rearrangement and merging. Importantly, changes in the vortex configuration are directly reflected in the momentum-space density, demonstrating that vortex nucleation and rearrangement produce pronounced modifications of the condensate momentum distribution. We further analyze the energy per particle and rotational energy as functions of the angular velocity and find that the presence of the optical lattice substantially alters the rotational response of the condensate. In particular, the rotational energy is progressively reduced at higher angular velocities as the lattice strength is increased. These results demonstrate how a stationary periodic optical lattice modifies vortex formation, momentum-space structure, and rotational energetics of a rotating trapped Bose--Einstein condensate.

papers.title_en: Holographic RG Flows from Running Couplings
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the RG flow in the holographic setup and study new IR physics at the IR fixed point, when a relevant scalar operator deforms a two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT). On the dual gravity side, the renormalization group (RG) flow from the UV to the IR CFT can be described by a scalar field rolling from an unstable to a stable equilibrium point. Specifically, to make the scale dependence of the RG flow more explicit, we study the running coupling constant obtained by solving the beta function. After considering a simple scalar potential, we study the change of the coupling constant and its effect on the ground state along the RG flow. We showed that the central charge monotonically decreases along the RG flow, and its value at the IR fixed point is determined by the conformal dimension of the deformation operator and the coupling constant at the IR fixed point. We further investigate how changing the ground state influences the two-point function and conformal dimension of a local operator in the probe limit.

papers.title_en: Electrically tunable moiré hybridization in scalable twist-with-a-spacer structures
papers.abstract_en: Moiré superlattices emerge from the interplay between interlayer hybridization and long-wavelength periodicity, both set by the twist angle between layers in direct contact. Here we show that moiré minibands and pronounced Brown-Zak oscillations persist even when twisted graphene layers are separated by an atomically thin spacer, such as a misaligned graphene monolayer. This twist-with-a-spacer architecture reduces interlayer coupling, such that moiré hybridization can be tuned with a modest displacement field without changing moiré periodicity, allowing us to disentangle the roles of those parameters in miniband formation. Importantly, the spacer suppresses atomic relaxation, enabling highly uniform, rigid superlattices at twist angles down to ~0.1 degree. This robustness allows twist-with-a-spacer structures to be grown directly by scalable chemical vapour deposition (CVD): devices fabricated from CVD-grown structures exhibit the same moiré physics phenomena as those assembled manually. Our work provides insights into the physics of moiré bandstructure formation and opens a route towards scalable moiré systems.

papers.title_en: Observation of Superconductivity in a Cu-Rich High-Entropy Alloy
papers.abstract_en: A Cu-rich multielement alloy containing Zn, Sn, Ag, and Au was synthesized and studied to explore its structural and physical properties. The alloy was prepared by vacuum-sealed melting of high-purity elements followed by rapid quenching in cold water. Powder X-ray diffraction confirms that the alloy crystallizes in a face-centered cubic (fcc) Cu-type structure. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping show uniform distribution of all constituent elements. Magnetic measurements indicate the appearance of a superconducting transition at low temperature, while electrical resistivity remains metallic without reaching zero resistance. This difference between magnetic and transport behaviour suggests that the superconducting state may be limited to local or partial regions within the sample. These findings indicate that the Cu-rich multielement alloy exhibits unusual low-temperature properties and may represent a new class of compositionally complex Cu-based materials with superconducting characteristics.

papers.title_en: Signatures of quark matter from neutron star mass-radius curve
papers.abstract_en: Signatures of the presence of quark matter inside neutron stars are obtained from the analysis of more than 250,000 mass-radius curves that describe nucleonic, hyperonic and hybrid stars, based on five different hadronic relativistic mean-field models and four different descriptions of quark matter. A radius maximum occurring above $1.7\,M_\odot$ strongly favors quark matter inside the star. A second criterion identifying the presence of quark matter is $X>-0.2$km, where X=[R(2.0)-R(1.6)]-[R(1.6)-R(1.4)] is obtained from the radius of stars with 2.0, 1.6 and 1.4 $M_\odot$. It is also shown that most of the hyperonic stars have a radius maximum that peaks around 1.5$M_\odot$ and compactness below 0.27 for the maximum-mass configuration, while for the nucleonic stars that have a radius maximum, this peaks below 1.3$M_\odot$ and the compactness of the maximum-mass configuration lies above 0.26.

papers.title_en: A magnetically heated slim disc-corona model for tidal disruption events
papers.abstract_en: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) can reach super-Eddington luminosities near their peak. While their optical/UV emission may arise from multiple processes, X-rays are more likely to be produced by the innermost accretion flow close to the black hole, analogous to super-Eddington flows in stellar-mass X-ray binaries (XRBs) and active galactic nuclei (AGNs). Super-Eddington AGNs typically show disc-dominated spectra, with weak and steep coronae, while super-Eddington XRBs show a wider variety of spectral shapes. Here we explore disc-corona coupling in TDEs by developing a super-Eddington ($\dot{m}>1$: slim) disc model in which magnetic reconnection transfers some of the accretion power from the disc into a hot Comptonizing corona. We test the model on the well-monitored X-ray TDE AT2021ehb, and can broadly fit the brightest X-ray spectra with a black-hole mass $M_{\rm BH}\sim10^6$--$10^7\,M_\odot$ at $\dot m\sim 1$, but need variable magnetic coupling to the disc to match the large observed fast changes in coronal contribution. AGN at similarly high luminosity do not show such variable coronae, but the transient XRB outbursts do, suggesting that it may be a common feature of rapidly changing, non-steady accretion flows. As the TDE declines to $\dot{m}\sim 0.01$, the source hardens, but never goes below $Γ\sim 2$, unlike both AGN and XRB at these luminosities. Thus the X-ray spectral evolution in this TDE does not resemble either XRB or AGN in detail, likely pointing to the very different, highly variable nature of the accretion flow in a tidal disruption event.

papers.title_en: 2+1 flavor light hadron spectrum with PACS10 configurations
papers.abstract_en: We present the results for the hadron spectrum, the pseudoscalar meson decay constants, and the quark mass ratio in the continuum limit using the ``PACS10'' gauge configurations generated with the $O(a)$-improved Wilson quark action and the Iwasaki gauge action. Numerical simulations are carried out at three lattice spacings keeping the space-time volumes over (10 fm$)^4$ in 2+1 flavor QCD at the physical point. We calculate physical quantities with two choices of conventions to define pseudoexperimental values expected in the isosymmetric QCD. In order to investigate the finite size effects on the physical quantities we have additionally generated the (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice at the coarsest lattice spacing of $a=0.08487(14)$~fm, which is a hypercube with half the length in each direction compared to the PACS10 configurations. While the finite size effect is hardly observed in comparison of the hadron effective masses on the (10.9 fm$)^4$ and (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattices, the results for the pseudoscalar meson decay constants show discrepancies beyond the error bars. The (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice also serves for determining the expansion parameters of the pseudoscalar meson masses and decay constants, and the octet baryon masses in terms of the quark masses around the physical point with the aid of the mass reweighting technique. The expansion parameters are used for the fine-tuning of the physical point employing the pseudoexperimental masses of the $π$ meson, $K$ meson, and the $Ξ$ baryon as physical inputs in each convention. We compare the results for the octet baryon masses and the pseudoscalar decay constants in the continuum limit with the corresponding pseudoexperimental values in both conventions. We also discuss the deviation between two results with different conventions. As for the quark mass ratio the result is compared with the recent FLAG summary.

papers.title_en: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
papers.abstract_en: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko. Both families converge coefficientwise to the vertex and satisfy the full commuting equations modulo $p^s$. For $n\geq3$, we prove sharp degree-dependent congruences and compute leading residues at every $p$-power scale. Their discrepancy has coefficient norm $p^{-1}$ and an exact weighted Gauss norm giving uniform decay on smaller closed polydiscs. For the master family, multivariable Dwork congruences reconstruct the vertex by an infinite product. The results hold in every rank for $0<r/d\leq1/2$ and odd prime $p$.

papers.title_en: Stacked strong and weak lensing united: Improved measurement of the stellar and dark matter distributions in massive early-type galaxies at $z\sim 0.5$
papers.abstract_en: We present a new measurement of the stellar and dark matter distributions in massive early-type galaxies at redshift $0.4<z<0.6$ by combining stacked strong and weak lensing measurements. The stacked weak lensing measurements down to the small radius of $0.013\,\mathrm{Mpc}/h$ enabled by the Subaru Telescope Hyper Suprime-Cam data are combined with stacked enclosed projected mass measurements from 13 strong lens systems. We find that adding strong lensing constraints improves constraints on the stellar and dark matter distributions. The central dark matter profile is found to be consistent with the standard Navarro-Frenk-White density profile. The stellar initial mass function is found to be bottom-heavy. The total density profile in the inner region is described well by the power-law density profile with the slope of $-1.96\pm 0.07$, which can also explain weak lensing signals out to $1\,\mathrm{Mpc}/h$ reasonably well. The stacked weak lensing profile constrains an internal mass-sheet transformation parameter to $λ_{\mathrm{c}}=0.978\pm0.010$ assuming a single cored component. Our analysis demonstrates that the combination of the stacked strong and weak lensing serves as a powerful tool for studying central density profiles of galaxies.

papers.title_en: Chemical abundances of a Galactic Centre ejecta discovered in DESI
papers.abstract_en: Chemical abundances in the Galactic Centre (GC) are challenging to measure because of high extinction, crowding, and distance, and are typically limited to the brightest AGB and M giants observed in the near-infrared. In contrast, hypervelocity stars (HVSs) ejected from the GC by Sgr A* carry their natal composition into accessible regions such as the Milky Way halo, making them unique probes of GC chemistry. We present high-resolution optical Magellan/MIKE spectroscopy of DESI-312, a bound HVS candidate in the halo with super-solar metallicity ($[\mathrm{Fe/H}]=0.2\pm0.1$). This sets it apart from accreted halo populations on radial orbits and is most naturally explained by GC formation and Hills-mechanism ejection. Updated isochrone fits give an age of 7.4-11.3 Gyr; together with its metallicity and kinematics, this strengthens the case for a GC origin. Korg and Turbospectrum spectral synthesis yields $[\mathrm{X/Fe}]$ for 22 elements, plus Li from an independent line-by-line NLTE analysis. As DESI-312 is near the main sequence, its C, N, and O abundances are unaltered by dredge-up; to our knowledge, these are the first such measurements of unevolved GC material. Its abundance pattern lies where the nuclear star cluster (NSC), nuclear stellar disc (NSD), and inner-bulge sequences overlap, with a Na enhancement ($[\mathrm{Na/Fe}]=+0.16^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$) more modest than in NSC giants of similar metallicity. Chemistry alone thus cannot identify its progenitor; we nevertheless favour the NSC, given its large reservoir of old, metal-rich stars and the star's kinematics. Alongside WINERED-HVS1 and the S-star S0-6/S10, whose abundances point to different progenitors, this tentatively suggests multiple progenitor populations for the S-star cluster. DESI-312 is a test case for sampling GC chemistry with ejected dwarfs at optical wavelengths, complementing near-infrared studies of giants.

papers.title_en: Reflected constraint algebras of open Carroll--Weyl null strings
papers.abstract_en: We study whether open null strings admit the full Carroll--Weyl gauge symmetry consistently with endpoint conditions and nontrivial physical degrees of freedom. For endpoints constrained to timelike defects, natural variations imply that any nonzero Carroll flow must be tangent to the worldsheet boundary. For a fixed linear defect through the target origin, we construct a differentiable Hamiltonian system on this branch. Its complete Carroll--Weyl generator requires no additional boundary charge. Smooth reflection defines a preserved subdomain and gives a circle interpretation to selected sine and cosine modes of the constraints. Their centreless algebra extends the two-constraint open-string algebra by the local scale constraint. An endpoint obstruction shows that this reflection condition excludes some gauge orbits of the natural interval theory: we exhibit a regular four-dimensional solution with no corresponding reflected representative. Within the reflected sector, we construct a local canonical field pair and conserved target-space Lorentz charges. A separate solution family has nonzero boost charge and a nondegenerate two-dimensional symplectic pullback. The constraint algebra, the boundary choice, and the physical observables thus provide complementary information about the open theory.

papers.title_en: Spectral Codes: A Geometric Formalism for Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract_en: We present a new geometric perspective on quantum error correction based on spectral triples in noncommutative geometry. In this approach, quantum error correcting codes are reformulated as low energy spectral projections of Dirac type operators that separate global logical degrees of freedom from local, correctable errors. Locality, code distance, and the Knill Laflamme condition acquire a unified spectral and geometric interpretation in terms of the induced metric and spectrum of the Dirac operator. Within this framework, a wide range of known error correcting codes including classical linear codes, stabilizer codes, GKP type codes, and topological codes are recovered from a single construction. This demonstrates that classical and quantum codes can be organized within a common geometric language. A central advantage of the spectral triple perspective is that the performance of error correction can be directly related to spectral properties. We show that leakage out of the code space is controlled by the spectral gap of the Dirac operator, and that code preserving internal perturbations can systematically increase this gap without altering the encoded logical subspace. This yields a geometric mechanism for enhancing error correction thresholds, which we illustrate explicitly for a stabilizer code. We further interpret Berezin Toeplitz quantization as a mixed spectral code and briefly discuss implications for holographic quantum error correction. Overall, our results suggest that quantum error correction can be viewed as a universal low energy phenomenon governed by spectral geometry.

papers.title_en: Circular dichroism in second- and third-harmonic generation in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi
papers.abstract_en: We theoretically investigate circular dichroism (CD) in second- and third-harmonic generation (SHG and THG) in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi. We demonstrate that both SHG and THG exhibit dichroic responses of order unity, while their robustness against spectral broadening is strikingly different. Specifically, while SHG-CD is strongly suppressed by dissipation, THG-CD remains robust over a wide frequency range. We show that this qualitative difference originates from the phase structure of the nonlinear current, where SHG-CD arises from subleading interference processes that are sensitive to dephasing, whereas THG-CD emerges already at the leading nonlinear order and is therefore protected against spectral broadening. As a result, THG-CD provides a robust probe of chirality encoded in nonequilibrium electronic dynamics. We further reveal non-monotonic frequency dependences and pronounced sensitivity of harmonic emission to the polarization state and crystallographic orientation of the driving field. Our results provide a representative example of robust nonlinear chiroptical responses in chiral topological semimetals and highlight the potential of high-harmonic spectroscopy as a probe of phase-resolved electronic dynamics.

papers.title_en: A Massive and Eccentric Binary Millisecond Pulsar in the Globular Cluster M10
papers.abstract_en: We present the timing solution of the millisecond pulsar PSR J1657-0406A in the globular cluster M10, based on observations performed with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). The timing results show that PSR J1657-0406A is in a long-period ($P_b \sim 37$ days) and eccentric ($e \sim 0.12$) orbit. We also measured the periastron advance $\dotω = 0.00090(13)$ degrees per year, which implies a total system mass of $2.5(6)$ solar masses, assuming that general relativity accurately models the orbital motion. No optical counterpart was detected within the positional uncertainty, indicating that the companion is unlikely to be a main-sequence star. Considering possible formation channels for the orbital eccentricity, we favor a helium white dwarf companion, although a massive white dwarf or neutron star cannot be completely excluded.

papers.title_en: Symmetry-Protected Topological Structures in Quantum Many-Body Scar Subspaces
papers.abstract_en: We investigate how symmetry-associated topological properties, originally defined for ground states, can be consistently extended to dynamically isolated subspaces of quantum many-body systems. Focusing on quantum many-body scars (QMBS), we show that a scar subspace is invariant under the relevant symmetries, and it can support well-defined topological properties inherited from an underlying symmetry-protected topological (SPT) ground state, even though individual scar states need not themselves be symmetric. We refer to such structures as SPT-like scar subspaces, emphasizing that the topological properties are defined at the level of the symmetry-invariant subspace rather than on a state-by-state basis. As a concrete example, we analyze the spin-$1$ Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki (AKLT) model, where a restricted spectrum-generating algebra (rSGA) generates a tower of QMBS on top of a nontrivial SPT ground state admitting a matrix product state (MPS) representation. We demonstrate that the resulting symmetry-invariant scar subspace inherits well-defined topological characteristics, encoded in bond-space symmetry representations, expectation values of symmetry-twist operators, and long-range string order in the dilute regime. We further show that these features persist in a broader class of models, including deformations and higher-spin generalizations that preserve the relevant symmetries and admit nontrivial SPT ground states with MPS representations. Our results provide a general framework in which symmetry-associated topological properties, while inherited from the ground state, are consistently realized at the level of symmetry-invariant nonthermal subspaces. This perspective clarifies how topological structures can be meaningfully defined beyond individual eigenstates.

papers.title_en: Nano-Nb Superconducting 3D Josephson Junctions Arrays in Cu-Normal Matrix: Superconducting Phase Coherence and Quantum Fluctuations Properties
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the superconducting behavior, phase coherence, and quantum fluctuation properties of three-dimensional arrays of nanometric Nb Josephson junctions embedded in a normal Cu matrix ($\text{Cu-}x\text{ wt}\%\text{Nb}$, $x = 3, 5, 15,$ and $20$), with emphasis on the $5$ and $15$ compositions. Magnetic properties were measured by dc magnetization as a function of temperature and magnetic field using a SQUID magnetometer and by ac susceptibility. Transport properties, including magnetoresistance, $V(I)$ curves, and the critical current $I_c(H,T)$, were measured at fields up to $90\text{ kOe}$. A micro-Hall sensor with ten transverse voltage bridges ($5.0 \times 0.2 \times 0.01\text{ }μ\text{m}^3$) was used to calibrate the magnetic field actually applied to the sample. Magnetization and transport measurements reveal a double superconducting transition that depends on the applied field and current: $T_c(H)$, with $T_c(0) = 8.2\text{ K}$, is associated with the intragranular response of the Nb grains, whereas the lower $T_c(H)$ is associated with Josephson coupling between grains through the Cu matrix. The response combines that of bulk Nb with signatures of weakly coupled grains, consistent with a collection of superconducting grains embedded in a nonsuperconducting matrix. The characteristic fields $H_{c1} = 400.03\text{ Oe}$ and $H_{c2} = 15\text{ kOe}$ (grains), and $H_{c1j} = 99.93\text{ Oe}$ and $H_{c2j} = 199.25\text{ Oe}$ (intergranular coupling), were determined. The critical current $I_c(H,T)$ exhibits a central maximum at low fields, followed by a long tail and small oscillations with a period of $ΔH \approx 24\text{ Oe}$, attributed to quantum interference between coupled grains. At higher fields, magnetic flux gradients destroy phase coherence and randomize the phase $θ$ of the order parameter $ψ= |ψ|e^{iθ}$, suppressing the oscillations.

papers.title_en: Full edge control of bulk energy gap in armchair graphene nanoribbons
papers.abstract_en: In solid-state physics, the ability to open and tune an electronic energy gap provides a direct route to controlling charge transport and accessing distinct electronic phases. In solids with physical boundaries, a bulk energy gap formed exclusively by extended bulk states is conventionally expected to be governed primarily by the interior bulk region, with only a minor contribution from the boundaries. Here we show that, in stark contrast to this conventional expectation, the bulk gap of armchair graphene nanoribbons in the $N_w=3p+2$ family with $p\in\mathbb{Z}\ge 0$ can be fully controlled through the hoppings solely at the boundaries. This full boundary control originates from an exact cancellation between the gap contributions of long-range hoppings along and across the ribbon in the bulk region. It persists in the presence of Hubbard interactions and holds irrespective of ribbon width in this family. Our findings establish boundary dynamics as an unexpectedly powerful means of manipulating bulk electronic properties, enabling width-preserving engineering of one-dimensional (1D) band structures and topological phases, with potential applications in qubits, artificial quantum spin chains, topological quantum dots and other quantum devices.

papers.title_en: 6d Large Charge and 2d Virasoro Blocks
papers.abstract_en: We compute observables in the interacting rank-one 6d $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ SCFT at large R-charge. We focus on correlators involving $Φ^n$, namely symmetric products of the bottom component of the supermultiplet containing the stress-tensor. By using the moduli space effective action and methods from the large-charge expansion, we compute the OPE coefficients $\langleΦ^nΦ^mΦ^{n+m}\rangle$ in an expansion in 1/n. The coefficients of the expansion are only partially determined from the 6d perspective, but we manage to fix them order-by-order in 1/n numerically by utilizing the 6d/2d correspondence. This is made possible by the fact that this $6d$ observable can be extracted in 2d from a specific double-scaling limit of the vacuum Virasoro block, which can be efficiently computed numerically. We also extend the computation to higher-rank SCFTs, and discuss various applications of our results to 6d as well as 2d.

papers.title_en: Fermi surface and field-induced Lifshitz transition in the antiferromagnet NbMnP exhibiting an anomalous Hall effect
papers.abstract_en: We performed Shubnikov--de Haas (SdH) oscillation measurements on the $\mathbf{Q}=0$ antiferromagnet NbMnP, which exhibits a large anomalous Hall effect. The SdH frequencies observed in the low-field region up to 17.5~T are well described by first-principles band-structure calculations based on the $B_{3g}+B_{2u}$ noncollinear magnetic structure determined by neutron diffraction. The effective masses are enhanced by approximately a factor of two relative to the calculated band masses. High-field measurements up to 41.5~T reveal a Lifshitz transition accompanied by a pronounced evolution of the SdH frequency spectrum. These results confirm that first-principles calculations provide a reliable tool for the development of functional antiferromagnetic materials, while also demonstrating that field-induced changes in the Fermi surface itself need to be taken into account in understanding their high-field magnetotransport properties.

papers.title_en: Static Vacuum Geometry Encodes Gravitational Collapse and Cosmology
papers.abstract_en: We show that, within covariant Hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, a prescribed one-parameter family of static vacuum geometries uniquely determines the local dynamics of gravitational collapse coupled to irrotational dust, despite the nonuniqueness of the underlying gravitational Hamiltonian. We further derive necessary and sufficient conditions under which the resulting dynamics admits a homogeneous and isotropic cosmological sector. These conditions establish a two-way correspondence between static vacuum geometries and modified Friedmann dynamics and impose a universal restriction on the spatial-curvature dependence of the latter. Our results provide a criterion for determining whether independently proposed black-hole and cosmological models can arise from a common covariant gravitational theory.

papers.title_en: Gauge-invariant non-universal scalar couplings in teleparallel gravity
papers.abstract_en: We develop a gauge-invariant teleparallel framework in which the universality of the gravitational coupling is relaxed for a scalar field, while the gravitational sector retains the form of the teleparallel equivalent of General Relativity. The non-universal interaction is encoded in a scalar-sector tetrad whose coupling to the universal translational gauge potential is controlled by a field-dependent gravitational charge. A Stückelberg completion preserves local translational gauge invariance, and we derive the gravitational, scalar-field, and Stückelberg equations, together with the antisymmetric constraint and their consistency relations. As a first application, we investigate homogeneous and isotropic cosmology, where the Stückelberg constraint provides a first integral governing the evolution of the non-universal coupling. In the kination-dominated regime, the standard stiff-fluid behavior is recovered asymptotically, whereas in the potential-dominated regime, accelerated expansion requires additional conditions beyond potential domination. We identify compatible expanding solutions in which departures from universality are dynamically suppressed, including examples approaching power-law inflation or asymptotically de Sitter expansion. Including a universally coupled perfect fluid and a constant scalar potential, we obtain a late-time solution exhibiting a subdominant matter-like contribution to the background Friedmann equation and an asymptotic de Sitter limit. These results provide a gauge-theoretic realization of non-universal scalar couplings and highlight their potential implications for early- and late-time cosmology.

papers.title_en: Imaging the Current Distribution in Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensors with Scanning SQUID Microscopy
papers.abstract_en: Transition-edge sensors (TESs) exploit the resistive transition of a superconductor to detect minute changes in temperature. While significant progress has been made in understanding the temperature- and current-dependent resistive transition in these devices, important aspects of TES behavior under bias remain unresolved. In particular, existing TES models largely neglect spatial variations in the superconducting state and current distribution arising from device geometry and proximity effects associated with the superconducting leads and normal metal features. Using scanning superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) microscopy (SSM), we directly image local superconducting properties and transport current in two molybdenum-gold (MoAu) X-ray TES designs. We measure the local diamagnetic response to identify superconducting regions in devices voltage-biased within the transition and the Oersted field generated by the transport current to reconstruct the corresponding current distribution. We observe bias-dependent reconfigurations of the current distribution that track current-induced changes in superconducting regions, highlighting the importance of mesoscale spatial variations for TES device physics, operation, and design.

papers.title_en: Pilot search for continuous gravitational waves from Hercules X-1 in O3 LIGO data: enhancements to a hidden Markov model
papers.abstract_en: A semi-coherent search is conducted for continuous gravitational waves from stellar oscillations in Hercules X-1 with data from Observing Run 3 of the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory, using an established hidden Markov model algorithm to track stochastic wandering of the signal frequency. The primary goal is to implement and test several algorithmic enhancements relevant to future searches, including a second-order projected semi-major axis correction, an orbital eccentricity correction, an adjustment to the width of a search subband, and propagation of the electromagnetically measured orbital parameters with a nonzero orbital period derivative. The enhancements are validated by injecting synthetic signals into Gaussian noise and improve the sensitivity depth by $\approx$ 14% for a Hercules X-1-like target. In the 60--200 Hz band, the pilot search yields four candidates that survive a five-level veto procedure, whose terminating frequencies are 76.41 Hz, 109.47 Hz, 144.40 Hz, and 189.24 Hz. The frequentist upper limit on the maximum detectable wave strain at 95% confidence is arbitrarily set at 174 Hz and found to be $9.3 \times 10^{-26}$, assuming a uniform prior on polarization.

papers.title_en: A concordance model of neutron star kicks
papers.abstract_en: Neutron stars (NSs) receive natal kicks during supernovae that affect their survival in binaries and motion through the Galaxy. The global distribution of these kick velocities across the NS population remains uncertain. Here, we combine the orbital properties and birth rates of Gaia NS and Be+NS binaries with velocity constraints from young isolated pulsars to construct a concordance model of NS natal kicks. We find that all three populations can be jointly described by a shared bimodal kick distribution. The low-velocity component follows a lognormal distribution with $μ_{\ln v}=1.87^{+0.65}_{-0.53}$ and $σ_{\ln v}=0.55^{+0.85}_{-0.44}$, corresponding to a median speed of $6.5^{+5.9}_{-2.7}~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$. The high-velocity component is consistent with the distribution inferred from young pulsars, which peaks near $200~{\rm km~s^{-1}}$. The low-velocity component contributes only $\sim10\%$ of all NS births, but produces most Gaia NS binaries and roughly half of Be+NS binaries. The same model predicts systemic recoil velocities consistent with the observed kinematics of Gaia NSs, Be+NS binaries, and NS low-mass X-ray binaries. For Gaia NSs, whose formation history remains unknown, we use this kick distribution to constrain their progenitors. We favor pre-supernova binaries containing intermediate-mass stripped stars with $\sim1~{\rm M_\odot}$ companions in au-scale orbits, and predict $\sim300$ such binaries in the Milky Way today, $\sim40$ in the LMC, and $\sim30$ in the SMC. Finally, we consider the implications of these kicks for NSs in hierarchical triples. We find that 2-10$\%$ of Gaia NS triples and 3-23$\%$ of Be+NS triples retain their tertiary after the supernova. Overall, our results suggest that a shared natal kick law can account for isolated pulsars and surviving NS binaries, where most NSs receive large kicks and low kicks are common among surviving binaries.

papers.title_en: Thirty years of primordial deuterium abundances: A provenance-aware statistical reanalysis
papers.abstract_en: (ABRIDGED:) Primordial deuterium provides one of the most precise observational tests of Big Bang nucleosynthesis, yet the published literature is built on a comparatively small number of high-redshift absorption systems. We construct a provenance-aware database of 957 published primordial-D/H values from 247 publications spanning 1994--2026 and trace observational entries, wherever possible, to their underlying physical absorbers. Of the 795 observational entries, 80.1 percent represent reused individual or compilation values; only 11.4 percent correspond to new determinations of individual absorption systems. Although 52 distinct absorbers are identified overall, the eight most frequently represented systems account for 62.0 percent of all identifiable absorber mentions. An inverse Herfindahl--Hirschman measure applied to our full database gives an effective representation equivalent to only 16.28 equally represented absorbers, demonstrating that the published literature is strongly concentrated around a much smaller effective subset. Despite this strong internal dependence, the modern consensus value of $10^5({\rm D/H})\simeq2.5$ is robust to alternative absorber-level treatments and survives removal of the eight dominant systems. However, the apparent precision of literature-level compilations is more sensitive to repeated representation than a simple count of published values implies. We also identify a synchronised transition in the compilation literature around 2013--2014, associated with increasingly selective and homogeneous analyses while older individual values continued to circulate. The modern D/H consensus is therefore robust in central value, but the underlying literature is less statistically independent than its publication density suggests. This thus highlights the importance of provenance-aware analysis in precision cosmology.

papers.title_en: Large superconducting diode effect indicates nonuniform triplet pairing in UTe2
papers.abstract_en: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking -- how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe$_2$, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory, demonstrating that the intertwining of magnetic and triplet superconducting orders can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.

papers.title_en: Chirality-Induced Angular-Momentum Pumping by Moving Charges
