papers.abstract_en: Trapped-ion quantum computers are promising as a platform for realizing quantum computational advantage. They promise long coherence times, near all-to-all connectivity, and potential multiqubit gates as distinguishing advantages compared to competing platforms. Regarding these advantages, it is crucial to understand the trade-offs between increasing engineering complexity and actual improvements in running quantum algorithms with a more flexible gate set. In this work, we investigate this question and develop a versatile toolset to evaluate the performance of gate sets composed of native Mølmer--Sørensen multiqubit gates. To this end, we employ unitary synthesis as an application-agnostic benchmark target and identify specific hardware requirements for multiqubit gates to be advantageous.

papers.title_en: A universal gauge structure in the photon content of light-matter systems
papers.abstract_en: After truncating the matter Hilbert space of a single-mode light-matter model, gauge transformations leave the spectrum invariant whereas the ground-state photon number is gauge dependent, hence, its meaning remains disputed. We show that this gauge dependence obeys an exact algebraic law whenever the gauge transformation acts as a displacement of the field coupled to a matter operator $G$. Namely, the ground-state photon number is a quadratic polynomial in the gauge parameter $λ$, $\langle a^{\dagger} a\rangle_λ$$=$$\langle a^{\dagger} a\rangle_{0}$$+$$Cλ$$+$$Qλ^2$. Here the coefficients are the correlator $C=\langle G\,p\rangle$ of $G$ and the field momentum $p$, and $Q=\langle G^2\rangle$. Its minimum over all gauges is naturally gauge-invariant, and for the quantum Rabi model it is determined by the ground-state energy alone. We show that it is strictly positive for the quantum Rabi and Dicke models with level splitting, so that a residual photon content survives in every gauge. At weak coupling the gauge of minimal photon number is the Jaynes-Cummings gauge, and for the Dicke model it remains so at all couplings in the thermodynamic limit.

papers.title_en: The Radio Neutrino Observatory in Greenland (RNO-G) - System Design and Instrumentation
papers.abstract_en: The Radio Neutrino Observatory in Greenland (RNO-G) is designed to measure cosmic neutrinos in the EeV range through an array of radio antennas detecting nanosecond-long radio flashes. In this contribution, the RNO-G electronic system is outlined, illustrating how signals are measured from the antennas to the recorded pulses. We present new instrumentation developments, focusing on electric melters to install LPDA antennas into the Greenlandic ice sheet. The new system will simplify deployment and reduce positioning uncertainty to $\pm$2cm (x/y) and $\pm$1°(rotational). We report on field tests from the RNO-G site at Summit Station.

papers.title_en: Enabling Dynamic Resource Scaling in Quantum Circuit Simulations
papers.abstract_en: Studies of quantum algorithms often simulate se- quences of circuits whose number of qubits changes from one circuit to the next, such as instances of increasing size of the same problem. Since each additional qubit doubles the state- vector, every circuit needs a different number of nodes, which a fixed allocation on a shared High-Performance Computing (HPC) system cannot provide: a job sized for the largest circuit leaves most of its nodes idle, and one job per circuit adds scheduler interactions and queue waits. We make the QuEST state-vector simulator malleable with the Dynamic Management of Resources (DMR) framework, so that a single job resizes between circuits. Because no state-vector exists between circuits, reconfigurations require no data redistribution and no changes to the simulation kernels, and a checkpoint holding the index of the next circuit is enough to resume. A right-sizing policy derives the number of nodes from the number of qubits, and the circuit_executor API hides reconfigurations from the user. We evaluate the reconfiguration overhead on MareNostrum 5 and show that a single job can run a batch of circuits of different sizes, adapting its allocation to each of them with negligible overhead.

papers.title_en: Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons II
papers.abstract_en: We extend the formalism of Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons to include Wilson Loops.

papers.title_en: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
papers.abstract_en: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

papers.title_en: Quantum Monte Carlo Studies of U(1) Lattice Gauge Models of Kondo Breakdown
papers.abstract_en: In the local-moment regime, heavy fermions are most economically described by a compact U(1) gauge theory. Motivated by this perspective, we study a minimal compact U(1) lattice gauge model describing a spin chain coupled to two-dimensional Dirac conduction electrons. The spin chain is described by fermionic partons carrying spin and U(1) gauge charge. The heavy-fermion quasiparticle is a bound state of a U(1) matter field carrying unit electric charge and U(1) gauge charge, and the fermionic parton. Using sign-problem-free determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we identify two symmetry-equivalent regimes: a heavy-fermion metal with a sharp composite-fermion resonance and robust low-frequency transport, and a Kondo-breakdown metal with an incoherent resonance and vanishing low-frequency transport. For any finite lattice extent in the direction perpendicular to the chain, the Luttinger volume of the heavy-fermion phase counts both composite and conduction electrons, while in the Kondo-breakdown phase it counts only the conduction electrons. The evolution of the composite-fermion spectrum, dynamical spin structure factor, and optical conductivity provides a nonperturbative demonstration of gauge-mediated Kondo breakdown and establishes transport fingerprints of an orbital-selective Mott transition in the context of U(1) gauge theories of heavy fermions.

papers.title_en: The role of the top-quark mass in electroweak physics
papers.abstract_en: The top quark, the heaviest elementary particle known, has a profound influence on electroweak physics. Its mass and interactions place it at the intersection of precision tests of the Standard Model (SM) and searches for physics beyond it (BSM). In this work, we provide a comprehensive review of the role of the top-quark mass in electroweak interactions, highlighting theoretical developments, latest experimental measurements, and their implications for Higgs physics, vacuum stability, and possible new physics scenarios.

papers.title_en: Combinatorial Residual Network: a decay-chain-aware classifier without explicit jet assignment
papers.abstract_en: Final states with several jets from the decays of heavy particles pose a combinatorial problem, since the jets must be assigned, at least implicitly, to their parent particles. We describe the Combinatorial Residual Network (CoReNet), a classifier that encodes the assumed decay chain of the final state in its architecture. CoReNet builds its event representation level by level along the decay hierarchy, evaluates every jet assignment hypothesis with weights shared across objects, and combines the hypotheses with learned weights using residual networks. The exchange symmetries of the decay are built into the construction, the size of the network does not depend on the number of hypotheses, and the network is trained with the classification loss alone, without generator-level jet assignments. The architecture was developed for the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state and has been used in several CMS searches. On fast-simulation samples of Higgs boson pair production in the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state against QCD multijet production, CoReNet with 1508 trainable parameters performs well above kinematic baselines and trains in minutes on a single GPU. Its hypothesis weights select the truth-matched jet pairing in most of the signal events in which it is defined, although no assignment target is used in training. Since only the encoded decay chain is specific to the final state, the construction carries over to other topologies, which we test with $HH \to b\bar{b}W^+W^-$ against semileptonic $t\bar{t}$. There, encoding the decay chain of the background as well as that of the signal further improves the classification, at a cost of about $10^3$ parameters. In both final states its performance is comparable to that of a state-of-the-art transformer-based network more than two orders of magnitude larger. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/cms-cmu/CoReNet.

papers.title_en: Predictive Maintenance at the Edge: An Embedded Anomaly Detection Pipeline Trained with Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract_en: This article presents a predictive-maintenance pipeline that detects anomalies in bearings from vibration signals, adapted for deployment at the edge on low-cost microcontrollers, and that uses quantum optimization in two steps of its training. The pipeline consists of a step of vibration feature extraction and a step of classification with a one-class support vector machine (OCSVM). The features are selected by minimum redundancy and maximum relevance (mRMR) with the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), under a limit on computing time. The OCSVM is adapted for inference at the edge without floating-point operations and is trained by a variational quantum algorithm with Pauli-correlation encoding (PCE). In small-scale tests on a simulator, with the Paderborn bearing dataset, the VQE found the optimal selection in 36% of the runs with Adam, and PCE chose better support vectors than chance, until a classical local search made the two equal. A classical baseline, the usual OCSVM trained by SMO with its weights rounded, matched them without any search.

papers.title_en: Clifford synthesis is NP-complete
papers.abstract_en: We show that the problem of synthesizing a quantum circuit for a given Clifford operator using at most a specified amount of resources is NP-complete for several resource models of practical interest. Specifically, we study synthesis of a given Clifford operator using single-qubit Clifford gates and two-qubit Clifford gates, with full qubit connectivity and no additional ancilla qubits. With single-qubit gates free and CNOT as the only two-qubit gate, we show that deciding whether a given target admits an implementation using at most a specified number of CNOT gates is NP-complete, and we show that the problem remains NP-complete when any two-qubit Clifford gate is allowed and the budget counts all such gates. Moreover, we show that both results continue to hold when SWAP gates may be inserted for free, and when single-qubit gates are also considered part of the budget. In each case, we build on recent work by Li and Guan and show that there are polynomial-time reductions from Hamiltonian path in grid graphs to these decision problems, using a number of qubits quadratic in the number of grid vertices.

papers.title_en: Hypergraph cycle enumeration for efficient inference of planted k-XOR with smooth trade-off
papers.abstract_en: We introduce hypergraph cycle enumeration (HCE), a simple spectral framework for detecting and recovering planted signals in noisy hypergraph inference problems. We study HCE on one representative problem from this class, namely planted noisy k-XOR, also known as sparse Learning Parity with Noise (LPN). Both theoretically and empirically, HCE achieves comparable recovery behavior to Kikuchi method, matching Kikuchi hierarchy. We identify parameter regimes where HCE outperforms Kikuchi method, showing that neither algorithm is universally better. We also show a subquadratic quantum speedup for HCE by replacing one of the algorithm's steps with a quantum walk. Our classical and quantum algorithms do not refute the quartic quantum speedup of quantum Kikuchi method, which remains valid for the practically relevant regime of large size and high noise strength.

papers.title_en: Layered Wire-Grid Haloscope for Millielectronvolt Axions and Dark Photons
papers.abstract_en: We propose MADGRID (Millielectronvolt Axions and Dark photons with layered GRIDs), a few wire grids in front of a mirror, tuned by their spacing, forming an epsilon-near-zero slab that radiates through its face into external optics. Unlike wire-plasma haloscopes, the signal need not cross the lossy medium to reach an antenna, and metal grids replace the disks of dielectric haloscopes. A 1 m$^2$ array in 10 T could probe axion-photon couplings below the CAST bound up to 1.4 meV with kinetic-inductance detectors, and KSVZ couplings over 0.8-3.9 meV with future photon counters. Without a magnet, it could probe dark photon mixings down to $3.4\times10^{-16}$.

papers.title_en: Quantum manifestations of converse symmetry breaking
papers.abstract_en: Quantum synchronization holds promise in advancing quantum technologies such as sensing, communication, and computation. A key challenge in this rapidly developing field is to identify mechanisms that can promote the emergence of synchronous dynamics. Here, we show that quantum synchronization can be enhanced by introducing controlled heterogeneity in the form of coupling mismatches. Using spin van der Pol oscillators as a model system, we show that this mechanism constitutes a quantum analog of the phenomenon of converse symmetry breaking previously identified in classical oscillator networks, where a synchronous state is stabilized by explicit symmetry breaking. We quantify how quantum effects modify this behavior by tuning the degree of quantumness through variations of the spin quantum number. These findings suggest that quantum synchronization can be enhanced in experiments by harnessing rather than suppressing heterogeneity.

papers.title_en: Separating Fermion and Gauge Resonances with Species-Dependent Lightcones in Warped Geometry
papers.abstract_en: Extra-dimensional flavor models generally tie together the mass scales of gauge and fermion Kaluza--Klein modes. We show how species-dependent five-dimensional lightcones, which can be generated, for example, by a simple scalar profile, can separate these scales while preserving four-dimensional Lorentz invariance and any proposed extra-dimensional flavor structure. In two illustrative models on stabilized backgrounds, right-handed quark partners lie at 6.6--12 TeV with 30 TeV KK gluons, or a 5.5 TeV gluon lies below fermion partners above 10 TeV. We compare with deconstructed and three-brane models.

papers.title_en: Variational Programs with Open Clocks
papers.abstract_en: Variational quantum algorithms leave the durations of Hamiltonian evolutions open for a classical optimizer to set. We present VHamilton, a minimal extension of the Hamilton quantum programming language in which such durations are open clocks: one program denotes a family of Hamiltonian trajectories, and a valuation fills its clocks with exact dyadic times, so that each instance is an ordinary Hamilton program that compiles to circuits as before. Because the semantics stays exact and affine in the clocks, the Hamiltonian structure of a variational program remainsavail able for reasoning about every valuation at once. Equivalence becomes a finite calculation, which we mechanize in Agda for a fragment and use to prove the VHamilton form of the compiler rewrite "rzz(t) = cx; rz(t); cx" for every clock value. We then show what the same structure supports in a two-qubit chemistry eigensolver written in VHamilton and run through a Haskell prototype. It supports a fusion of commuting blocks, a closed form and an expressibility proof for the ansatz, and an exact split of the error between the precision of the target and that of the clocks, with a priori bounds. It also supports a coordinate search whose queries per sweep, fixed by the spectra of the generators, do not grow with the precision. On the benchmark this search reaches the numerically verified optimum of a grid of 134 million valuations in 53 energy queries. It finds the grid optimum in only 21 of 30 validation settings, however, so the gain is conditional, not a global-optimization guarantee.

papers.title_en: Vacuum amplification across a programmable bosonic Bogoliubov stability boundary in a trapped-ion chain
papers.abstract_en: A quantum oscillator always carries vacuum fluctuations, and modulating its parameters converts them into correlated pairs of real quanta. This vacuum amplification underlies squeezed light and Hawking radiation. In a closed quadratic system, pair creation competes with the energy splitting of the modes, and growth turns exponential only once pairing overcomes the splitting. Here we realize this competition in two motional modes of a trapped-ion chain. A two-mode-squeezing drive creates the pairs, and a beam-splitter coupling splits the motion into two coupled modes at different frequencies. The two rates are tuned and calibrated independently. Starting near the motional ground state, we cross the stability boundary in two ways. First, with the drive at the sum of the two bare-mode frequencies, the phonon number stays bounded until the pairing rate exceeds the splitting and grows exponentially beyond it. Second, tuning the drive into resonance with one coupled mode lowers the threshold to zero, and only that mode is amplified into a squeezed vacuum. Separate control of the two interactions makes the threshold for vacuum amplification programmable. This control can be used to simulate particle creation and quantum phase transitions, and to operate parametrically driven bosonic devices close to their stability limit.

papers.title_en: Liouvillian spectral snapshots: A reduced-subspace approach for time-dependent and noisy open quantum systems
papers.abstract_en: Driven-dissipative quantum devices are routinely operated with time-dependent drives and exposed to temporally correlated classical noise. When these perturbations vary on timescales comparable to the system's intrinsic dynamics, rotating-wave and Markovian approximations can fail, making effective static descriptions unreliable. As a result, accurately modeling systems in this regime often relies on simulating the full time-dependent master equation. This is particularly demanding for processes requiring long integration times, such as rare switching between metastable states, or for stochastic perturbations requiring averaging over many noise realizations. To address these challenges, we introduce Liouvillian spectral snapshots (LSS), a reduced-basis method that enables efficient simulation of such systems by projecting the master equation onto a low-dimensional subspace capturing their coarse-grained dynamics. LSS constructs this subspace by computing the slowly decaying, low-frequency eigenoperators of the Liouvillian at a few adaptively sampled perturbation values and compressing them into a common basis. This basis is built once and can be reused across noise realizations and perturbation parameters, reducing the cost of ensemble averages and parameter sweeps.

papers.title_en: Machine Learning Sensor Fusion for Water Vapor Radiometry based Tropospheric Delay Calibration
papers.abstract_en: The next-generation Very Large Array (ngVLA) intends to use 22 GHz water vapor radiometry (WVR) to correct for tropospheric phase fluctuations in its high-frequency bands. However, current delay-retrieval methods do not reach the required accuracy and reliability. As a remedy, we propose a machine-learning based retrieval concept and a preliminary architecture, framed as heterogeneous, multi-rate sensor fusion. Atmospheric reanalysis profiles and surface weather set the context in which per-antenna WVR spectra are used to estimate excess path by a Kalman filter whose parameters are learned from high-cadence calibrator phases. The method is being developed, with planned first validation on the 183 GHz WVR system of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

papers.title_en: Search for long-lived heavy neutral leptons in signatures with one prompt muon and a secondary vertex formed by two non-prompt muons in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 and 13.6 TeV
papers.abstract_en: A search for heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) in the decay of W bosons is performed in final states with three muons, with one originating promptly from the primary interaction vertex and the other two stemming from a common secondary vertex. The analyzed proton-proton collision data correspond to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$ recorded at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV in 2016$-$2018, and of 34.6 fb$^{-1}$ recorded at 13.6 TeV in 2022. The analysis strategy is optimized for large HNL decay lengths by requiring highly non-prompt muons forming a secondary vertex far from the beam line, and hence reconstructed only in the muon system of the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC. This enhances the analysis reach in the high HNL lifetime region, corresponding to low HNL masses (2$-$4 GeV) and small mixing parameters with the standard model neutrinos (10$^{-6}$$-$10$^{-5}$), where prompt and tracker-based non-prompt analyses have limited acceptance. No excess over the background prediction is found. Under the Majorana HNL hypothesis, exclusion limits at 95% confidence level are set on the HNL mixing parameter as functions of the HNL mass in the range of 1$-$5 GeV.
authors: De Favereau De Jeneret, Jerome Paul E.
Vieira De Castro Ferreira Da Silva, Pedro Manuel
Beirao Da Cruz E Silva, Cristovao
Calderon De La Barca Sanchez, Manuel

papers.title_en: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract_en: We present a numerical study of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for boost-invariant flows in 2+1 dimensions. The Density Frame is a formulation of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics that is first order in time, requires no auxiliary fields, and has no non-hydrodynamic modes; the only parameters are the shear and bulk viscosities and the equation of state. We formulate the numerical method in terms of a discrete analog of the dissipative function, which guarantees that the discrete equations produce entropy on all length scales and leads to a remarkably robust algorithm. We test the method against the exact solution of kinetic theory in the relaxation time approximation with Gubser symmetry. In making this comparison, we clarify how the kinetic solution matches onto hydrodynamics: we organize the solution by the opacity and show how the Bjorken attractor passes onto the Gubser solution order by order in gradients. We then replace the hydrodynamic engine of the MUSIC code with the Density Frame, and compare the two for IP-Glasma initial conditions in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$ TeV. The Density Frame smooths sharp gradients more rapidly. The largest differences arise in the bulk-viscous sector, where the bulk pressure in the Density Frame responds instantaneously to the flow, while in the Müller-Israel-Stewart-based MUSIC it relaxes over a finite time. With shear viscosity alone, the multiplicity, mean transverse momentum, and elliptic flow of final-state hadrons from the two codes are very similar. The Density Frame is now ready for a complete Bayesian analysis of heavy-ion data.

papers.title_en: Witnessing and quantifying stellar rank with the Wigner function
papers.abstract_en: Quantifying non-Gaussianity is essential for assessing the computational power of bosonic quantum systems. We introduce a framework to witness and quantify non-Gaussianity from displaced parity measurements, and we directly apply it to experimental data obtained with superconducting cavities. Our method estimates fidelities with target pure states from the displaced parity measurements, enabling certification of non-Gaussianity via the stellar rank. We further introduce refined witnesses computed by measuring the value of the Wigner function at a few points, providing efficient certification tools outperforming existing ones. Applying these techniques to Fock, binomial, cat, and GKP experimental data, we rigorously certify non-Gaussian resources and establish a stellar rank of $8$ for a GKP state, setting a new benchmark across all quantum platforms. Our methods enable a rigorous quantification of non-Gaussian quantum resources directly applicable to superconducting devices.

papers.title_en: Benchmarking One-Dimensional Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Methods on Quantum Hardware
papers.abstract_en: Classical computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods encounter significant computational bottlenecks in large systems and at high Reynolds number flows due to the rapid increase in degrees of freedom, even on flagship supercomputers. As quantum computers emerge, the Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Method (QLBM) has been proposed as a quantum-native alternative for solving fluid dynamics problems. However, until recently, nearly all studies have relied on classical quantum simulators rather than real quantum hardware. This study presents a benchmark of a one-dimensional QLBM implementation executed on three different IBM Quantum hardware. We design and test a quantum circuit for the advection-diffusion equation using amplitude encoding, a Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK)-type collision operator, and a streaming step with periodic boundary conditions. Our numerical experiments evaluate transpiled two-qubit gate count, total circuit depth, runtime, and accuracy metrics including maximum absolute error ($L_\infty$ norm) and root-mean-square error (RMSE). We find that the present collision and streaming operators dominate the overall cost and become the primary scalability bottleneck on current hardware. To mitigate the prohibitive cost of full quantum state tomography on hardware-based benchmarking exercises, we introduce a sampler-based measurement strategy that reconstructs macroscopic density fields directly from computational-basis measurements. This approach substantially reduces measurement overhead while preserving the expected advection-diffusion dynamics on hardware. These results provide a quantitative assessment of QLBM performance in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) regime and identify the principal algorithmic and experimental limitations that must be addressed for QLBM to become viable for fluid dynamics.

papers.title_en: Electronic-Structure-Informed Many-Body Encoding for Quantum Machine Learning
papers.abstract_en: Data encoding is a central challenge in quantum machine learning (QML), as it determines how classical information is mapped onto quantum states and influences the expressive power and efficiency of parameterized quantum circuits. Here, we introduce a physics-informed quantum encoding strategy that exploits the intrinsic many-body structure of electronic systems to establish a direct correspondence between the body order of input descriptors and the locality of quantum gates. Specifically, $n$-body electronic descriptors obtained from a single mean-field electronic-structure calculation are encoded through $n$-qubit gates, yielding a systematic hierarchy of quantum circuits with increasing many-body expressivity. Using reduced-density-matrix descriptors, we construct quantum machine-learning models incorporating one- through four-body encodings and benchmark their performance in predicting electron-correlation energies along bond-stretching potential energy surfaces. We demonstrate that increasing the body order of the encoding systematically improves prediction accuracy toward the full configuration interaction limit. Remarkably, disconnected many-particle densities constructed from lower-order electronic information achieve accuracy comparable to explicitly correlated two-particle densities in key cases, providing a computationally inexpensive route to higher-body quantum encodings. These findings establish a connection between the many-body structure of classical data and the design of quantum feature maps, offering a systematic, physically interpretable framework for enhancing the expressivity and predictive performance of quantum machine-learning circuits.

papers.title_en: Transverse momentum correlations and QED effects in TMD determinations
papers.abstract_en: Extractions of the non-perturbative, transverse momentum dependent (TMD) hadron's structure from experimental measurements of vector-boson spectra at hadron colliders are strongly influenced by correlations across boson's transverse momentum bins and by Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) effects, both from photon emission and from the photon-photon collision background. We present a Monte Carlo framework to take this into account, and illustrate the results with a comparison of theoretical predictions with the high-precision LHCb measurements of $Z$-boson production in the forward rapidity region. We discuss the relationship with the CMS data set at central rapidities.

papers.title_en: Phenomenological Chiral Effective Field Theory for Neutrino Event Generators
papers.abstract_en: Single-pion production is a crucial interaction channel for accelerator-based neutrino experiments, which rely on neutrino event generators for its cross sections. However, no model implemented in current generators provides a consistent and systematically improvable description of the resonance region. In this work, we develop a phenomenological chiral effective field theory model of pion production, built from nucleons, pions, and the $Δ(1232)$ with consistent, spin 3/2, gauge-invariant couplings, and we implement it in a fully automated pipeline from the Lagrangian to events using FeynRules, UFO 2.0, and Sherpa. We validate our results with pion photoproduction data and compare against neutrino bubble chamber, MINERvA, T2K, MicroBooNE, MiniBooNE, and electron-carbon scattering data. The framework can be systematically improved by extending the Lagrangian with higher-order operators and additional degrees of freedom, and by refitting couplings and form factors as new data become available. Combined with nuclear model interfaces, our approach opens a path to resonance-region predictions that meet the needs of next-generation experiments.

papers.title_en: Nuclear-geometry-tagging events in high-energy Ne--Ne collisions
papers.abstract_en: Nucleon-nucleon interactions within atomic nuclei give rise to collective properties such as deformation and nuclear clustering. Ultrarelativistic nucleon-nucleon collisions offer a novel way to probe the many-body correlations of the incoming nuclei, as the nuclear structure is reflected in the initial geometry of the produced system. State-of-the-art low-energy nuclear theory calculations predict highly deformed $^{20}$Ne nuclei with a characteristic $α$+$^{16}$O bowling-pin-like shape. Since such nuclei have recently been collided at the LHC, investigating methods to maximise the sensitivity to the nuclear structure is pertinent. In this paper, we investigate whether body--body and tip--tip configurations of $^{20}$Ne nuclei can be identified in Monte--Carlo Glauber simulations using geometry-sensitive observables: the eccentricity, $\varepsilon_2$, and the transverse compactness, $d_\perp$. The nuclear configurations are obtained from nuclear lattice effective field theory calculations within the framework of Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory (NLEFT) and $\textit{ab initio}$ Projected Generator Coordinate Method (PGCM). We utilise a Fisher linear discriminant to select body--body and tip--tip configurations based on the $\varepsilon_2$-$d_\perp$ correlation. With classifier thresholds chosen to retain $30\%$ of the target class in a validation sample, the two-variable Fisher selection obtains purities in NLEFT (PGCM) of $0.201$ ($0.156$) and $0.573$ ($0.540$) for body--body and tip--tip events, respectively.

papers.title_en: Deconfinement in weak electric and magnetic fields
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the thermal deconfinement transition in weak electric and magnetic fields, describing the hadronic phase by a pion gas and the quark--gluon plasma by the MIT bag model. Besides the thermal response of each phase, we include the one-loop electromagnetic vacuum terms of quarks and charged pions, renormalized at a common scale that fixes the charge in the confined vacuum. With no fitting of the electromagnetic response, the critical temperature rises with the electric field and falls with the magnetic one. The electric curvature is of the same size as that obtained on the lattice, while the magnetic one is a few times larger. We discuss the dependence on quark mass and renormalization scale, and a large-$N_c$ organization of both curvatures, whose sum is independent of the vacuum terms and connects directly to perturbative QCD.

papers.title_en: Construction and Commissioning of a Compact Xenon Gas Recycling System for a High-Harmonic Generation VUV Frequency Comb
papers.abstract_en: A compact, closed-loop xenon recycling system for application in a High-Harmonic Generation (HHG) Vacuum-UV (VUV) frequency comb laser systems is designed, constructed and commissioned. It consists of three main sections, a low-pressure section (LPS) pre-filtering the gas of particulates, water and hydrocarbons, then a compression station (CS), allowing for a variable pressure of up to 60 bar, and a high-pressure section (HPS) with more filtering, pressure control and monitoring. The system proves to meet all design criteria in gas quality (the sum off all hydrocarbon contaminations up to 120 amu and CO$_{2}$ being below 10$^{-8}$ mbar) and recovery efficiency (>99.8$\%$ for all expected operational cases, neglecting possible geometric gas catcher losses in the HHG laser itself). The operation and results are presented and discussed. Furthermore, the system is compared to the performance of a similar system from which it is derived.

papers.title_en: Characteristics of VHF and UHF band detection using Stark shifting in Rydberg-atom sensors
papers.abstract_en: We present a characterization of the sensitivity of broadband electric field measurements in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands using AC stark shifting of Rydberg states. The dependence of the sensitivity and dynamic range of the field measurements using nD5/2 states of cesium for principal quantum numbers n= 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 is presented, detailing the intricacies involved. The frequencies considered for the measurement range from 50 MHz to 900 MHz for which a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell is used to excite the Rydberg atoms with the RF fields. The corresponding sensitivities achieved are in the $(μV/m)/\sqrt{Hz}$ range. A general trend of better sensitivity for higher principal quantum numbers is observed. This work paves the way for a better understanding of the AC Stark dependent field measurements using Rydberg sensors.

papers.title_en: Incorporating deep neural networks into lepton-nucleus interaction modeling
papers.abstract_en: We present a scheme to incorporate precise inclusive cross-section predictions from a deep neural network trained on electron--carbon scattering data into a Monte Carlo event generator. The inclusive prediction is decomposed into independent exclusive interaction channels using the generator's theoretical models, and the resulting events are reweighted accordingly. We apply this scheme to investigate nuclear effects in inclusive and semi-exclusive electron-scattering measurements.

papers.title_en: The Yottascale at Tera-$Z$: Petascale SUSY?
papers.abstract_en: As experimental and theoretical advances are made, the paradigm of grand unification faces growing challenges. In light of what has been learned at the LHC, from Higgs mass measurement and direct searches for supersymmetry, we contrast the current theoretical predictions in a simplified supersymmetric grand unified theory against present and future experimental precision, focussing on threshold corrections and renormalisation group effects above the electroweak scale. More precisely, the theoretical precision is juxtaposed to the experimental one. Especially, the impact of a future Tera-$Z$ factory such as FCC-ee is examined, while also considering the expected future improvement of proton decay constraints. We find that the improvement on the measurement of the gauge couplings expected at Tera-$Z$ will yield sensitivity to higher loop orders in the evolution of the couplings up to the Yottascale, calling for further theoretical efforts. In a minimal $\rm{SU}(5)$ scenario with nearly degenerate SUSY spectrum, we study the impact of the proton decay constraint on the SUSY scale, comparing 2- and 3-loop analyses. While the 2-loop results point to a SUSY scale around 1 PeV, the 3-loop analysis seems to exclude the model entirely. This follows from the fact that at 1-loop in the GUT threshold corrections, the mass of the colour-triplet Higgs is completely determined by the IR parameters. This \textit{IR determination} is not accidental, but rooted in the group structure and breaking of the GUT theory.

papers.title_en: Optical Quantum Memory Processing for Quantum Hashing
papers.abstract_en: Sender authentication is an important requirement for secure quantum communication networks. We propose programmable photon-echo quantum memory processing of a multi-time-bin photonic qudit for implementing a quantum-hash-based verification protocol. In this approach, using QM, sender (Alice) generates a quantum hash state by transforming a single stored photonic wave packet into the programmable photonic qudit. Bob's memory coherently maps the received time-bin photonic qudit into a single output mode according to phase encoding. Our scheme relies on a time-resolved coherent detection method introduced here, in which the coherent responses from individual time-bins are sequentially accumulated within Bob's spin coherence prior to the final sender verification. The key advantage of this coherent detection for quantum hashing is shown, and its potential applications are also discussed. The performed analysis demonstrates that experimentally verified parameters of contemporary optical quantum memories enable a proof of principle realization of the proposed architecture. These results reveal an additional role for quantum memories, serving not only as synchronization and repeater resources for long-distance quantum communication, but also as active elements for quantum hashing in conventional quantum key distribution systems.

papers.title_en: The signature-changing soft-gluon term as a possible source of non-planar $ζ_2$ terms at small $x$ in the non-singlet quark-plus-antiquark splitting function
papers.abstract_en: A relation underlying resummations at small momentum fraction $x$ predicts the highest logarithms of quark-plus-antiquark flavor-difference splitting functions from lower orders. Complete three- and four-loop results violate it at third-highest logarithms by pi-squared terms suppressed for many colors, of unexplained origin and color structure. At four loops Moch and Vogt suggested a squared imaginary phase. We retain the signature-changing soft-gluon term also in positive signature in Kirschner and Lipatov's double-logarithmic equations for forward quark-antiquark scattering, without derivation, with their printed negative-signature sign and adjoint Born term. We show that the proposed equations reproduce both violations in full color for quark-plus-antiquark flavor differences at zero power of $x$, fixed coupling and first order in pi squared, for defining-representation quarks of special unitary groups with at least three colors. The proposed equations at third-highest logarithms use one wave per exchanged color and signature, the retained term at lowest-order strength as the positive-signature color-neutral channel's only new source of these violations, no such terms from gluons across the softest exchanged quark-antiquark pair at comparable or larger transverse momentum, and unchanged quark-pair normalization in the splitting function. This agreement gives three independent tests of one system with no continuous coefficient adjusted to the violations, although corresponding non-quartic quark-minus-antiquark terms are missed. In the proposed equations, the retained term weighted by this phase is a possible origin of both violations. The equations predict these full-color five-loop quark-plus-antiquark terms if the relation otherwise holds and no new source first acts at five loops. Confirmation would support the retained term as the origin of the violations through five loops.

papers.title_en: Pure annihilation decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ with improved perturbative QCD formalism
papers.abstract_en: We study the pure annihilation decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ for the first time in the standard model with $S$ and $T$ representing the states of the light scalar ($1^3\!P_0$) and tensor ($1^3\!P_2$) correspondingly. Utilizing the assignment $q\bar q$ for light scalars with two-scenarios classification, we calculate the branching ratios of $B_c^+ \to ST$ with the improved perturbative QCD (iPQCD) formalism at leading order in the strong coupling $α_s$. The large branching ratios around $10^{-6}$ within uncertainties in the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa-favored channels, such as $B_c^+ \to a_0(1450) a_2(1320)$, $B_c^+ \to a_0(980, 1450)^+ f_2(1270)$, $B_c^+ \to K_0^*(700, 1430) K_2^*(1430)$, and $B_c^+ \to f_0(500, 1370, 1500) a_2(1320)^+$, are obtained in the iPQCD formalism, which would be tested at the Large Hadron Collider-beauty detector in the (near) future. The relevant tests to these theoretical predictions of large branching ratios associated with typical relative ratios could provide important opportunities for understanding the QCD dynamics of the involved modes or light scalars, as well as for exploring the reliability of the iPQCD formalism. Moreover, the direct charge-parity violating asymmetries in the decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ are naturally zero, since only tree-diagram contributions are involved.

papers.title_en: Microscopic Theory of Spin-Orbit Interactions of Light
papers.abstract_en: Optical spin-orbit interactions (SOI), demonstrated experimentally in optical cavities, enable the polarization degrees of freedom of light to be described and controlled as an effective pseudospin, providing a foundation for spintronic-like control of light and the development of next-generation optical technologies. However, prior works describe this emergent effect using phenomenological models that fail to uncover its microscopic quantum origins, and as a result, a rigorous connection between material electronic structure and the optical SOI remains elusive. In this work, we address this fundamental challenge by developing a microscopic quantum theory starting from the non-relativistic quantum electrodynamical (QED) description of light-matter interactions. We show that this effect arises from virtual interactions between confined photons and material excitations. Crucially, our theoretical framework provides microscopic material-design principles for tuning the distinct components of optical SOI, which include the optical birefringence, photonic self-energies, TE-TM splitting, and optical Zeeman splitting, enabling precise engineering of effective magnetic fields, diabolical points, and pseudospin textures. We anticipate that the predictive capability of our microscopic theory will enable systematic screening and design of material systems for photonic spintronics and optical technologies.

papers.title_en: An Assessment of Water Vapor Radiometry Landscape in ngVLA Context
papers.abstract_en: The ngVLA intends to utilize Water Vapor Radiometry (WVR) as an approach to lower calibration overheads for tropospheric phase fluctuation correction in its high frequency bands (5 & 6; 30.5-116 GHz) to levels below those feasible with fast switched reference gain calibration. As a stepping stone to an eventual ngVLA WVR system, the JVLA/ngVLA teams pursued an effort to develop and install a set of MMIC based compact water vapor radiometers (CWVR) and carry out on-sky testing. Most recent tests found that the CWVRs installed on the VLA antennas under this effort were non-functional in tracking visibility phases. As part of the program to develop a WVR system for the ngVLA, this memo summarizes the current landscape of water vapor radiometry experience, the situation with the CWVRs, how they relate to the ngVLA WVR requirements, and the work needed to operationalize the CWVRs as useful test systems and to make broader progress. We currently lack statistically relevant WVR correction data to understand their expected performance for the ngVLA sites. We also discuss parallel additional approaches alternative and/or complementary to the CWVRs. A path involving tests to establish the functionality, stability, sensitivity, and switched power cal/data synchronism of the CWVR system in the lab and on antenna, followed by on-sky tests, and a parallel effort to assess the utility of autocorrelation outputs of the VLA K-band receivers for delay estimation is recommended. Potential paths going beyond traditional excess path estimation methods which may be necessary to meet ngVLA requirements and goals are touched upon.

papers.title_en: Colloquium: Quantum information processing with ensembles of identical particles
papers.abstract_en: Identical particles underpin most quantum technologies, but the role of indistinguishability in these processes extends far beyond the symmetrization of many-particle states. This Colloquium presents a unified operational perspective on how particle identity, indistinguishability, exchange statistics, and many-particle interference can instead be harnessed as resources for quantum information processing. We first clarify the notions of entanglement and indistinguishability for identical particles, emphasizing their dependence on the accessible measurements and information. We then review how spatial overlap, multiparticle interference, and path identity enable the generation, extraction, protection, and distillation of coherence and entanglement. Their applications to quantum metrology and imaging, state discrimination, teleportation, entanglement swapping, and quantum cloning are examined. Finally, we discuss the thermodynamic role of indistinguishability, from the Gibbs paradox to quantum thermal machines and statistics-driven engines. Across these settings, indistinguishability emerges as a controllable, task-dependent resource whose benefits are determined by state preparation, exchange statistics, interference, and measurement constraints.

papers.title_en: Ensemble equivalence and asymptotic equipartition property in information theory
papers.abstract_en: •Classical information theory corresponds to the canonical ensemble description of information sequences.•The asymptotic equipartition property parallels ensemble equivalence in statistical physics.•Ensemble equivalence guarantees the validity of classical information theory.•Microcanonical Boltzmann entropy sets a new limit of information compression. There is a consensus that information theory and statistical physics have a close relationship but the rigorous proofs are still missing. In this work, according to the statistical ensemble description of the information sequences that are generated by the i.i.d. single variable and multivariate information source, the relationship between the ensemble equivalence and asymptotic equipartition property is established. We find that classical information theory is a special case of the canonical ensemble description from statistical physics. They are both the maximum entropy approximation of the real signal generation. We also find the microcanonical ensemble description is closer to the real signal generation than the conjugate canonical ensemble, but the ensemble equivalence between the microcanonical and canonical ensemble in the thermodynamic limit guarantees the effectiveness of classical information theory, i.e., the asymptotic equipartition property in information theory is an analogue of ensemble equivalence from statistical physics.

papers.title_en: Periodic orbits and numerical-kludge gravitational-wave signatures of an <math altimg="si121.svg" display="inline" id="d1e648"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> Einstein–Skyrme black hole
papers.abstract_en: We investigate timelike geodesic dynamics, periodic zoom–whirl orbits, and associated numerical-kludge gravitational-wave proxies in the black-hole solution of <math altimg="si121.svg" display="inline" id="d1e877"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> Einstein–Skyrme theory. We examine how black hole phenomenological deformation parameters affect the horizon structure, effective potential, circular orbits, and bound periodic trajectories. Particular attention is paid to the marginally bound orbit and innermost stable circular orbit. Periodic orbits are characterized using the established rational taxonomy <math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e892"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>ω</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mi>w</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> and their closure is verified numerically through the accumulated azimuthal advance. Representative trajectories are then used to construct leading-order numerical-kludge waveform proxies using a quadrupole prescription. The resulting numerical-kludge waveforms exhibit qualitative variations in amplitude modulation, phase evolution, and temporal morphology associated with the orbital topology and phenomenological Skyrme parameters. Since the Einstein–Skyrme spacetime possesses an asymptotic solid-angle deficit, these waveforms are interpreted as qualitative quadrupole proxies rather than quantitative gravitational-wave predictions. The comparison with Schwarzschild spacetime illustrates the sensitivity of periodic orbital motion and approximate waveform morphology to the modified background geometry, without establishing observational distinguishability.

papers.title_en: The field-theoretical formalism for the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity
papers.abstract_en: The teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (TEGR) is formulated in a field-theoretical form, in which tetrad and matter perturbations propagate on an arbitrary background solution of TEGR. The perturbations may be finite rather than infinitesimal and are treated as dynamical fields described by a Lagrangian. Gauge transformations are defined, and the gauge invariance of the dynamical Lagrangian and field equations is established. Applying the Noether procedure, we construct conserved currents, superpotentials, and charges. An identically conserved current and the associated superpotential are also derived from the Noether identity for the auxiliary linear gravitational Lagrangian density. The field-theoretical conserved quantities turn out to be insensitive to total-divergence terms in the original Lagrangian, including the term containing the inertial spin connection. Their gauge behavior at the asymptotic boundary is analyzed, and falloff and parity conditions ensuring well-defined charges are formulated. As an application, we consider linear gravitational perturbations on a Ricci-flat background and derive the gravitational-wave equations and tetrad perturbations in the transverse-traceless gauge. The antisymmetric part of the tetrad perturbation is explicitly shown to be pure local-Lorentz gauge and therefore does not represent additional gravitational-wave polarizations, leaving only the two standard tensor modes. Using the resulting charge formulae, we calculate the Schwarzschild and Kerr masses and the Kerr angular momentum. The required asymptotic conditions are verified for both black hole solutions in Cartesian coordinates of a flat background. The physically acceptable charge values demonstrate the consistency of the formalism and indicate its potential for extension to generalized teleparallel theories.

papers.title_en: Taiji drag-free and attitude control system: Modeling and end-to-end simulation for the science mode
papers.abstract_en: In the Taiji project—a Chinese space-borne gravitational wave detector—the drag-free and attitude control system (DFACS) is the core technology responsible for maintaining the inertial motion of the test mass (TM). A thorough understanding of the spacecraft (SC) dynamic behavior under complex gravitational perturbations and multisource nongravitational disturbances is crucial for optimizing control system design, studying data processing pipelines, and verifying the detector performance. In this paper, we propose a unified simulation framework integrating the constellation orbital motion with a full-state closed-loop DFACS system and develop a 60-degrees-of-freedom (DoF) DFACS simulator. Furthermore, benefiting from the introduction of high-precision numerical methods, the simulator is extended to 31 significant digits, which supports high-fidelity numerical simulations of the intersatellite laser interferometry measurements from picometers to million kilometers. Three different experiments are implemented to assess the performance of DFACS by analyzing the single TM’s residual force noise, moving optical subassembly’s jitter, and the arm-length variation of TM-TM and SC-SC. Moreover, we quantitatively demonstrate the feasibility of decoupling DFACS design and orbit optimization. For the Taiji project, this study enables a more realistic on-orbit simulation of the detector and provides a representative system response under closed-loop control, supporting more accurate detector sensitivity analysis and facilitating refined optimization for scientific objectives.

papers.title_en: RAM-based coincidence window optimization for robust real-time muon reconstruction in the ATLAS Level-0 endcap muon trigger
papers.abstract_en: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN provides the world’s highest center-of-mass energy proton–proton collisions. The ATLAS detector, located at one of the collision points, aims to perform precision measurements of Standard Model processes and to search for phenomena beyond it by observing particles produced in these collisions. From 2030, the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) will begin operation, increasing the instantaneous luminosity by about a factor of three. In preparation for HL-LHC, we report on studies of firmware optimization for the first-level muon trigger in the HL-LHC ATLAS experiment. Real-time muon track detection is implemented around a “Coincidence Window”, which projects hit combinations across three detector stations into momentum space through a predefined mapping. This is realized with RAM resources of FPGAs, where the input addresses correspond to hit patterns and the output to the associated track parameters. In the endcap region, the reconstruction principle is based on the point-angle measurement, and the reconstructed tracks are expected to follow straight-line trajectories. Non-straight combinations are rejected with null outputs, thereby serving as a pattern finding mechanism. Optimization is performed, respecting different tasks for the three stations: while the first and third stations mainly determine the momentum, the second station serves as a confirmation layer. Relaxing the straight-line constraint in the second station within a controlled range improves efficiency in the presence of multiple scattering and maintains robust performance against detector misalignments. As a result, the plateau efficiency for transverse momentum improves from 93.7% to 94.5% in the nominal configuration, and from 85.9% to 93.5% under a misalignment model based on Run-1 alignment constants. This optimization achieves a significant performance gain without increasing FPGA resource usage or latency. Moreover, it contributes to overall resource reduction and design simplification of the trigger system.

papers.title_en: TeV halos around pulsars and prospects for next generation gamma ray observatories
papers.abstract_en: The detection of extended very-high-energy (VHE, E > 0.1 TeV) gamma-ray emission surrounding the middle-aged pulsars Geminga and PSR B0656+14 by the HAWC Observatory in 2017 provided the first clear observational evidence for an extended inverse Compton component produced by electron-positron pairs diffusing away from pulsars, a component whose existence under conditions of suppressed diffusion had been anticipated theoretically. Such sources are now commonly referred to as TeV halos. These structures, now comprising two well-established halos and several candidates detected by HAWC, LHAASO, H.E.S.S., and Tibet ASγ, are understood to arise predominantly from inverse Compton (IC) scattering of interstellar radiation fields by relativistic electron-positron pairs that have escaped from their parent pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe) and diffuse through the surrounding interstellar medium (ISM). A defining observational characteristic of TeV halos is the strongly suppressed diffusion coefficient inferred within them, typically two orders of magnitude below the Galactic average, whose physical origin remains a subject of active debate. While purely leptonic models have been remarkably successful in reproducing the broadband spectral energy distributions and radial surface brightness profiles of known halos, the possible contribution of a hadronic component has also been discussed, particularly in light of LHAASO detections of ultra-high-energy (UHE, E > 100 TeV) emission from pulsar-associated sources. We show that, for middle-aged halo pulsars, the available pulsar potential and the rapid escape of energetic protons make a significant hadronic contribution unlikely, whereas PeV proton acceleration remains plausible in young, energetic pulsar wind nebulae. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current observational landscape of TeV halos across the electromagnetic spectrum, from GeV energies probed by Fermi-LAT to the UHE domain accessed by LHAASO. We present the theoretical framework underpinning particle transport and emission in TeV halos, covering the standard two-zone diffusion model with isotropic and anisotropic diffusion scenarios, energy-dependent morphologies, and the role of self-generated turbulence. We critically examine the case for a lepto-hadronic interpretation, reviewing constraints from current gamma-ray and neutrino observations, including IceCube stacking analyses. We discuss the implications of TeV halos for the cosmic-ray positron excess measured by AMS-02 and DAMPE, the nature of particle escape from PWNe, and the transition from the nebular to the halo phase. Finally, we assess the transformative potential of next-generation observatories, the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO), the Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory (SWGO), and upcoming neutrino telescopes, for resolving open questions through improved angular resolution, extended energy coverage, and Southern Hemisphere access to the inner Galaxy.

papers.title_en: Background particle response of CMS GEM detectors with Run 3 data and simulation
papers.abstract_en: The upgrade of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) will boost the instantaneous luminosity to 5–7 × 10<sup loc="post">34</sup> cm<sup loc="post">−2</sup>s<sup loc="post">−1</sup>, increasing particle fluxes in the forward region of the CMS detector. High particle fluxes can damage electronics and induce spurious signals. This study focuses on the GE1/1 triple-GEM detector’s sensitivity to both neutral and charged background particles, performed using FLUKA and GEANT4 simulations. FLUKA provides a comprehensive description of the radiation field around the GE1/1 chambers across a broad energy spectrum. GEANT4 delivers complementary insight into the detector response based on realistic geometry, materials, and interaction processes. The results show how the detector’s sensitivity changes with particle energy and incident angle, and how different configurations affect its performance. The article also includes comparisons with CMS Run 3 data, providing valuable guidance for optimizing GEM operation under HL-LHC conditions. This approach can be extended to other forward detectors like ME0 during the HL-LHC era. •FLUKA simulations for radiation environment studies.•GEANT4 simulations for GE1/1 geometry and sensitivity analysis.•Hit-rate calculation and comparison with Run 3 data.

papers.title_en: Variational quantum circuit learning for bilinear control of nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics
papers.abstract_en: Variational quantum circuits have emerged as expressive learning architectures for hybrid quantum-classical optimization. In this work, we developed a dual-channel variational quantum framework for bilinear optimal control of the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation. A parameterized quantum circuit with time reuploading is used to generate two control fields, which modulate the displacement and confinement terms. We proved global well-posedness and existence of optimal controls in a weighted energy space, via an energy identity requiring no time differentiability of the controls. Also, we show that the realizable controls are trigonometric polynomials with frequencies drawn from a finite set. This frequency set grows linearly with the circuit depth. However, this family is not dense in the space of continuous functions because the readout imposes a uniform bound on the amplitude of the controls. Numerical experiments are demonstrated over twenty restarts, matched in parameter count, amplitude bounds, budget, and initial occupancy, to show that the quadratic channel raises the terminal fidelity from 0.833 to 0.999. Compared with equal-size Fourier, chopped-random-basis, and spline parameterizations, the circuit achieves comparable fidelity while using approximately half the control energy.

papers.title_en: Fast implementation of controlled $\pi $ phase gate using superadiabatic shortcuts with Rydberg superatoms
papers.abstract_en: Quantum phase gates serve as core fundamental resources for quantum information processing, and their preparation efficiency and structural stability directly determine the overall performance of quantum computing and quantum communication. The traditional adiabatic preparation method is prone to the influence of decoherence due to its excessive time consumption, while superadiabatic shortcut technology can significantly shorten the evolution time while retaining the advantages of the adiabatic process. In this paper, we propose a scheme for rapidly implementing a quantum phase gate by combining superadiabatic scheme and quantum Zeno dynamics to construct shortcuts to adiabatic passage. We demonstrate the superadiabatic shortcut by using Rydberg superatoms in a distant-atom-cavity system. Furthermore, we utilize the controlled $\pi $ phase gate to achieve the preparation of N-particle cluster state. In addition, the effects of decoherence and operational errors induced by various parameters are discussed. Numerical simulation demonstrates the proposed scheme has high fidelities and robustness against both cavity leakage and atomic spontaneous emission. Different from previous superadiabatic shortcut schemes, our protocol adopts second-order iterative counterdiabatic driving to avoid experimentally inaccessible direct couplings, where the counterdiabatic correction is realized merely by reshaping feasible Gaussian laser pulses. Furthermore, we analyze the scalability of cascaded controlled $\pi $ phase gate for generating N-particle cluster state under realistic decoherence sources.

papers.title_en: Injectivity of G-fusion frames for quantum state identification
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the injectivity problem for g-fusion frames of Hilbert-Schmidt operators and its relation to unique identification of quantum states from measurement statistics. A g-fusion frame combines a family of closed subspaces of a Hilbert space with operator-valued measurements acting into auxiliary Hilbert spaces. For the induced measurement operators $A_i = \Lambda _i P_{W_i}$, we define the measurement map on self-adjoint Schatten-class operators by $m_i(T) = {{\,\textrm{tr}\,}}(A_i T A_i^*)$. We prove equivalent characterizations of injectivity in the Hilbert-Schmidt and trace-class settings. The key step is an explicit Jordan decomposition of a self-adjoint operator into its positive and negative parts; no common eigenbasis assumption for two arbitrary positive operators is required. We then interpret the trace-class result on density operators and explain its relation to informationally complete quantum measurements. A finite-dimensional qubit example illustrates how a subspace-based g-fusion construction can generate an informationally complete measurement scheme. The contribution is an injectivity criterion for a structured class of operator-valued measurements; it is not a claim of universal computational superiority over arbitrary POVMs or full quantum tomography.

papers.title_en: Model-Agnostic Search for New Physics in the Presence of Imperfect Background by Smearing the Data
papers.abstract_en: In the search for new particles in high-energy physics, it is necessary to first define the signal region (SR) enriched in signal events, and then compare events in this region with the expected background distribution. While most existing search methods rely on prior domain knowledge of either the signal or the background, there has been less effort to relax both assumptions simultaneously, as methods that weaken one assumption typically rely on strong knowledge of the other. We propose Model-Agnostic Search with Smearing and Imperfect Background (MASSIB), a method that addresses this challenge by learning the density ratio of events relative to a misspecified background distribution using modern tools from machine learning, and defining the SR as the region with high density ratio. Recognizing that a naive application of this idea introduces significant bias in background estimation when interpolating from the control region to the SR, MASSIB mitigates this issue by introducing a "smeared" density ratio, which can be learned efficiently through data-level manipulation and used to define an SR that allows for accurate background estimation. By applying it to various types of simulated Large Hadron Collider (LHC) events with realistic background mismodeling, we demonstrate that MASSIB identifies a data-driven SR that achieves high signal concentration consistently across different types of signals while avoiding bias in background estimation. The method does this without making strong assumptions about either the signal or background distribution. We then show that this robustness extends to the validity and strong statistical power of the resulting hypothesis tests for signal detection, demonstrating the potential of this approach for future model-agnostic searches at the LHC.

papers.title_en: Connes spectral distance as a quantum distance measure and a geometric measure of entanglement
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we study the Connes spectral distance as a quantum distance measure and its applications in discriminating quantum states and calculating quantum entanglement. Based on finite matrix algebra, we construct a spectral triple for finite dimensional quantum states. The Connes spectral distance is a generalization to the quantum trace distance and Hilbert-Schmidt distance. The corresponding optimal elements can always be chosen to commute with the difference matrix $Δ$, and then the optimal element and $Δ$ can be simultaneously diagonalized. We obtain the formulas of Connes spectral distances in three different parameter regimes which depending on the spectrum of difference matrix. As applications, we show how to use spectral distances to distinguish state pairs that have the same trace distance and Hilbert-Schmidt distance. We also define a new geometric measure of entanglement based on spectral distance. These results can help us study the relationships among Connes spectral distance, quantum trace distance and other quantum distance measures. These concrete constructions are significant for studies of quantum states in the framework of noncommutative geometry.

papers.title_en: Single-Temperature Ranked Greedy Cluster Exchange for Max-Cut on Two-Dimensional Tori
papers.abstract_en: Ground-state search in two-dimensional Ising spin glasses on large toroidal lattices remains challenging for local-update heuristics because rugged energy barriers impede relaxation across metastable states. Equivalent to zero-field toroidal Max-Cut problems, these spin-glass instances also serve as standard benchmarks for optimization heuristics. Many Monte Carlo approaches combine single-spin flips or cluster moves with temperature ladders or annealing schedules, yet even with tuned parameters, rarely achieve rapid, reliable ground-state convergence at scale. Here, we address the need for faster ground-state search through cooperation between replicas. We introduce ranked greedy cluster exchange (RGCX) and combine it with fixed-temperature Metropolis sweeps to form single-temperature RGCX. Replicas are ranked by cut to determine the pair-processing order. Each pair deterministically exchanges every disagreement cluster that raises the better replica's cut, retaining the complement and conserving the pair's summed cut. On the 20,000-spin Gset instance G81, the estimated runtime to reach the certified optimum with 99% success probability (TTS99) was 12.1 s on an 8-core desktop computer. With the same population size, exchange interval and temperature, the method reached the best known cuts on all 17 toroidal Gset graphs, including 9 certified optima. These findings advance ground-state search on large two-dimensional tori by establishing single-temperature RGCX as an efficient population-based method that combines ranked greedy cluster exchange with fixed-temperature Metropolis dynamics.

papers.title_en: Search for $\mathrm{GeV}$-scale axion-like particles in PbPb collisions
papers.abstract_en: A search is performed for the production of axion-like particles with masses in the range 3-10 GeV using PbPb collision data recorded by the LHCb experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $0.228~\mathrm{nb}^{-1}$ and a nucleon-nucleon centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV. This is the first search for axion-like particles produced exclusively by two photons ($γγ\to a\toγγ$) in the forward direction. It extends sensitivity to previously unexplored regions of the parameter space, probing axion-like particle masses and couplings down to 3.0 GeV and $3.2\times10^{-4}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, respectively. This result provides the most stringent limits to date on the production of axion-like particles from exclusive photon-photon fusion processes with masses between 3 and 5 GeV.
authors: De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca, Ulisses

papers.title_en: Unitarity and Positivity Constraints on C- or P-odd Anomalous Quartic Couplings
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we provide a comprehensive study of partial-wave unitarity and positivity constraints in the dimension-eight genuine anomalous quartic gauge coupling (aQGC) sector of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We extend previous partial-wave unitarity analyses to include all C- or P-odd operators, thereby completing the coverage of the full basis of 34 operators. We also derive an analytical set of necessary forward-limit positivity bounds that include all CP-odd Wilson coefficients. We demonstrate that non-vanishing CP-odd Wilson coefficients require non-vanishing contributions from the CP-even sector to satisfy the derived positivity conditions. Combining the positivity conditions with partial-wave unitarity, we obtain stronger bounds on twenty-three of the thirty-four Wilson coefficients in this sector of the SMEFT.

papers.title_en: Global and crustal properties of neutron stars
papers.abstract_en: We investigate how the treatment of the neutron star crust affects both the global properties of the star and the properties of the crust itself. Three approaches are compared: a direct connection between a fixed crust and the core equation of state (EOS), a smooth crossover between them, and a unified EOS in which the crust is computed within a compressible liquid-drop model with the same nuclear empirical parameters of the relativistic mean-field model used for the core. For each approach, we consider four values of the symmetry energy slope, $44 \le L \le 92$ MeV. For a $1.4\,M_\odot$ star, some global properties are weakly to moderately affected: the radius and the moment of inertia agree within 1% among the three approaches. On the other hand, the tidal deformability obtained with the direct connection is up to 21% lower than the unified one for $L = 92$ MeV. A much larger contrast comes from the crustal properties. Relative to the unified EOS, the direct connection yields a crust that is 15--36% thinner, 6--12 times less massive, and that carries a fraction of the total moment of inertia 5--8 times smaller (0.3--1.1% instead of 2.8--6.2%). The differences between crust treatments are thus comparable to or larger than those arising from variations in $L$ for crustal properties, while they remain subleading for global ones.

papers.title_en: $α$-decay widths from two-potential approaches and WKB prefactors
papers.abstract_en: The accurate calculation of $α$-decay widths can be obtained with several equivalent descriptions of the Gurvitz-Kalbermann two-potential approach (TPA) or a semiclassical WKB description having both correct barrier penetrability and consistent inner-state normalization prefactor. This prefactor, which is related to the assault frequency, is implemented in several ways in the literature, producing systematically different results that can be mistaken for $α$ preformation effects. We benchmark single-particle $α$-decay widths across 161 even-even nuclei ($A_p=144$--$252$) using several TPA descriptions and WKB calculations with four common prefactors, employing a Woods-Saxon potential fixed by the quantization-constrained parameter method. The TPA formulas agree to within a few parts in $10^{-8}$, highlighting their robustness. Among semiclassical prefactors, only the widely used round-trip (RT) approximation closely reproduces the TPA widths to within a few percent. An Airy-function analysis reveals this $\cos^2\to 1/2$ averaged WKB prefactor is the correct leading-order semiclassical normalization of the exact quasibound state, clarifying the counterintuitive empirical observations associated with the WKB prefactors. Our benchmark identifies the WKB prefactor appropriate for $α$-decay tunneling analysis and provides a clean reference for isolating preformation and structure effects in future studies.

papers.title_en: OPALX: A performance-portable framework for particle accelerator simulations
papers.abstract_en: Accurate charged-particle beam simulations require self-consistent collective fields and realistic accelerator models, while their computational cost motivates efficient use of heterogeneous computing systems. We present OPALX, a performance-portable accelerator simulation framework that builds on the beam-dynamics capabilities of OPAL. Its modular architecture uses the Independent Parallel Particle Layer (IPPL) and Kokkos to support distributed-memory execution on multicore CPUs and GPUs from a common codebase. The framework combines relativistic particle tracking with prescribed accelerator fields, particle-in-cell space charge calculations, and spin tracking. We describe the physical and numerical models and their integration into the simulation workflow. The implementation is assessed using disorder-induced heating and frozen-spin test cases, together with comparisons of spin evolution with G4Beamline and beam transport with TraceWin. A three-dimensional space charge benchmark evaluates throughput on CPU and GPU systems, reaching approximately $10^9$ macroparticles per second on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU for this benchmark. These results provide initial verification of the implemented models and demonstrate CPU and GPU execution of self-consistent space charge calculations. OPALX provides a common foundation for extending accelerator models and numerical methods across heterogeneous computing platforms.

papers.title_en: Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of the symmetric Werner state
papers.abstract_en: This paper determines exactly the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of the normalized symmetric Werner state in every local dimension $d\ge2$\begin{equation*} \mathrm{EoP}_2(W_{+,d})=\log_2\frac{4d(d+1)}{d^2+3d+4}. \end{equation*} We establish additivity for tensor power and, more generally, additivity for finite products of symmetric Werner states with different local dimensions. A canonical purification and its products achieve these values globally, even when arbitrary joint purifications with unrestricted finite dimensional auxiliary systems are allowed. We further examine perturbations away from the symmetric endpoint, and prove the continuity of the optimal value at this endpoint; moreover, we show a sharp square root order of variation in the optimal purity, while the canonical purification remains asymptotically optimal in the achieved entropy as this weight goes to zero.

papers.title_en: Investigation of transfer coupling strength in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Hf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>178</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction
papers.abstract_en: Disentangling the effects of nucleon transfer via <math><mi>Q</mi></math> value and deformation on fusion has been a longstanding objective.
